title: Impact of dataset partitioning on the reliability of SERS–machine learning models for antimicrobial resistance classification
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) represents a major global health challenge and motivates the development of rapid analytical approaches for characterizing clinical bacterial isolates. Surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS), combined with machine learning (ML), has emerged as a promising approach for label-free spectral classification of bacterial isolates. However, the field lacks methodological consensus on how hierarchical spectral datasets should be structured, standardized, and partitioned for reliable model evaluation. This gap has led to widespread data leakage and inflated performance reports in SERS-AI studies. Here, we present a systematic benchmarking framework based on 15,000 SERS spectra acquired from 15 clinical Staphylococcus aureus isolates representing distinct resistance phenotypes (MRSA, ERSA, and SSA), evaluating twelve data-partitioning strategies across five machine learning models and three feature selection or dimensionality-reduction methods. Our results show that spectrum-level splits consistently overestimate classification accuracy due to non-independent samples, whereas isolate- or subject-level partitioning provides more realistic estimates of model generalizability. Among the evaluated models, random forest combined with Boruta feature selection produced consistently robust and interpretable performance. Overall, model performance depended more strongly on dataset organization and partitioning strategy than on the choice of machine learning algorithm.

title: Complementarity validation of strain identification based on LIBS spectra and gram-stained microscopic images
abstract: Background LIBS provides chemical fingerprints of strains, while Gram-stained microscopic images offer morphological traits including staining reaction, cell morphology, and spatial arrangement. These two modalities have distinct physical origins and potential complementarity, yet their combined value in complex multi-category strain identification remains to be verified. Results Using 33 strains under a unified preparation workflow, we built single-modal classification models and three decision-level fusions (fixed-weighted probability, adaptive confidence, and Stacking meta-learning). LIBS single-modal (PCA-SVM on graphite) achieved Accuracy and Macro-F1 of 0.9694, with residual errors mainly on a few chemically similar strain pairs. Microscopic image single-modal (DN201) reached 0.9879, but still confused some morphologically similar pairs. Among fusions, adaptive confidence fusion (Fusion B) achieved the highest Accuracy and Macro-F1 values, both at 0.9991. The highest bidirectional mutual misclassification rate was 5.00% for LIBS, 6.00% for images, and dropped to 0.50% after Fusion B. Significance These results indicate that, in the measurement-level evaluation under the current controlled cultivation and preparation conditions, LIBS chemical information and microscopic-image morphological information exhibit a certain degree of complementary discrimination. Their combination can improve classification performance on the current dataset and reduce some residual misclassifications of the single modalities, providing preliminary experimental evidence for subsequent research on multimodal microbial identification methods.

title: Dual-channel CNN fusion of raw and preprocessed serum Raman spectra for robust echinococcosis screening
abstract: Background Serum Raman spectroscopy provides label-free molecular fingerprints for bioanalytical screening, but conventional models often rely on a single preprocessing pipeline. Because preprocessing can alter spectral distributions and attenuate information retained in raw spectra, this study developed a dual-channel fusion strategy for echinococcosis screening. Results We analyzed 573 serum samples from hepatic echinococcosis (HE), liver cirrhosis (LC), hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), and normal controls (NC); 458 formed the development set and 115 were reserved for held-out testing. We developed a dual-channel convolutional neural network (DCNN) that fused complementary features from raw and preprocessed Raman spectra. Eight preprocessing pipelines and three fusion strategies were evaluated using identical stratified five-fold splits within the development set, and the configuration with the highest mean five-fold accuracy was fixed before held-out testing. The selected fusion strategy was then assessed across all eight pipelines against single-channel models. Under the locked configuration, the DCNN achieved 94.98% ± 1.62% mean accuracy, compared with 89.95% ± 4.36% for the preprocessed-spectrum CNN (P-CNN) and 88.42% ± 2.66% for the raw-spectrum CNN (R-CNN). Held-out accuracies were 95.65% for DCNN, 91.30% for P-CNN, and 89.57% for R-CNN. For binary screening, a DCNN trained on the development set achieved 96.52% accuracy on the held-out set, whereas the dot immunogold filtration assay (DIGFA) yielded 88.70% on the same samples. Significance Feature-level fusion improved the use of complementary spectral information and reduced dependence on a single preprocessing pipeline. This strategy provides a robust framework for rapid, label-free serum Raman screening of echinococcosis.

title: Uncovering allergen presence and accumulation in glucose monitoring systems: evidence of a “sponge effect” via validated GC–MS
abstract: BACKGROUND: Despite the clinical benefits associated with the use of continuous and flash glucose monitoring systems (GMS), they are frequently associated with dermatological adverse effects, most notably allergic contact dermatitis (ACD). Chemical analysis of devices is often the only means to confirm the presence of suspected sensitizers or detect emerging allergens in these products. Although previous research efforts lead to the identification of some main allergens such as acrylates and colophony compounds, new allergens continue to emerge and the presence of known allergens in devices cannot be excluded. However, no validated quantitative analytical methods for these compounds in GMS have been reported. RESULTS: A quantitative gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) method was developed and validated, with a focus on optimizing the extraction from the devices. An untargeted screening workflow was incorporated to detect additional potentially relevant allergens. Targeted analysis enabled quantification (14 compounds) or estimated abundance analysis determination (5 compounds) of relevant allergens. The method was applied to unused and used Dexcom G7 and associated adhesive patches. Different allergens were detected and quantified including isobornyl acrylate, methyl dehydroabietate, and isocyanates. Other compounds were only detected in used devices, such as cetyl alcohol, isopropyl palmitate and isopropyl myristate. SIGNIFICANCE: The analysis revealed the presence of known and new allergens in medical devices for diabetes. Several allergens were present in unused devices, but others were detected only in used devices. These additional compounds likely accumulated from daily usage, leading to what we defined as the "sponge effect".

title: Breaking the channel barrier: same-fluorescence, different-Tm probe strategy enables seven-target respiratory virus detection on a six-channel PCR platform within 20 minutes
abstract: Background Respiratory pathogens with overlapping symptoms-including SARS-CoV-2, influenza A/B, H5/H7/H10 avian influenza, and RSV-co-circulate and co-infect, demanding rapid multiplex screening at points of care. Conventional multiplex real-time PCR is constrained by hardware channel capacity (≤6), making it difficult to detect seven targets while distinguishing influenza A and B in a single tube. This work addresses the contradiction between high-order multiplexing and limited fluorescence channels without sacrificing speed or sensitivity. Results We developed a six-channel ultra-fast PCR platform detecting seven respiratory viruses in a single tube within 20 min, using a same-fluorescence, different-Tm probe strategy. Influenza A and B share the FAM channel yet generate distinct melting peaks (∼12 °C difference, 84.8 °C vs. 72.3 °C), enabling accurate typing via melting curve analysis. Primers, probes, and enzymes are pre-embedded as lyophilized beads in sealed cartridges for fully automated sample-to-result operation. The assay achieved 100% detection at 5 copies/test for all targets, linearity (R 2 > 0.95) across 5-10 5 copies/test, 90-110% efficiencies, and no cross-reactivity against 39 non-target pathogens. Cartridges remained stable for 12 months at 25 °C. Validation on 271 clinical specimens showed 100% agreement with sequencing-verified single-plex qPCR. Significance and novelty This work provides the first integration of melting-curve-based same-channel multiplexing with lyophilized cartridge technology on an ultra-fast PCR platform. By overcoming channel limitations while maintaining speed and sensitivity, the system offers a practical, field-deployable screening tool for decentralized respiratory pathogen detection in resource-limited settings.

title: Quantitative TLC-based assay for the detection of urease inhibitors in complex mixtures
abstract: Background Urease inhibitors are increasingly relevant in agricultural and food chemistry because urease activity influences nitrogen-use efficiency, ammonia emissions, microbial survival, and food quality. Although numerous solution-based assays are available, no quantitative thin-layer chromatography (TLC)-based bioautographic method has been reported for detecting and localizing urease inhibitors directly within complex mixtures. This study aimed to develop and validate a quantitative TLC bioautographic assay suitable for effect-directed analysis of food-related matrices. Results The assay combines chromatographic separation, urease immobilization in an agar layer, and ammonia detection through the Berthelot reaction to quantitatively visualize urease inhibition zones while avoiding false-positive responses associated with pH indicator-based detection. Validation showed linearity for thiourea over 0.47-15 μg/spot (R 2 > 0.999), with LOD and LOQ values of 0.15 ± 0.08 and 0.46 ± 0.25 μg/spot, respectively, and intra-plate and intraday RSDs of 7.6-11.8% and 9.9%, respectively. Parallel screening of essential oils enabled rapid comparative evaluation of urease-inhibitory activity, while direct gas chromatography-mass spectrometry analysis of active chromatographic zones allowed microscale identification of eugenol as the principal bioactive constituent without preparative isolation. Significance This work presents the first quantitative TLC-based bioautographic assay for urease inhibitors and establishes an integrated effect-directed analytical workflow that combines quantitative activity localization with direct molecular identification. The methodology provides a simple and cost-effective platform for screening and characterizing urease inhibitors in complex food- and agriculture-related matrices, facilitating the discovery of bioactive compounds with potential applications in food preservation, quality control, and sustainable agricultural practices.

title: Aptamer/magnetic-MIP dual-recognition sandwich biosensor for rapid and recyclable determination of kanamycin in food
abstract: Background The rapid and precise monitoring of antibiotic residues is a cornerstone of food safety and diagnostic science. Herein, we report a high-performance dual-recognition sandwich-type fluorescent biosensor engineered by integrating Fe 3 O 4 @UiO-66-based molecularly imprinted polymers (FUMIP) with a fluorescein-labeled aptamer probe (Apt-FAM) for the ultrasensitive detection of kanamycin (KANA). Results Central to this design is the confined microenvironment provided by the FUMIP framework, which facilitates the selective pre-concentration of KANA through coordinated boronate affinity and hydrogen bonding. This interfacial enrichment significantly facilitates subsequent recognition by the Apt-FAM probe, forming a stable sandwich architecture that achieves a 156-fold sensitivity enhancement compared with the single-recognition control system constructed in this work. The FUMIP component exhibits a superior imprinting factor of 5.19 and an adsorption capacity of 45.11 mg/g, ensuring high-fidelity target capture even in complex matrices. The optimized biosensor enables rapid quantification within 30 min, delivering an exceptional detection limit of 0.0032 ng/mL across a broad linear range (0.01-1000 ng/mL). In comparison, the single-recognition sensor exhibits a linear range of 1-500 ng/mL with a detection limit of 0.5010 ng/mL. Furthermore, the sensor demonstrates robust reusability (70% signal retention after 20 cycles) and high practical reliability, with recoveries of 98.0%-106.2% in real food samples. Significance This work not only provides an advanced platform for KANA monitoring but also offers a universal strategy for the ultrasensitive detection of small-molecule contaminants by exploiting the synergy between synthetic and biological receptors.

title: Multiphase phosgene detection on machine learning-enhanced fluorescent sensor arrays
abstract: Phosgene is a highly toxic, volatile asphyxiant and a notorious chemical warfare agent, posing severe threats to public safety, environmental security, and industrial operations. The capability for rapid, selective, and ultrasensitive on-site detection of phosgene is therefore critically important. Nevertheless, the coexistence of phosgene in liquid, gaseous, and solid-phase environments imposes substantially different sensing requirements, making universal detection across multiple phases a longstanding challenge. Herein, we report the rational design and synthesis of three donor-acceptor (D-A) fluorescent probes and the construction of a conjugated donor-regulated fluorescent sensor array for comprehensive phosgene sensing. The developed platform enables highly sensitive detection and selective of phosgene across liquid, gas, and solid phases, demonstrating excellent adaptability under diverse detection conditions. The detection limit of BTTANT in the liquid phase was 0.48 μM, in the gas phase 0.88 ppm, and the fluorescence quenching rate in the solid phase was 88.28%. By integrating RGB colorimetric analysis with a smartphone, we achieved portable on-site quantification. Leveraging machine learning to enhance recognition strategies, we performed in-depth analysis of multidimensional response signals to distinguish phosgene from various structurally similar interferents with high precision. This study established an integrated fluorescence sensing-intelligent recognition detection platform, providing a significant impetus for the rapid, accurate, and in-situ monitoring of phosgene in complex environments.

title: Highly efficient RPA product degradation and expanded PAM recognition enable RPA-Cas3 detection of Clonorchis sinensis
abstract: Clonorchis sinensis is a major foodborne pathogen threatening aquatic food safety. Microscopy, the diagnostic standard, is laborious and often lacks sensitivity for low-intensity infections. Molecular strategies coupling isothermal amplification with CRISPR/Cas systems have attracted interest, but their reliability is often undermined by competition between amplification and detection and intrinsic limitations of Cas effectors, notably PAM dependence of Cas12a and nonspecific activation of Cas13a. To address these limitations, we used the type I-A CRISPR-Cas3 system (TsiCas3) from T. siculi. Because TsiCas3 displays trans-cleavage activity at 65 °C, a temperature that completely abolishes RPA polymerase activity, this temperature gap can be exploited to avoid interference. A one-tube, closed-reaction workflow was established where target DNA is first amplified by RPA at 37 °C for 20 min, then the temperature is raised to 65 °C. This shift simultaneously inactivates RPA polymerase and activates TsiCas3-Cascade, enabling specific amplicon recognition, trans-ssDNA cleavage, and fluorescence generation. The sequential temperature control physically separates amplification from detection, eliminates mutual interference, and requires no tube opening or reagent addition. Moreover, Cas3 efficiently and near-completely degrades the RPA amplicons, substantially reducing aerosol carryover risk. This closed-tube, contamination-resistant method provides a rapid, sensitive, field-deployable tool for C. sinensis detection and represents a practical addition to clonorchiasis control.

title: One-drop electrosynthesis of 3D Prussian blue analog@PEDOT on flexible porous graphene for portable NFC-enabled hydrogen peroxide determination in human semen
abstract: Hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) is a relatively stable reactive oxygen species and an important biomarker of oxidative stress in human semen. Elevated H 2 O 2 levels have been associated with impaired sperm function and male infertility. Therefore, the accurate determination of total H 2 O 2 levels in semen is valuable for assessing semen oxidative status. In this work, a cost-effective and sensitive electrochemical sensing platform was developed for the determination of total H 2 O 2 in human semen. A lab-made flexible porous graphene electrode was modified with a three-dimensional poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) film embedded with Prussian blue analog (3D PBA@PEDOT/F-PGE). The 3D PBA@PEDOT/F-PGE transducer was fabricated via a one-step electrodeposition process, providing high electrical conductivity, low charge-transfer resistance, excellent structural integrity, and stable electrocatalytic activity toward H 2 O 2 reduction. The transducer exhibited a linear detection range from 0.50 μM to 6.0 mM, a sensitivity of 390 μA mM -1 cm -2 , and a detection limit of 0.18 μM. The transducer was further integrated with a paper-based microfluidic device and a battery-free near-field communication (NFC) potentiostat to construct a portable electrochemical sensing platform capable of determining H 2 O 2 over a concentration range of 1.0 μM to 4.0 mM with good precision and long-term stability. The smartphone-controlled sensing platform was successfully applied to the determination of total H 2 O 2 levels in human semen samples, providing a convenient approach for assessing semen oxidative status. This platform shows considerable potential for point-of-care monitoring of oxidative stress associated with male reproductive health and for future applications in portable electrochemical sensing technologies.

title: Probing reactive oxygen species formation in electrospray ionization microdroplets
abstract: Background Electrospray ionization (ESI) is conventionally regarded as an ionization process governed primarily by charged-residue and ion-evaporation mechanisms. However, increasing evidence suggests that ESI microdroplets may also provide a chemically active environment capable of promoting redox reactions and generating reactive oxygen species (ROS). The origin of such reactivity remains controversial because electrochemical reactions at metal emitters, strong interfacial electric fields, and electrical discharge may all contribute to the observed chemistry. Therefore, this study systematically investigates whether ROS-related oxidation occurs during ESI and how operating parameters influence this process. Results 3,3',5,5'-Tetramethylbenzidine (TMB), 5,5-dimethyl-1-pyrroline N-oxide (DMPO), and ascorbic acid (AA) were employed as complementary probes of oxidation and radical-related chemistry. Without added catalysts during ESI-MS analysis, TMB oxidation generated a peak at m/z 240, assigned to its radical-cation intermediate, and this signal was strongly suppressed by AA, demonstrating its redox-sensitive nature. The empirical intensity ratio I 240 /I 241 increased as the orifice voltage changed from -1500 to -4500 V but decreased at higher voltage magnitudes, accompanied by an increase in ion current from ∼5 nA at -4500 V to ∼740 nA at -6000 V, suggesting possible corona-discharge involvement. Lower sample flow rates enhanced I 240 /I 241 , while oxidation of the spin-trapping reagent DMPO provided additional evidence for ROS formation. TMB oxidation persisted with an insulating capillary without direct electrical contact, excluding metal-emitter electrochemistry as the primary origin of the observed oxidation. Significance and novelty These results provide systematic evidence that ESI can function as a chemically active microenvironment, in which ROS-related oxidation occurs and is strongly dependent on operating conditions.

title: Ternary In2O3/ZnIn2S4/CdS heterojunction-based APE1-assisted “AND” logic gate photoelectrochemical biosensor for dual-miRNA detection
abstract: Photoelectrochemical biosensing has become a powerful technique for disease monitoring and therapeutic tracking. Most existing photoelectrochemical platforms are only capable of detecting a single biomarker, which limits their effectiveness in comprehensive disease management. To address this challenge, we developed a novel biosensor that integrates DNA-based logic gates with an In 2 O 3 /ZnIn 2 S 4 /CdS photoelectrode for dual-miRNA detection. The rationally designed ternary heterojunction exhibited significantly enhanced photoelectric conversion performance compared with binary composites, providing a high-quality photoelectric sensing platform. Based on it, a photoelectrochemical biosensor with DNA logic gates and a cascade reaction was designed, in which APE1 enabled target recovery and DNA walker movement. MiRNA-144 and Let-7a are recognized as promising diagnostic biomarkers for type 2 diabetes mellitus, early clinical application is hindered for their low-abundance. Upon miRNA introduction, APE1 cleaved hairpins to release strands, leading to GOD immobilization on the electrode. The subsequent reaction with glucose enhanced the photocurrent, enabling quantitative miRNA detection. Benefiting from the APE1-assisted cascade signal amplification strategy, the optimized biosensor displays a good linear correlation between photocurrent response and the logarithmic concentration of dual miRNAs within the range of 0.001 nM-10 nM, with a low detection limit of 0.43 pM (S/N = 3). Moreover, the carefully designed DNA tracks enable a well-ordered sensing interface, offering broad possibilities for clinical diagnosis and disease monitoring.

title: Multifunctional SnO2/SnS2/CdSe heterojunction coupled with CuO nanoenzyme-regulating synergistic strategy enable multimodal biosensing for breast cancer genes
abstract: Multimodal detection significantly enhanced detection accuracy in complex biological matrices. In this work, a high-efficiency multimodal biosensor is proposed based on multifunctional SnO 2 /SnS 2 /CdSe QDs heterojunction and CuO nanoenzyme-regulating synergistic strategy, which achieves ultra-sensitive and specific detection of breast cancer-related BRCA1 gene. A high-performance photoelectrochemical (PEC) SnO 2 /SnS 2 /CdSe QDs heterojunction was constructed for the first time, which effectively enhances the light absorption capability and photogenerated charge separation efficiency. The heterojunction yields a PEC signal approximately 3.75-fold higher than that of pure SnO 2 /SnS 2 and 11.3-fold higher than that of CdSe QDs, realizing stable PEC and electrochemiluminescence (ECL) dual signals. Notably, CuO nanoenzyme with intrinsic oxidase-like activity are introduced onto the sensing interface through target-induced amplification strategies, serving as multifunctional signal regulatory units. The CuO nanoenzyme can not only catalyze the oxidation of ascorbic acid but also trigger the ECL resonance energy transfer effect. This dual functionality enables the simultaneous "shutdown" of PEC and ECL signals and "activation" of fluorescence signals, constructing a self-verifiable triple-modal sensing platform for BRCA1 detection. The developed biosensor has been successfully applied to the quantitative detection of BRCA1 in human serum samples. This report offered a promising and versatile platform for early clinical diagnosis of breast cancer and detection of other important disease biomarkers.

title: Highly sensitive detection of exosomal miR-122 with CRISPR-Dx for precise HCC diagnosis
abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), one of the most common malignancies worldwide, poses a major threat to the global health. Its prognosis depends heavily on early detection. Currently, alpha-fetoprotein (AFP) is the widely used biomarker for HCC diagnosis. Nevertheless, approximately 40% of the HCC cases do not produce AFP. It has been reported that the downregulation of miR-122 is strongly associated with the development and progression of HCC. Here, employing miR-122 as a biomarker, we developed a cascade amplification-based CRISPR-Dx platform for HCC diagnosis. Owing to the strong trans-cleavage activities of Cas13a and Cas12a, the proposed assay enabled sensitive miR-122 detection down to 1 aM. Clinical sample analysis (n = 48) demonstrated a sensitivity of 91.3%, a specificity of 84.0%, and an overall accuracy of 87.5%, which is significantly better than that of the conventional AFP-based diagnosis (sensitivity, 43.5%; specificity, 80%; accuracy, 62.5%). In addition, because CRISPR-Dx eliminates the RNA extraction and reverse transcription steps that may cause target loss, it also showed better performance than miR-122-targeted qPCR. Given its high diagnostic accuracy and simplified workflow, the proposed miR-122-based CRISPR-Dx assay holds great promise for the clinical diagnosis of HCC.

title: CuO-ZnO heterojunction-engineered V-gCN nanosheets coupled with multi-footed DNAzyme walker for highly catalytic, ultrasensitive and label-free electrochemical aptamer ertapenem assay
abstract: Ertapenem (ER), a clinically important carbapenem antibiotic, is increasingly recognized as a residue contaminant that may accelerate the dissemination of antimicrobial resistance through environmental and food-chain exposure. Here, we report a label-free electrochemical aptasensor for ultrasensitive ER detection by coupling a heterojunction-engineered catalytic interface with multivalent DNA nanomachine amplification. The sensing interface was constructed from gold nanoparticle (AuNP)-decorated CuO-ZnO heterojunctions grown on vanadium-doped graphitic carbon nitride (V-gCN) nanosheets. In this architecture, V-gCN provides a conductive and high-surface-area scaffold, CuO-ZnO heterojunctions promote interfacial charge transfer and electrocatalytic activity, and AuNPs facilitate probe immobilization and biocompatible signal transduction. Target recognition by the ER aptamer releases an initiator strand that triggers catalytic hairpin assembly (CHA) circuit, generating abundant multi-footed DNAzyme walkers. In the presence of Mg 2+ , the walkers cleave electrode-confined hairpin substrates and liberate G-quadruplex strands that subsequently complex with hemin to form electroactive G-quadruplex/hemin. The resulting H 2 O 2 -mediated catalytic reduction of hemin is further amplified by the AuNPs/CuO-ZnO/V-gCN interface. Under optimized conditions, the aptasensor achieved linear range of 0.1 to 100 ng mL -1 with 58.99 pg mL -1 detection limit. The sensor also showed high selectivity against interferents of penicillin (PEN), meropenem (MR), imipenem (IMI), and biapenem (BIA) and satisfactory performance in spiked milk samples with recovery rate from 97.3% to 108.4%, demonstrating its potential for the establishment of various robust aptamer-based electrochemical biosensor for sensitive antibiotic-residue analysis.

title: Machine learning-assisted fluorescent sensor array based on siloxane-derived porous polymers for high-throughput discrimination of multiple antibiotics in milk
abstract: Both simultaneous monitoring of multiple antibiotic residues for public health security and accurate single-analyte quantification for regulatory compliance are critically important, though the former remains challenging due to structural diversity among analytes. Herein, we constructed a four-channel fluorescent sensor array based on siloxane-derived porous polymers for discriminative detection of 12 antibiotics spanning four categories (chloramphenicols, nitrofurans, nitroimidazoles, and tetracyclines), and further achieved discrimination of 6 antibiotics in real milk samples at lower concentrations (0.5 μM), along with quantitative determination of oxytetracycline (OTC) in two brands of milk. The array primarily generates differential fluorescence responses through synergistic inner filter effects and photoinduced electron transfer, featuring rapid response ( 90% fluorescence retention for tetracycline (TC) after 5 consecutive cycles). Integrated with machine learning algorithms (e.g., LDA and KNN), the sensor achieved 100% identification accuracy in spiked milk samples, demonstrating its potential as a robust platform for high-throughput antibiotic screening in complex matrices.

title: Primer-programmed circular template generation enables padlock-free rolling circle amplification for low-background CRISPR-based pathogen detection
abstract: Rolling circle amplification (RCA) is a powerful nucleic acid amplification strategy, yet conventional RCA-based biosensing often relies on target-specific padlock probes for circular template construction, which increases probe-design complexity and may introduce nonspecific ligation and background amplification. Here, we develop a padlock-free RCA strategy for CRISPR-based pathogen detection through primer-programmed circular template generation (PPCTG) strategy. Asymmetric recombinase polymerase amplification (RPA) with rationally designed phosphorylated primers generates target-derived single-stranded DNA (ssDNA), which subsequently undergoes universal splint-mediated circularization to form amplification templates without target-specific padlock probes. By integrating target recognition into the amplification-derived ssDNA intermediate, PPCTG couples target amplification with circular template generation while simplifying probe design and reducing nonspecific background. The resulting circular templates support continuous RCA, generating long ssDNA scaffolds that provide abundant activator sites for CRISPR-Cas12a, thereby enabling cascaded signal amplification through trans-cleavage of fluorophore-quencher reporters. The platform achieved a limit of detection of 3.47 aM for Staphylococcus aureus with high analytical specificity. Moreover, extraction-free detection was demonstrated in crude sputum and exhaled breath condensate, with recovery rates of 96.4%-105.5% and good agreement with qPCR results. Overall, PPCTG provides a padlock-free strategy for programmable circular template generation and integrates target amplification, RCA, and CRISPR-Cas12a signal amplification into a streamlined workflow, offering a low-background and ultrasensitive approach for pathogen detection in complex biological matrices.

title: SpectralTAG: Functional group identification from infrared spectra via unified LLM and GNN textual graphs
abstract: Background Spectral analysis underpins much of modern chemical characterization, yet extracting chemically meaningful interpretations from spectral signals remains constrained by the disconnect between data-driven pattern recognition and structured domain knowledge. Results Here we present SpectralTAG, a unified graph-based reasoning framework that bridges this gap by representing infrared spectra, hierarchical chemical knowledge graphs, and scientific text within a common textual attribute graph (TAG). In this representation, continuous spectra are discretized into semantically annotated range nodes, aligned with functional-group and vibration-type entities from a chemical ontology, and augmented with task-specific prompt and response nodes, enabling a single graph backbone to support node-level functional group classification, edge-level peak-pair relationship judgment, and graph-level molecular classification tasks through large language model encoding and graph neural network inference, without task-specific architectural redesign. Evaluated on 306 organic molecules with infrared spectra, SpectralTAG achieves AUC > 0.98 on edge- and graph-level tasks across 24 encoder-GNN combinations, with LLaMa2-7b paired with R-GCN delivering the most consistent cross-task performance. The framework further supports multitask training with negligible performance trade-off and exhibits emerging zero-shot and few-shot generalization under disjoint label conditions. Significance These results establish textual attribute graphs as a viable paradigm for unifying heterogeneous scientific data within a single reasoning architecture, with implications beyond spectroscopy for broader knowledge-enhanced scientific analysis.

title: ESI-Orbitrap MS enables reliable lead isotopic measurements in lake sediment cores
abstract: Background High resolution mass spectrometry, and particularly Orbitrap based instrumentations, are emerging as powerful technologies for speciation analysis, mainly to collect reliable information on isotope ratios (IRs). During recent years, traditional, stable isotopic systems, namely H, C, N, O and S have been investigated, but we only recently demonstrated that a dedicated complexation procedure followed by collisional dissociation may enable the investigation of metal ion IRs, and particularly lead, employing a standard electrospray ionization source. The procedure has not yet been demonstrated to be applicable to real-world samples. Results A total of 31 sediment samples from Lake Como were analyzed for lead IRs by both ESI-Orbitrap and Multi collector ICP-MS. Minor modifications to the original ESI-Orbitrap method, including increased ligand concentration, were required due to sample complexity; the simple Standard–Sample Bracketing (SSB) procedure was demonstrated to be effective in correcting the mass bias. Bland–Altman analysis showed no statistically significant differences between the two methods (95% confidence level) for the two isotope ratios 204 Pb/ 206 Pb and 207 Pb/ 206 Pb, while a small deviation (<2‰) was observed for the 208 Pb/ 206 Pb, remaining acceptable for environmental applications. The isotopic data trend identified leaded gasoline as the main contributor to lead contamination in Lake Como during the period 1950-2000. Significance This work presents the first reported application of ESI-Orbitrap-based metal isotopic analysis in complex environmental matrices. Factors influencing accuracy and precision were systematically evaluated, demonstrating robust analytical performance. The results establish the potential of the ESI-Orbitrap approach for determining isotope ratios of metal ions in real-world samples.

title: Wide-range and sensitive detection of LPS using a transporter@liposome enhanced electrochemical aptasensor
abstract: Stringent detection of lipopolysaccharide (LPS) is crucial for ensuring drug and food safety, enabling effective control of endotoxin contamination in pharmaceuticals and food. Given the wide variation in LPS concentrations across different matrices, the assay methods for LPS are extremely needed combining a wide dynamic range with high sensitivity. Employing metallohelicate embedded liposomal for electrochemical sensor modification, a novel strategy is developed for high-performance detection of LPS with aptamer probes. Metallohelicates are non-destructively incorporated into the lipid bilayer and act as a selective chloride ion transporter, enhancing the influx of chloride ions across the membrane, thereby increasing the permeability of the liposomal membrane and its conductivity. The current response is therefore amplified, significantly improving the sensitivity and reducing the limit of detection (LOD). The extensive surface area of liposomal spherical structure with high-density aptamers also greatly enhances its capacity to adsorb high-concentration targets. This aptasensor achieves a LOD of 0.44 fg/mL and provides an extremely wide dynamic range up to 1 μg/mL, with satisfied recovery and accuracy for LPS detection in pharmaceutical injections and food matrices.

title: Mechanisms and applications of condensed RNA-based molecular crowding on enhancing RNA aptamer performance
abstract: Background RNA aptamers represent promising recognition bioreceptors for biosensing, yet practical applications are severely hampered by limited binding affinity, poor thermal stability and high susceptibility to nuclease-mediated degradation. Intracellular molecular crowding environments driven by liquid-liquid phase separation can remodel RNA conformation and improve biomolecular function, inspiring the construction of artificial condensed RNA systems to address the performance bottlenecks of RNA aptamers for foodborne pathogen detection. In this work, we engineered a CUG-trinucleotide-repeat-based condensed RNA platform coordinated with cationic Poly-l-lysine (Poly-L-Lys) to enhance the detection performance of an RNA aptamer targeting Staphylococcus aureus (S. aureus), a critical food-contaminating pathogen. Results Non-hollow RNA condensates with heterogeneous spatial architecture were successfully formed in vitro. Compared with non-condensed aptamers, the condensed RNA achieved 22.04% higher binding affinity, an 11.63% elevated melting temperature, and improved nuclease resistance. Mechanistic investigations revealed that molecular crowding rearranged aptamer secondary-structure, switched binding thermodynamics from entropy-driven to enthalpy-driven, and accelerated target-binding kinetics. After integration into a pH-sensitive colorimetric assay, key analytical performance metrics including sensitivity, linear dynamic range, limit of detection, and reproducibility were comprehensively characterized. The sensor exhibited a sensitivity of 0.06 absorbance per log 10 (CFU·mL -1 ), a linear dynamic range spanning 10 2 -10 8 CFU mL -1 , with a limit of detection of 236 ± 43 CFU mL -1 . Satisfactory assay selectivity, good reproducibility, and acceptable recoveries ranging from 80% to 120% were achieved across multiple complex food matrices including pork, oilseed rape, milk and apple juice. Significance This work establishes a feasible molecular crowding engineering strategy for boosting RNA aptamer performance. The condensed RNA sensing platform provides a reliable analytical tool for food-safety monitoring and opens new avenues for designing next-generation nucleic-acid-based biosensors.

title: Spatial organization of glucose oxidase and catalase in layered polyethylenimine coated carbon nanotube electrodes affects coupled reaction kinetics and oxygen recycling in glucose biosensors
abstract: The buildup of H 2 O 2 often diminishes the sensitivity and stability of glucose oxidase (GOx)-based glucose biosensors. This work assessed four carbon nanotubes (CNT) and polyethylenimine (PEI) - based biocatalyst configurations using a layer-by-layer approach (CNT/PEI/GOx; CNT/PEI/GOx-Cat; CNT/PEI/GOx/PEI/Cat; CNT/PEI/Cat/PEI/GOx) to modulate the H 2 O 2 diffusion route and O 2 regeneration via catalase (Cat). Voltammetric and amperometric analyses were conducted in 0.1 M phosphate-buffered saline at pH 7.4 (aerobic conditions) at a potential of -0.45 V vs. Ag/AgCl. The optimal configuration was CNT/PEI/GOx/PEI/Cat, exhibiting analytical performance metrics of J max of 22.0 μA cm -2 , K m app of 6.55 mM, sensitivity of 3.34 μA×cm -2 ×mM -1 , and LOD of ≈ 44.84 μM. This structure exhibited an active enzyme coverage (as FADH 2 ) of 16.47 pM·cm -2 and maintained signal retention of around 90% through the fourth cycle, showing that the rate-limiting factor under amperometric circumstances is governed by the generation, diffusion, and conversion of H 2 O 2 , as well as the availability of O 2 , rather than exclusively by direct electron transfer (DET). Positioning catalase as the topmost layer above GOx (isolated from PEI) efficiently inhibits H 2 O 2 buildup next to the electrode while regenerating local O 2 , hence optimizing catalytic current and stability. This configuration also achieved the most accurate glucose recovery (average error ∼3%) in spiked solutions containing common electroactive interferents, confirming its practical reliability for complex sample analysis. These results provide a structured framework for the development of more sensitive and resilient glucose biosensors.

title: Filter paper-based wet assay with programmable DNA spacer-guided hotspots for dual-mode detection of chloramphenicol
abstract: Background Reliable analysis of antibiotic residues in complex food matrices remains challenging owing to severe matrix interference and insufficient signal reproducibility. Conventional dry-phase paper-based sensors often suffer from coffee-ring effects and uneven signal outputs, compromising both detection sensitivity and analytical reliability. Therefore, the development of sensing platforms with enhanced sensitivity, analytical reliability, and portable signal readout remains highly desirable for practical food analysis. Results Herein, a dual-modal SERS/colorimetric sensing platform with a self-validating signal readout strategy was constructed on a hydrophobic silver-sputtered filter paper for reliable chloramphenicol (CAP) detection. The innovative wet-phase assembly interface effectively suppressed the coffee-ring effect and improved signal uniformity and reproducibility. Upon target recognition, a hybridization chain reaction-mediated programmable DNA spacer regulated the average interparticle spacing of polyadenine-modified gold nanoparticles (AuNPs pA )@4-ATP, enabling the programmable formation of uniform and high-density SERS hotspots. Coupled with a portable Raman spectrometer, the SERS mode achieved ultrasensitive CAP detection over the range of 0.5-1000 ng/mL with a detection limit (LOD) of 6 pg/mL. Meanwhile, unassembled AuNPs pA @4-ATP served as nanozymes to catalyze TMB oxidation for smartphone-based colorimetric detection (10-1000 ng/mL, LOD 0.7 ng/mL). Importantly, these two complementary modes cross-validated each other, substantially enhancing detection reliability. The platform was successfully validated in spiked tap water, milk, and honey samples, underscoring its strong potential for portable food safety analysis. Significance This work presents a wet-phase plasmonic paper-based dual-mode sensing strategy with a self-validating signal readout strategy that combines ultrasensitive detection with built-in signal readout verification, providing a reliable and portable platform for sensitive food safety monitoring.

title: Highly fluorescent Cucurbit[7]uril covalent organic frameworks for fluorescence sensor array
abstract: Developing highly fluorescent COFs represents a challenging task due to their aggregation-caused quenching effect. In this research, highly fluorescent COFs were successfully constructed by introducing Q[7] as a macrocyclic framework unit into their backbone via a mechanical interlocking strategy. These Q[7]-based polycyclic COFs exhibited fluorescence quantum yields that were 10 times higher than those of their Q[7]-free counterparts, owing to the weakened interlayer aggregation and the cavity confinement effect of Q[7]. The recognition sites from Q[7] and also endowed these Q[7]-based polycyclic COFs with a prominent fluorescence response to various targets. These prominent properties enable COFs as a sensor array for highly sensitive identification and detection of 13 sulfonamide antibiotics (SAs) with detection limits down to the nanomolar range, with recovery rates of 90.3%-104.7% in real samples. The supramolecular isolation strategy and cavity confinement effect caused by Q[7] will drive increased interest in fabricating COFs using macrocyclic molecules.

title: Vibrational spectroscopy of microorganisms: A review
abstract: Vibrational spectroscopic methods, mid- and near-infrared, and Raman spectroscopies, have been extensively applied to the study of microorganisms. This is due to the relatively rapid analysis time, relative low-cost, experimental flexibility, and phenotypic nature of these methods. Consequently, vibrational spectroscopies have been investigated for clinical, environmental and industrial microbiology applications. This review outlines the principles of mid- and near-infrared, and Raman spectroscopies, and steps through vibrational spectroscopic experiments in the context of microbiological studies. Further applications within species/strain identification, antimicrobial resistance, bioremediation, cell sorting and intracellular microbial protein analysis are examined. Vibrational spectroscopy is expected to become increasingly routine in microbial analyses, particularly in clinical settings, driven by the harmonisation of spectral databases, the expanding application of deep learning methods and improved instrumentation to reduce sampling-to-reporting time.

title: A sequentially activated DNA biosensor for in vivo molecular imaging of nickel ion release from nickel alloy implants
abstract: Background Existing fluorescent probes for nickel ions (Ni 2+ ) are inadequate for in vivo monitoring of Ni 2+ release kinetics and deep-tissue tracing of nickel alloy implants intended for clinical use. Therefore, in this study, a sequentially activated DNA nanomachine (18S-Zyme-tFNA) was developed for in vivo imaging of cytoplasmic Ni 2+ . Results The 18S-Zyme-tFNA utilizes a Ni 2+ -dependent DNAzyme as its core recognition module. Its catalytic domain is pre-hybridized with a lock strand complementary to 18S rRNA, thereby maintaining the DNAzyme in an inactive state prior to cytoplasmic entry. Upon cellular internalization, the abundant endogenous 18S rRNA competitively displaces the lock strand via sequence-specific hybridization, restoring the catalytic conformation of the DNAzyme. In the presence of Ni 2+ , the activated DNAzyme site-specifically cleaves the riboadenosine (rA) residue within the substrate strand, inducing spatial separation of the fluorophore and quencher and consequently eliciting a fluorescence signal. Critically, each enzyme molecule catalyzes multiple substrate cleavage events, thereby achieving robust signal amplification via an enzymatic turnover mechanism. Experimental results demonstrate that 18S-Zyme-tFNA achieved a low limit of detection (LOD = 0.09 μM) and demonstrated excellent selectivity for Ni 2+ over other metal ions. In particular, 18S-Zyme-tFNA enabled in vivo visualization of Ni 2+ in foot, subcutaneous, and intraosseous nickel alloy implants, with no significant organ toxicity observed. Significance This study develops a sequentially activated DNAzyme-tFNA biosensor that enables selective and amplified imaging of cytoplasmic Ni 2+ in living systems. By integrating 18S rRNA-mediated intracellular activation with Ni 2+ -dependent catalytic signal generation, the platform improves the specificity and biological applicability of DNA-based metal-ion sensing. Importantly, it extends Ni 2+ imaging from cells to mammalian nickel alloy implant models, providing a useful tool for evaluating implant-associated nickel release and biosafety.

title: A near-infrared fluorescent probe for point-of-care screening of male infertility in seminal plasma
abstract: Diagnosis of male infertility currently relies on cumbersome semen analysis and lacks a rapid screening method. Elevated seminal plasma Hcy and Cys are early biomarkers linked to impaired sperm quality, yet no fluorescent probe has been reported for their direct detection in this matrix. To fill this gap, we developed JC-THA, a near-infrared probe comprising a julolidine-coumarin core and a chlorine-substituted tetrahydroacridine salt as the thiol-reactive site. Exploiting differences in molecular volume and electronic effects between Hcy/Cys and GSH, JC-THA exhibits a strong turn-on response toward Hcy and Cys but negligible enhancement toward GSH, enabling selective discrimination. The probe completes quantitative measurement within 4 min, with detection limits of 40 nM for Hcy and 39 nM for Cys. It shows good cytocompatibility and enables the first fluorescence imaging of Hcy/Cys in NTERA-2 cl.D1 cells. We also pioneered the direct use of this probe in real human seminal plasma, obtaining spike recoveries of 90%-110% for Hcy, which preliminarily supports its clinical feasibility. A smartphone-based colorimetric device using JC-THA further allows rapid visual semi-quantitative analysis via visible color changes, demonstrating point-of-care testing potential. Collectively, this work offers a simple and cost-effective near-infrared tool for early male infertility screening, with considerable promise for clinical translation.

title: Self-luminescent cyano-vinylene-linked covalent organic framework boosts coreactant-free electrochemiluminescence for sensing
abstract: Exogenous coreactants required in conventional electrochemiluminescence (ECL) systems inevitably bring about toxicity, poor signal reproducibility and unstable luminescence output, severely restricting the biological compatibility and practical application of ECL sensors. Herein, we designed a novel self-luminescent cyano-vinylene-linked covalent organic framework (CV-COF) via Knoevenagel polycondensation using 1,3,6,8-tetrakis(p-formylphenyl) pyrene (Py) and 2,2'-([2,2'-bipyridine]-5,5'-diyl) diacetonitrile (Bpda) as building monomers. Its π-conjugated skeleton and electron-deficient units boost intramolecular charge transfer to generate coreactant-free ECL without extra oxidants/reductants or dissolved oxygen. Leveraging this self-luminescent CV-COF, a highly sensitive and selective ECL sensing platform was constructed for iodide ion detection, achieving a low detection limit of 83.8 nM, and could also quantitatively detect iodixanol with an LOD of 74.47 nM. This work pioneers the design of self-luminescent cyano-vinylene COFs as coreactant-free ECL emitters, establishes a universal molecular engineering strategy for constructing intrinsic self-enhanced ECL COF materials, and broadens the application prospect of COF-based ECL sensors in environmental pollutant monitoring.

title: Why choose between prediction power and mechanistic insight in QSRR modeling? A case study of artificial membrane chromatography and machine learning
abstract: Quantitative structure-retention relationship (QSRR) modeling of immobilized artificial membrane (IAM) chromatography was performed on a chemically diverse set of 2003 analytes to determine whether mechanistically interpretable, descriptor-based models can match the predictive performance of advanced machine-learning approaches. Chromatographic hydrophobicity indices (CHI IAM ) were measured under standardized fast-gradient IAM conditions and modeled using three molecular representation strategies: physicochemical descriptors, ECFP4 fingerprints, and a Graph Isomorphism Network (GIN) operating on molecular graphs. Among the descriptor- and fingerprint-based methods, the Gradient Boosting Regressor gave the best performance. The descriptor-based model achieved a test R 2 of 0.817, MAE of 4.43, and RMSE of 6.46 CHI IAM units, whereas the GIN model showed only a marginal numerical improvement (R 2 = 0.828, MAE = 4.27, RMSE = 6.25). In contrast, fingerprint-based modeling performed worse (R 2 = 0.771, MAE = 5.04, RMSE = 7.22). Statistical analysis of paired prediction errors showed no significant difference between the descriptor-based and GIN models, while the fingerprint-based model was the least accurate of the three. The observed differences among the best models were smaller than the long-term reproducibility of the IAM protocol. Applicability-domain analysis further showed that approximately 94-99% of compounds fell within the interpolation region. SHAP analysis identified lipophilicity, ionization, charge, and polarity as the major determinants of IAM retention, with cationic character enhancing retention and high polarity reducing it. These results demonstrate that descriptor-based QSRR modeling can achieve near-deep learning performance while preserving mechanistic interpretability, providing a practical and physically grounded strategy for IAM retention prediction.

title: Signal-amplified electrochemical aptasensor based on multi-branched circular DNA and bimetallic nanomaterials for sensitive histamine detection in complex food matrices
abstract: Background Histamine is a high-risk biogenic amine produced during food spoilage. Excessive intake can trigger severe allergic reactions or poisoning, making the development of an accurate detection method critically important. This study proposes a novel electrochemical aptasensor for the sensitive detection of histamine. Results The sensor comprises a multi-branched circular DNA structure, thionine/Au@prussian blue analog (Thi/Au@PBA), Au@Pd nanoflowers (Au@Pd NFs), and an Apt screened via molecular docking and experiment. Compared with the linear DNA, the amplification effect of the circular was observed with low and high concentrations, demonstrating that the circular structure can effectively enhance the sensor's signal. The response signal difference between the presence and absence of the target on the Au@Pd NFs-modified electrode was 1.55 times that of the bare electrode. Furthermore, in a solution of Thi at a certain concentration, the signal response of the Au@PBA-modified electrode was 2.77 times that of the bare electrode. The resulting aptasensor exhibited an ultra-low detection limit of 2.16 pg/mL and a broad linear range (0.01-500 ng/mL) for histamine, alongside high selectivity, reproducibility, repeatability and stability. The sensor's accurate detection results in food matrices (salmon, canned tuna, and red wine) have confirmed its practical value. Significance and novelty This study proposes an electrochemical aptasensor based on multi-branched circular DNA and bimetallic nanomaterials for the sensitive detection of histamine. This sensor shows great potential in the field of rapid food safety detection.

title: Direct and efficient analysis on monosaccharide composition of polysaccharides from various sources by GEMSTONE–TOCSY NMR spectroscopy
abstract: NMR spectroscopy is a powerful spectroscopic technique that permits the detailed study of the molecular structure elucidation and mixture component analysis, especially in the identification of complex mixtures. However, the conventional 1 H NMR generally suffers from crowded resonances when measuring and identifying carbohydrates of polysaccharide hydrolysis systems, which contain various chemically similar compounds and even multiple isomeric monosaccharides. Herein we describe the application of a targeted detection NMR approach, gradient-enhanced multiplet-selective targeted-observation NMR experiment GEMSTONE-TOCSY, exploited for studying polysaccharide hydrolysis mixtures by spectroscopically targeting the desired compounds in separate 1D NMR spectra. There are six model mixtures of natural bioactive polysaccharide hydrolysis (including 11 monosaccharides) and three real reaction systems (carob seed polysaccharide, tremella polysaccharide and stachyose hydrolysis), which are tested by GEMSTONE-TOCSY NMR showing satisfactory performance in monosaccharide identification and structure analysis even when proton signals are crowded and overlapped in conventional 1 H NMR. Moreover, GEMSTONE-TOCSY NMR uses a fast, single-scan method that allows selective excitation of the signals of a single proton multiplet and available for highly efficient analysis. The results demonstrate that GEMSTONE-TOCSY NMR technique is robust and reliable to analyze and identify monosaccharide composition of various polysaccharides from mixture systems, even providing efficient analysis tool for detecting the polysaccharide hydrolysis process.

title: Electrochemical control meets enhanced Raman sensitivity: a critical review of electrochemical surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (EC-SERS) sensors
abstract: Electrochemical surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (EC-SERS) is an advanced analytical technique that integrates the molecular specificity and high sensitivity of surface-enhanced Raman scattering with the dynamic control of electrochemistry. This hybrid approach enables real-time investigation of interfacial processes, including adsorption phenomena, charge-transfer interactions, and redox reactions at electrified surfaces. In recent years, significant progress has been achieved through the development of engineered plasmonic substrates, hybrid nanomaterials, and improved spectroelectrochemical configurations, greatly enhancing sensitivity, stability, and analytical performance. This review provides a critical overview of EC-SERS advancements over the last few years, focusing on substrate design strategies, methodological developments, and applications in energy systems, catalysis, and sensing with particular attention to analytical figures of merit, including sensitivity, selectivity, reproducibility, and quantitative reliability. Despite notable progress, several challenges remain, including signal variability, substrate heterogeneity, and limited standardization across studies. Finally, emerging approaches aimed at overcoming these limitations are discussed, highlighting the potential of EC-SERS as a robust and versatile platform for next-generation analytical sensing and in situ characterization of complex electrochemical interfaces.

title: Biomedical and clinical frontiers of LA-ICP-MS: Insights from cell cultures and animal models to human samples
abstract: ABSTRACT Laser ablation – inductively coupled plasma – mass spectrometry (LA-ICP-MS) has become a powerful tool for the spatially resolved analysis of elements and biomolecules in biomedical and clinical research. This review covers advances in instrumentation, sample preparation, calibration and labelling, most of them published between 2014 and 2026, which have considerably expanded the application of LA-ICP-MS across biological systems, from single cells and spheroids to animal models and human tissues. Rather than describing instrumentation in detail, we focus on the experimental parameters that determine high-resolution imaging and on the main challenges of quantitative bioimaging, including matrix effects, internal standardization and the limited availability of certified reference materials (CRMs). Current quantification approaches are discussed, such as gelatine- and hydroxyapatite-based standards and isotope dilution mass spectrometry. The review also covers the imaging of endogenous elements and of biomolecules using metal-labelled immunoprobes, including lanthanide chelates, metal-chelating polymers and metal nanoparticles (NPs). Representative applications illustrate quantitative analysis at the single-cell and tissue levels, together with multimodal workflows combining LA-ICP-MS with matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionisation, optical microscopy or magnetic resonance imaging, spanning the biodistribution of NPs and metallodrugs and studies of neurodegenerative diseases, cancer and toxicology. Finally, we critically assess the challenges that still limit a broader adoption of LA-ICP-MS, particularly the lack of matrix-matched CRMs and standardized sample-preparation protocols, which hinder traceable quantification and interlaboratory comparability. Multimodal and multiparametric approaches are expected to play an increasingly important role, but their routine use will require further methodological standardization before LA-ICP-MS can be widely adopted in biomedical and clinical practice.

title: Plant-wearable fluorescent hydrogel patch based on PDA-PEI copolymer dots for on-site visual detection of glyphosate
abstract: Background Glyphosate (GLY) residues are difficult to remove from agricultural products and pose potential risks to food safety, making their sensitive detection highly desirable. In this study, a Cu 2+ -mediated ratiometric fluorescence sensing platform was constructed for the sensitive detection of GLY by physically mixing polydopamine-polyethyleneimine copolymer dots (PDA-PEI CPDs) with terephthalic acid (PTA) based on a competitive coordination strategy. Results Cu 2+ coordinated with the amino groups on the surface of CPDs and the carboxyl groups of PTA to form a CPDs-PTA-Cu 2+ complex. This process quenched the green fluorescence of CPDs at 530 nm while generating a new blue emission at 450 nm. Upon the addition of GLY, competitive coordination between GLY and Cu 2+ disrupted the complex, resulting in fluorescence recovery at 530 nm and fluorescence quenching at 450 nm, thereby producing a ratiometric fluorescence response. The sensor shows linear ranges of 0-80 μg/mL for GLY (LOD = 5.73 ng/mL). To meet the requirements of on-site applications, a CPDs-Cu 2+ @sodium alginate hydrogel was further prepared. Under 365 nm excitation, the hydrogel responded to GLY through single-emission fluorescence recovery at 530 nm. The hydrogel enabled smartphone-assisted RGB quantitative analysis and in situ semi-quantitative screening of GLY on vegetable surfaces using a wearable hydrogel patch. Significance By integrating solution-phase ratiometric fluorescence quantification with hydrogel-based visual readout, a simple and portable sensing platform was established for accurate GLY determination and visual screening of surface residues.

title: Photoactivated tetrahedral DNA nanostructure for intracellular imaging of ATP
abstract: Background Adenosine triphosphate (ATP) is not only the most direct energy source in living organisms, but also acts as a signaling molecule to regulate various biological pathways. Thus, accurate detection and intracellular imaging of ATP are of great significance for disease diagnosis. However, existing ATP detection and imaging methods generally face challenges of relatively low sensitivity and limited spatiotemporal accuracy. In this work, a photoactivated tetrahedral DNA nanostructure (PTDN) was developed for sensitive detection and precise intracellular imaging of ATP. Results After PTDN was delivered into cells, ultraviolet (UV) irradiation cleaved the photocleavable linker on H1, activating PTDN. The ATP in the cells bonded to its adapter on S4, releasing T strand and triggering catalytic hairpin assembly (CHA) among H1, H2 and H3, restoring fluorescence signal. The T strand released from this process continuously triggered CHA reactions, forming TDN-mediated DNA nanonetwork. The developed PTDN system achieved significant signal amplification through spatial confinement effects for ATP detection with a limit of detection (LOD) as low as 0.41 nM. Combined with the exogenous light activation strategy, precise intracellular imaging of MCF-7 and HeLa cells was achieved. Moreover, this system exhibited excellent selectivity for ATP and has been successfully applied to the actual sample testing of cell lysates. Significance This work simultaneously overcomes the challenges of low sensitivity and limited spatiotemporal accuracy in ATP detection and in situ cell imaging. This externally light-activated DNA nanonetwork provides a promising fluorescence platform for the sensitive and accurate monitoring and imaging of biomarkers, and is expected to be extended for the detection of other signaling molecules.

title: Mislabeling (label noise) – an often overlooked issue in chemometrics
abstract: Background In supervised learning, errors can arise in label values. This fact is well known in machine learning (ML), where it has been studied since the late 1960s, but is often ignored in chemometrics. The main reason for mislabeling is human errors when supervision is carried out by a person. It is also inevitable in cases where a continuous process is divided into stages for their subsequent supervised discrimination. Another reason is the imperfection of an instrumental method, which poorly reflects the differences between classes. Results This paper pursues two goals. The first one is to introduce the concept of mislabeling in chemometrics. The second goal is to share our experience in solving mislabeling problems that arise in real-world examples. In our opinion, the most appropriate approach is the integration of the domain knowledge with the outlier detection methods, which should be based on probabilistic (soft) classifiers. This approach is used systematically and is illustrated by three cases that employ both well-established and new methods. Significance Mislabeling is a real problem that can occur across a variety of applications, reaching up to 20%, and in some areas, such as medicine, this rate can be even higher. There is no doubt that mislabeling deserves investigation and correction. In mission-critical fields, particularly in medicine, the cost of an error caused by mislabeled data can be significant, measured not only in financial losses but also in human lives.

title: Discovery of thiol-reactive Staphylococcus aureus sortase A inhibitors from natural products by machine learning and thiocholine mass-shift profiling
abstract: Methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) remains a major clinical challenge, and Sortase A (SrtA), a cysteine transpeptidase involved in surface-protein anchoring and biofilm formation, represents an attractive anti-virulence target. In this study, we developed an integrated analytical workflow combining machine-learning (ML)-guided taxon prioritisation, affinity magnetic capture, mass-shift profiling, and biochemical target-engagement assays to identify natural-product SrtA inhibitors from complex botanical extracts. A random-forest classifier trained on ChEMBL SrtA bioactivity data was applied to the LOTUS natural-product database to prioritise Michael-acceptor-containing botanical sources, leading to the selection of Piper retrofractum for constituent-level analysis. Subsequent chemical profiling and affinity-capture experiments identified piperlongumine as a thiol-reactive constituent preferentially associated with active SrtA. Piperlongumine inhibited SrtA transpeptidase activity with an IC 50 of 27.83 ± 1.04 μmol/L and showed a higher TCI-adduct response and stronger SrtA inhibition than the structurally related alkaloid piperine. Time-dependent enzyme inhibition, competitive 5-FAM-LPETG bead imaging, and mPEG-maleimide thiol-occupancy analysis further supported thiol-dependent SrtA engagement under the assay conditions. Piperlongumine also inhibited biofilm formation across multiple S. aureus strains while exerting limited effects on planktonic growth at corresponding concentrations. These findings demonstrate an analytical strategy that links computational prioritisation, crude-extract chemical profiling, affinity capture, and target-engagement validation for the discovery of thiol-reactive natural products targeting SrtA.

title: ZnO/ZIF-8@Au nanoarchitectures with nanoconfinement-enhanced plasmonic coupling for ultrasensitive photoelectrochemical detection of malondialdehyde
abstract: Background Malondialdehyde (MDA) is a pivotal oxidative stress biomarker implicated in cardiovascular diseases, neurodegeneration, and cancer; however, its trace quantification in complex biological matrices remains analytically daunting. Photoelectrochemical (PEC) sensing offers inherently low background noise and exceptional sensitivity for trace bioanalysis. Nevertheless, efficiently translating molecular recognition into amplified PEC signals remains a challenge. Results We report a nanoconfinement-mediated PEC interface that integrates covalent molecular conjugation with plasmonic amplification within a crystalline matrix scaffold. Within this nanoconfined environment, localized Au nanoparticles serve as plasmonic amplifiers that anchor 4-aminothiophenol (4-ATP) receptors. Upon MDA recognition, the optimized sensor exhibits dual linear detection ranges spanning 0.001 to 1.0 nmol L -1 (R 1 2 = 0.9928) and 1.0 to 1000 nmol L -1 (R 2 2 = 0.9992), yielding an ultralow detection limit of 0.3 pmol L -1 . Significance The confined Schiff-base reaction between 4-ATP and MDA generates an interfacial reaction product, leading to a new absorption band at approximately 450 nm and modulation of the Au LSPR band. This change is mainly attributed to the altered local dielectric environment around Au NPs. Wavelength-dependent operando transient photovoltage spectroscopy (TPV) provides mechanistic evidence that plasmon-driven hot-carrier injection augments PEC signal output. Overall, this work establishes an interface-engineering paradigm that integrates molecular conjugation with plasmonic coupling, offering a promising blueprint for the PEC detection of small-molecule biomarkers.

title: Deep learning-based excitation-emission matrix fluorescence spectroscopic analysis of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons in coal tar
abstract: Background Rapid and accurate analysis of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) in coal tar (CT) is essential yet challenging due to spectral overlap and matrix effects. Excitation-emission matrix (EEM) fluorescence spectral analysis using deep learning algorithms can address this challenge. Results Coal tar samples were extracted and diluted with cyclohexane. A dataset of 1173 EEM spectra covering 3- to 6-ring PAHs and various concentration gradients was constructed. Seven machine learning algorithms were used for qualitative classification of PAHs, and the deep learning algorithm, ResNet18, achieved the highest accuracy, close to 90%. Quantitative analysis was performed using a convolutional neural network-based variational autoencoder (CNN-VAE) model, yielding Root mean square error (RMSE) and (Mean absolute error) MAE values as low as 0.0036 mg/L and 0.0028 mg/L, respectively. These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method for accurate PAH quantification in complex coal-tar matrices. Significance and novelty This new approach provides a cost-effective, rapid, and reliable alternative to conventional methods, mitigating issues such as Rayleigh scattering and spectral overlap. It offers a new strategy for detecting PAH molecules in complex matrices.

title: Automated nanopore sensing by current-feedback membrane reformation
abstract: Stochastic nanopore sensing relies on large numbers of current blockage signals for statistical molecular analysis. Automated formation of planar bilayer lipid membranes (pBLMs) has been reported, but sustaining a single biological nanopore remains challenging, since nanopore reconstitution is inherently probabilistic. Here, we report an automated, current-feedback nanopore sensing platform that autonomously sustains single alpha-hemolysin (αHL) nanopores through repeated pBLM reformation. The sensing platform locates the pBLM formation position by measuring membrane capacitance, recognizes nanopore reconstitution through ion current feedback, and automatically reforms the pBLM once multiple nanopores have reconstituted. We first optimized the experimental parameters, including stage velocity, calibration interval, and αHL concentration, to achieve stable long-term operation. Under these optimized conditions, the system repeatedly formed pBLMs over 6 h with almost no spontaneous membrane rupture, while autonomously maintaining single-nanopore measurements. We then applied the platform to automated stochastic nanopore sensing of single-stranded DNA. Over 3 h of continuous operation, the dwell time, current blockage rate, and translocation event frequency remained unchanged, confirming stable sensing performance during long-term autonomous measurements. These results demonstrate that combining capacitance-based determination of the pBLM formation position with current-feedback-controlled pBLM reformation realizes long-term nanopore measurements with substantially reduced operator intervention. Although signals analyses are currently performed retrospectively, the present platform provides a basis for further development toward fully automated single-molecule analysis.

title: Ratiometric fluorescence probe based on lipase coated Au NCs covalently linked to FITC for smartphone-integrated dual-mode detection of paraquat
abstract: The use of paraquat (PQ) poses significant environmental and health risks, necessitating the development of rapid and sensitive detection methods. Herein, a novel ratiometric fluorescent probe, FITC-Lip-Au NCs, was constructed by covalently linking fluorescein isothiocyanate (FITC) to Lip-Au NCs prepared using lipase (Lip) as a pioneering protein template for the selective and visual detection of PQ. Upon PQ interaction, FITC-Lip-Au NCs showed electrostatic interaction-assisted dynamic quenching at 650 nm and a constant signal at 520 nm, enabling a LOD of 15 nM and a linear range of 0.025-45 μM. Leveraging the distinct color change, paper-based and hydrogel-film sensors coupled with smartphone RGB analysis enabled on-site visual and quantitative detection of PQ. This work not only expanded protein template diversity for nanocluster synthesis but also presented a reliable, rapid, and dual-mode sensing strategy for monitoring PQ residues in food quality and safety.

title: Outside Front Cover
Editorial Board
RP-UHPLC/MS/MS reveals statin-induced alterations in profiles of free monohydroxy sterols and tocopherols in human plasma
abstract: Background Statins are the most prescribed cholesterol-lowering drugs in the world. Reversed-phase ultrahigh-performance liquid chromatography coupled with tandem mass spectrometry (RP-UHPLC/MS/MS) enables the analysis of isomeric lipid species, and the chemical derivatization enhances ionization efficiency. Here, we address the need for a validated quantitative method for sterols and tocopherols in human plasma and its application for the characterization of statin-induced alterations in lipid composition at the level of isomeric species. Results We developed a high-throughput RP-UHPLC/MS/MS method using multiple reaction monitoring (MRM) in the negative ion mode, which is based on the chemical derivatization with 3-(chlorosulfonyl)benzoic acid. The optimized and validated method using eight internal standards (IS) was applied to NIST SRM 1950, which enabled the quantification of 18 sterol species and two tocopherols (α- and γ-tocopherols). The lipidomic profiling of human plasma samples obtained from 41 statin-treated and 41 statin-naïve subjects provided a broad overview of cholesterol-related lipids. The separation of sterol isomers was an essential aspect due to the varying statistical importance of individual isomeric species. Significance This methodology provides a highly sensitive and selective quantitative analysis of free sterol species and tocopherols with isomeric structural resolution, which is critical for biological interpretation. Univariate and multivariate statistical analyses demonstrated statistically significant alterations in the statin-treated cohort among endogenous free sterol species and α-tocopherol, while exogenous free sterols showed no statistically significant changes.

title: Automatic analyses of quantitative dried material spots by on-line coupling of sequential injection to high-performance liquid chromatography: A proof-of-concept
abstract: Background The development and integration of platforms for reliable handling of dried material spots (DMSs) as a front-end to advanced analytical instrumentation continues to pose methodological challenges. Although robotic platforms have been developed for autonomous manipulation of dried blood spot (DBS) cards, these systems exhibit limited flexibility regarding ancillary unit operations and remain incompatible with quantitative DMS (qDMS) devices. Results Leveraging off-the-shelf fluidic components using advanced liquid handling, this proof-of-concept work exploits the versatility of sequential injection-high-performance liquid chromatography (SI-HPLC) coupling for automatic processing and analysis of DMSs. The flow setup features a multi-position rotary valve as the core of the SI manifold connected to two 3D-printed 60-position racks. This hyphenation enables flexible in-vial processing of various DBS, qDBS, qDMS, and volumetric absorptive microsampling (VAMS) samples by controlled dispensing of microliter volumes of methanol for the spot rehydration, protein precipitation, and analyte elution, followed by mixing and homogenization of the eluate with water for the HPLC compatibility. Demonstrated on model non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs, the fully synchronized SI-HPLC setup enabled entirely unsupervised analysis of up to 120 DMS samples with triplicate HPLC injections per eluate (8.2 min each). Using a matrix-matched calibration based on spiking 10 μL of analyte-free blood, multiple qDBSs were eluted with 135 μL of methanol, followed by the eluate composition adjustment with 135 μL of water for HPLC compatibility prior to reversed-phase HPLC analysis. Under these conditions, calibrations were linear over 15 - 60, 0.8 - 12, 0.8 - 6, and 6.2 - 100 μg mL -1 ranges, and LODs were 5.7, 0.3, 0.3, and 1.4 μg mL -1 for ibuprofen, ketoprofen, diclofenac, and naproxen, respectively. The method precision was 2.3 - 12.7% RSD for intra-day and 9.3 - 13.2% RSD for inter-day experiments. The reliability of the proposed automatic SI-HPLC setup was demonstrated for qDBSs with therapeutic naproxen levels, with no statistically significant concentration differences at the 0.05 level when compared to manual qDBS processing with off-line analysis by capillary electrophoresis. Significance For the first time, the proposed analytical concept enables automatic handling and analysis of various DMS and qDMS samples, while using standard off-the-shelf SI and HPLC components and freely available control software.

title: Structure-Based Prediction of Reversed-Phase Liquid Chromatography Retention Time Using Machine-Learning Models Built from Miniature Datasets
abstract: : Structure-based chromatographic retention prediction is critical for efficient method development and impurity characterization or monitoring in pharmaceutical analysis yet remains challenging without proper databases. Here, we present a practical project-specific quantitative structure–retention relationship (QSRR) framework that integrates descriptor fusion with a rigorously designed feature- and model-selection strategy to enable accurate retention time (RT) prediction using unfiltered miniature reversed-phase liquid chromatography (RPLC) datasets. Six molecular descriptor libraries, along with their various combinations, were evaluated using multiple machine learning algorithms within a nested cross-validation (CV) framework optimized to balance model fit and generalizability. The workflow was benchmarked using three late-stage Pfizer small-molecule projects, each comprising 17–21 compounds, including an externally validated set. High prediction accuracy was achieved across all case studies (R 2 > 0.96, mean absolute percentage error < 9%), with absolute RT errors below 2.5 minutes (for analysis time ranging between 30 and 60 min) for all compounds in the EV set, including regioisomeric impurities. Notably, unlike the conventional localized QSRR modeling, the project-specific QSRR modeling does not require explicit structural similarity filtering because the compounds for model development and external validation are inherently chemically related.
