title: The sensing and anti-counterfeiting performance of novel tripodal cauldron-like lanthanide compounds: from molecule to composite material
abstract: Rapid, sensitive, and selective detection of explosives and pesticides is vital for environmental and human health. Herein, three tripodal cauldron-like compounds, [NH 2 (CH 3 ) 2 ] 6 [Ln 3 L 3 (OAc) 3 ]·4H 2 O·DMA·3CH 3 CN (L-Ln, Ln = Tb, Eu and Gd; DMA = N,N-dimethylacetamide), have been synthesized and characterized based on H 4 L, where a flexible diethylene oxide group is terminated by two 2,6-pyridinedicarboxylic acid (DPA) moieties. In these complexes, Ln III contained macrocycle is protected by folded alkyl ether chains of H 4 L. Benefiting from its bright green emission and excellent water stability, L-Tb enables rapid and sensitive detection of 4-nitrotoluene (4-NT) and paraquat (PQ) in aqueous media. For portability, a luminescent film (L-Tb@PMMA) was prepared to render stronger luminescence, mechanical robustness, and enhanced sensing capability. To further expand its practical applications, L-Tb@SA was developed using sodium alginate (SA) as the matrix. Leveraging its excellent hydrophilicity, L-Tb@SA exhibited enhanced sensing performance, characterized by an exceptionally fast response time ( 3 -HCl' vapors, underscoring their potential for information encryption and anti-counterfeiting applications. These results demonstrate the strong potential of lanthanide-based materials for practical use in environmental monitoring and anti-counterfeiting.

title: Data processing tools comparison applied to clinical datasets for untargeted GC-MS-based metabolomics
abstract: BACKGROUND: In metabolomics studies, biological data are highly complex, requiring robust computational tools to detect biological variation in the organism under investigation. Despite this, comparative studies of data processing software for GC-MS data are scarce. This work evaluated the performance of two open-source software programs, XCMS and MS-DIAL, on three datasets: cells, serum, and tissue, acquired by GC-MS. RESULTS: Software performance was assessed based on the quality of the raw data matrix, the number of extracted features, the presence of missing values, and the number of annotated metabolites or chemical classes. Overall, both tools produced robust matrices and adequate statistical models, with high similarity in the regulation of common metabolites. For the investigated datasets, XCMS demonstrated slightly better performance in raw matrix quality, while MS-DIAL showed a higher correlation with the annotations. The combination of matrices broadened metabolic coverage, allowing for improvements in supervised statistical models. The choice of data processing platform and the parameters used directly impact the extracted data matrix and the conclusions regarding metabolic alterations. SIGNIFICANCE: These observations reinforce the need for careful evaluation in metabolomics analyses, so that selection involves not only parameters such as the number of features and metabolites obtained, but also the method's stability and its ability to show the chemical variability of the analyzed biological system.

title: Separation and identification of dammarane-type ginsenoside isomers from Panax ginseng using cyclic ion mobility and tandem mass spectrometry
abstract: Background Dammarane-type ginsenosides (DTGs) exhibit extensive isomerism including aglycone isomers, glycosylation site isomers, double-bond positional isomers, and R/S configurational isomers. Many of these isomers co-elute in liquid chromatography and are difficult to distinguish by MS/MS alone, compromising the accuracy of identification in Panax ginseng extract. Consequently, a more systematic approach is needed to separate and identify these isomers. Results Multi-pass cyclic ion mobility (cIMS) was validated on both reference standards and Panax ginseng extracts for its ability to resolve challenging DTG isomers. Following optimization of the trap collision energy, a systematic putative identification strategy was established by integrating MS/MS data, CCS values of intact DTGs, and CCS values of their characteristic aglycone fragments. This approach enables the differentiation of aglycone isomers, sugar type isomers, glycosidic linkage isomers, glycosylation site isomers, R/S configurational isomers and double-bond positional isomers, markedly improving the reliability of identification. Significance The use of characteristic CCS values of homologous aglycones offers a complementary approach for inferring C-20 R/S configurations, which may help to address a key limitation of conventional MS in certain cases. While the current study focuses on ginsenosides, this workflow-particularly the integration of MS/MS with aglycone CCS data-may serve as a useful reference for isomer identification in other natural products with similar isomeric complexity.

title: Signal on–off ratiometric electrochemical immunosensor based on Au@C-COFs and Thi@aCOFs for ultrasensitive IGF-1 detection
abstract: Insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) is a critical biomarker linked to various human diseases, necessitating sensitive and reliable detection methods. Herein, we report a novel sandwich-type ratiometric electrochemical immunosensor with signal on-off capability for the ultrasensitive measurement of IGF-1. The sensor was constructed using gold nanoparticle-engineered carbonized covalent organic frameworks (Au@C-COFs) as the sensing platform and thionine-enriched alkynyl COFs (Thi@aCOFs) as the signal amplification probe. Au@C-COFs exhibited excellent electrocatalytic activity toward hydroquinone (HQ) oxidation, providing a stable internal reference signal, while Thi@aCOFs generated a concentration-dependent reporter signal upon specific recognition of IGF-1 via the immobilized aptamer. The ratiometric strategy effectively eliminated external interferences, significantly enhancing accuracy and reliability. Under optimal conditions, the biosensor displayed a wide linear range from 10 fM to 1 nM, a low detection limit of 0.45 fM (S/N = 3), good specificity, stability, and satisfactory reproducibility. Furthermore, the sensor performed well for measuring IGF-1 in diluted human serum, achieving satisfactory recoveries. This work presents a robust and adaptable platform toward ratiometric electrochemical biosensing, holding great promise to achieve clinical diagnosis and management treatment of IGF-1-related disorders.

title: Digitally plotted graphene oxide-modified paper for syringe-assisted micro-solid-phase extraction of antiepileptic drugs in rat blood
abstract: Background Graphene oxide (GO) has considerable potential as a sorbent for solid-phase extraction because it interacts strongly with aromatic compounds, yet practical use can be hindered by difficulties in handling GO powder and reproducibly immobilizing it on solid supports. Cellulose paper is an attractive low-cost substrate, although conventional coating methods may yield uneven deposition. Digital plotting offers a straightforward way to place GO onto paper with controlled deposition and without complicated chemical modification. Accordingly, this study addressed the need for a reproducibly fabricated GO-paper sorbent that could be incorporated into a simple flow-through micro-solid-phase extraction (μ-SPE) system for bioanalytical sample preparation. Results GO-modified cellulose paper was prepared with a commercial digital plotter, providing uniform and reproducible sorbent substrates. Initial screening of ten aromatic organic compounds led to the selection of carbamazepine and oxcarbazepine as model analytes. The optimized conditions were pH 6.0-7.5, a 5-min extraction period, and two GO layers. For spiked rat blood, 1 mL of sample underwent protein precipitation with 80% acetonitrile before GO-based extraction, followed by elution with 500 μL of 1% formic acid in acetonitrile. Placing the GO-modified paper in a syringe filter holder enabled syringe-assisted flow-through μ-SPE, with sample passage completed in approximately 30 s. Analysis by sweeping-micellar electrokinetic chromatography yielded recoveries of 87.5 ± 4.0 to 90.3 ± 3.1% for carbamazepine and 85.5 ± 4.7 to 89.1 ± 3.6% for oxcarbazepine. Significance and novelty This work is novel in integrating digitally controlled GO deposition on cellulose paper with a syringe-assisted flow-through μ-SPE configuration. The resulting approach combines reproducible sorbent preparation with rapid sample handling, low sorbent and solvent requirements, and effective cleanup of pretreated blood samples. It therefore shows the potential of digitally fabricated GO-paper sorbents as a simple and accessible platform for bioanalytical sample preparation.

title: Laser-induced graphene synergized with Pr/Zn-MOF for an enhanced flexible electrochemical sensing platform toward dual detection of estrogens
abstract: Estrogens, as typical endocrine-disrupting compounds, pose potential risks to ecological safety and public health even at trace levels, making the development of highly sensitive detection methods crucial. In this work, a flexible electrochemical sensor was developed for the highly sensitive dual detection of 17β-estradiol (E2) and estriol (E3). A three-electrode system of three-dimensional porous laser-induced graphene (LIG) was directly fabricated on a flexible polyimide substrate via laser writing and further modified with a Pr/Zn metal-organic framework (MOF). MOF modification shifted the electrode process from diffusion-controlled to adsorption-controlled, significantly enhancing the enrichment of target molecules, while the 3D porous LIG provided abundant active sites and rapid electron transport channels. The synergistic effect of these two components substantially improved sensor sensitivity. The sensor exhibited linear detection ranges of 1 × 10 -9 to 5 × 10 -6 mol L -1 for E2 and 1 × 10 -8 to 5 × 10 -6 mol L -1 for E3, with detection limits as low as 3.5 × 10 -10 mol L -1 and 3.5 × 10 -9 mol L -1 , respectively. It also demonstrated excellent anti-interference performance, reproducibility, and long-term stability, achieving recoveries of 92%-111% in spiked real-sample tests. The combination of superior electrochemical performance and flexible substrate integration provides a promising strategy for designing flexible and portable platforms for on-site trace estrogen monitoring.

title: Spent battery-derived LiCoO2-modified 3D-printed electrochemical sensors for cellular hydrogen peroxide monitoring
abstract: Electrochemical (bio)sensors fabricated by fused deposition modeling (FDM) represent a versatile and cost-effective platform for customizable analytical devices. However, their performance often requires surface modification strategies that improve electrocatalytic activity while maintaining sustainable fabrication approaches. Here, we introduce a waste-to-sensor strategy based on the upcycling of lithium cobalt oxide (LiCoO 2 , LCO) recovered from spent lithium-ion batteries as an electroactive modifier for FDM 3D-printed carbon-based electrodes. Although spent batteries represent an increasing environmental challenge, their functional components can be repurposed as valuable secondary resources for high-value technological applications. The developed LCO-modified electrodes were investigated for the electrochemical detection of hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ), a key reactive oxygen species (ROS) involved in cellular signaling and oxidative stress-related diseases. LCO modification was optimized and characterized by cyclic voltammetry and chronoamperometry, demonstrating enhanced electrocatalytic performance compared with unmodified electrodes. The optimized sensor exhibited a linear response toward H 2 O 2 detection in DMEM over the 0-2.5 mM concentration range, with a limit of detection of 0.02 mM and a limit of quantification of 0.06 mM, demonstrating analytical performance suitable for monitoring biologically relevant concentrations. The applicability of the platform was demonstrated using C2C12 muscle and HeLa cervical cancer cell models subjected to oxidative stress conditions, with or without glutathione antioxidant treatment. Electrochemical measurements showed consistent trends with the conventional DCFH-DA fluorescence assay, confirming the ability of the sensor to monitor ROS variations associated with oxidative stress and antioxidant protection. Overall, this work demonstrates that battery-derived LCO can be effectively repurposed as a sustainable electrocatalytic modifier for 3D-printed electrochemical sensors, bridging circular economy principles with biomedical sensing technologies. The proposed platform provides a low-cost, customizable, and environmentally conscious approach for future ROS monitoring and point-of-care biosensing applications.

title: A blood–brain barrier-penetrating NIR fluorescent probe enables cross-model optical imaging of H2O2 in three neuroinflammation-related experimental mice models of brain injury
abstract: Background Hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) is a key mediator of oxidative stress in neuroinflammation-related brain injury, yet brain H 2 O 2 imaging remains challenging because of the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and tissue autofluorescence. In addition, most reported probes have been evaluated in only one or a few disease models, limiting cross-model comparison. Here, we developed MH-1, an H 2 O 2 -responsive near-infrared (NIR) fluorescent probe for brain-section optical mapping after systemic administration. Results MH-1 exhibited an approximately 60-fold fluorescence turn-on at 667 nm, enabled H 2 O 2 detection over 0.107-1000 μmol/L, and reached a stable response within approximately 30 min, with high selectivity, interference resistance, pH stability, and low cytotoxicity. Its fluorescence quantum yield increased from 0.72% to 2.45% upon activation. CD31 co-staining confirmed MH-1-associated fluorescence in extravascular brain parenchyma after systemic administration. Ex vivo brain-section imaging further revealed model-dependent H 2 O 2 -associated fluorescence in LPS-induced neonatal neuroinflammation, hypoxic-ischemic encephalopathy (HIE), and Alzheimer's disease (AD), with an effective imaging window of approximately 12 h. Significance Rather than relying on a single best-in-class analytical parameter, MH-1 integrates NIR emission, a large fluorescence turn-on, BBB access, and applicability across three mechanistically distinct brain-injury models. This combined performance enables region-resolved, cross-model comparison of H 2 O 2 -associated oxidative stress in preclinical brain tissue.

title: Multilevel dual-cyclic DNA cascade amplification strategy for cancer cell inhibition and ultrasensitive electrochemical detection
abstract: Background Integrating ultrasensitive biosensing with cellular behavior regulation is crucial for cancer theranostics, yet traditional methods lack sensitivity and spatial precision. Programmable DNA nanodevices enabling simultaneous receptor modulation and signal amplification provide a promising paradigm to address these challenges. Herein, an electrochemical biosensor based on a multilevel dual-cyclic DNA cascade amplification strategy was developed for cancer cell detection and cellular behavior regulation. Results The cell-surface DNA nanodevice comprises aptamers A1 and A2, which specifically recognize MET and CD71 proteins on cancer cell membranes, respectively. In the presence of an initiator strand S1, a cascaded hairpin-mediated strand displacement reaction is triggered on the cell surface, bringing MET and CD71 into close proximity. The spatial restriction blocks the hepatocyte growth factor (HGF)-MET interaction, inhibiting cell migration. Concurrently, the reaction releases H3H4 duplexes into the culture medium. Upon the introduction of hairpin probes functionalized with bimetallic platinum-palladium nanoparticles (PtPd/H6), H3H4 duplexes initiate a secondary strand displacement cycle on the electrode surface. This electrode-confined cascade recruits an amount of PtPd/H6, which exhibits excellent electrocatalytic activity toward H 2 O 2 reduction to amplify the electrochemical signal. The biosensor displays a linear response to cell concentrations ranging from 10 2 to 5 × 10 6 cells/mL, with a limit of detection of 4 cells/mL. Significance The dual functional sensing strategy provides a reliable approach for integrated cellular regulation and electrochemical analysis.

title: A trifluoromethyl-triggered J-aggregation switch for Cu+-Responsive fluorescence imaging and in vivo application in mice
abstract: Herein, we elucidate the structural basis of J-aggregation in our previously reported dual-locked fluorescent probe HBimmCue, a trifluoromethyl-substituted sensor for neuronal mitochondrial Cu + . By designing a methyl-substituted control probe HBimmCH3, we demonstrate that the trifluoromethyl group is the critical moiety triggering J-aggregation in PBS. This aggregation enables HBimmCue to function through a photoinduced electron transfer (PET) + J-aggregation-caused quenching (J-ACQ) dual-quenching mechanism, affording an exceptional 59-fold fluorescence turn-on response. In contrast, HBimmCH3 lacks J-aggregation entirely and exhibits only a 13.2-fold enhancement via single PET quenching. DFT/TD-DFT calculations and electrostatic potential (ESP) analysis further corroborate the PET mechanism, energy-level shifts, and substituent-dependent assembly behaviors. Given its excellent photophysical performance, we further explored the in vivo imaging capability of HBimmCue. This work demonstrates a facile substituent-engineering approach to modulate J-aggregation, which provides valuable insights for the rational design of high-performance activatable fluorescent probes.

title: pH-switched single-assay spectrophotometric determination of xanthine and hypoxanthine based on urate-mediated response modulation
abstract: Enzymatic assays based on oxidase/peroxidase coupling usually assume quantitative conversion of enzymatically generated hydrogen peroxide into the optical product. Here, we show that this assumption fails in the xanthine oxidase-horseradish peroxidase-Amplex Red system because urate, the final product of xanthine and hypoxanthine oxidation, is not a silent product. Urate competes with Amplex Red in the peroxidase cycle, decreasing the apparent yield of resorufin formation; for xanthine, this yield was only 0.40 ± 0.01, independently of pH. A mechanistic mathematical model was developed to relate substrate oxidation, hydrogen peroxide generation, radical reactions, and final absorbance. The model explains the reduced sensitivity observed for xanthine, the different response regimes found for hypoxanthine, and the residual urate concentration after reaction completion. This understanding was then used to design a sequential single-assay spectrophotometric method for the individual determination of xanthine and hypoxanthine, two metabolites that are commonly measured together in enzymatic freshness assays. Xanthine is quantified first at pH 6, where hypoxanthine oxidation is negligible, and hypoxanthine is subsequently determined in the same recording after increasing pH and xanthine oxidase concentration. Application to refrigerated cod extracts gave recoveries of 104 ± 13% for xanthine and 90 ± 12% for hypoxanthine, supporting the feasibility of the approach for freshness-related analysis and highlighting the broader need to consider product-driven effects in oxidase/peroxidase-coupled assays.

title: In situ high-resolution mapping of Cr(VI) in soil using an NFR-functionalized diffusive gradients in thin-films technique
abstract: Background Chromium (Cr) speciation governs its environmental behavior, toxicity, and biogeochemical cycling in soils, especially within the highly dynamic rhizosphere where steep redox gradients prevail. Accurate assessment of Cr(VI) bioavailability and its microscale distribution is essential for risk evaluation and remediation of contaminated sites. However, conventional sampling and laboratory methods often perturb Cr speciation, and few low-disturbance analytical techniques are available for reliable in situ speciation data at relevant spatial resolutions. This leaves a critical gap in our ability to characterize Cr(VI) dynamics in complex soil microenvironments. Results We developed and systematically validated a novel diffusive gradients in thin-films (DGT) technique using an optimized N-methyl-d-glucamine functionalized resin (NFR) for selective Cr(VI) detection. NFR binding gels fabricated with two distinct particle sizes exhibited strong adsorption affinity and rapid uptake kinetics, sequestering >96% of Cr(VI) within 24 h while displaying negligible Cr(III) accumulation. Performance matched theoretical predictions across pH 3.50-9.52 and ionic strengths of 0.1-100 mmol L -1 NaNO 3 . Blank values were below 0.028 μg L -1 and method detection limits under 0.017 μg L -1 for a 1-day deployment. Coupling the 500NFR binding gel with a planar optode enabled simultaneous high-resolution two-dimensional imaging of Cr(VI) and O 2 in the rice rhizosphere, revealing localized Cr(VI) depletion zones within 2.5 mm of the root axis and excellent spatial uniformity (RSD Significance and novelty This work establishes the 500NFR-DGT as a robust and selective platform for high-resolution in situ mapping of Cr(VI), overcoming heterogeneity limitations of conventional DGT binding gels. The integration of NFR with a planar optode enables simultaneous imaging of Cr(VI) and O 2 , providing a powerful tool to elucidate redox-driven Cr dynamics in the rhizosphere and inform remediation strategies for contaminated soils.

title: Photo-controlled CRISPR/Cas12 systems: Molecular design evolution and applications in diagnostics and gene editing- A review
Coordination-induced suppression of non-radiative decay in carbon dots: A novel fluorescent-enhancement sensor for sensitive and selective determination of Al3+ in pharmaceutical samples
abstract: Excessive intake of aluminum ions (Al 3+ ) has been associated with significant health risks. Therefore, the development of simple, accurate, and reliable methods for the determination of aluminum content in pharmaceutical products is critical for drug quality control and patient safety. Herein, we report a novel type of fluorescent carbon dots (Suc-CDs) synthesized from sucrose and anhydrous ethanol via a one-pot solvothermal treatment, and their development into a fluorescent-enhancement sensor for Al 3+ . The highly selective fluorescence enhancement of the Suc-CDs toward Al 3+ is supported by a sensing model dominated by suppression of non-radiative decay, while the available spectroscopic evidence is consistent with contributions from inhibited photoinduced electron transfer and reduced surface defect-state trapping. Under optimized conditions, the sensor exhibits a relatively wide linear range of 5.0-80 μM for Al 3+ with a detection limit as low as 1.49 μM. Furthermore, the sensor was successfully applied to the determination of the active pharmaceutical ingredient in Compound Aluminium Hydroxide Tablets and was evaluated by spike-recovery experiments in Mannitol Injection, with recoveries and precision meeting the acceptance criteria cited in this study. Consequently, this study provides a new strategy for simple, cost-effective, and reliable fluorometric detection of Al 3+ for broader application scenarios.

title: Engineering of a self-feeding and sustainable catalytic hybridization circuit for efficient TK1 mRNA imaging
abstract: DNA amplifiers have shown considerable potential in biomarker imaging, yet their practical application is often constrained by slow reaction kinetics and insufficient amplification efficiency. To address these limitations, we herein report a self-feeding and sustainable catalytic hybridization circuit (SCHC) for efficient intracellular mRNA imaging. By integrating rationally designed palindromic sequences into the catalytic hairpin assembly (CHA) reactants, hairpin monomers are induced to form compact hairpin dimers, thereby promoting an increase in local reactant concentration. Benefiting from the self-feeding and sustainable hybridization mechanism, the hairpin dimer reactants undergo alternating assembly to form directionally aligned DNA nanowires upon activation by the initiator (I), concurrently achieving efficient fluorescence transduction. In comparison to the typical CHA system, this strategy exhibits accelerated response kinetics and enhanced amplification performance. Moreover, leveraging its simplified modular design, we further establish a bridge between the analyte and I by introducing a conversion hairpin module, enabling the monitoring and imaging of TK1 mRNA (T) without substantial modifications. We anticipate that this simple yet effective strategy holds tremendous potential for application in human cancer diagnosis.

title: 4D-printed Cd2+-responsive rolling needle panel meter
abstract: Background Determining cadmium (Cd) is essential for assessing Cd contamination and its toxic effects. Four-dimensional printing (4DP) technologies enable stimuli-induced, time-dependent shape programming of fabricated devices and are transforming fabrication processes and enhancing the geometric functionalities of stimuli-responsive devices. However, analytical approaches that leverage the degree of shape programming of 4D-printed ion-responsive sensing devices for metal ion detection remain limited. 4D-printed portable ion-responsive sensing devices hold great promise for reducing the complexity and cost of reliable on-site metal ion detection. Results We employed a digital light processing 4DP technique with photocurable resins incorporating 2,2'-(ethylenedioxy)diethanethiol (EDT) to fabricate a Cd 2+ -responsive rolling needle comprising EDT-incorporated parallel active fibers and a nonresponsive layer. Pre-treatment of the needle with hydrogen peroxide oxidized the thioether groups in the copolymer, resulting in the formation of sulfoxide and sulfone groups. Due to electrostatic interactions and selective complexation between Cd 2+ ions and these sulfoxide and sulfone groups (dissociation constant: 14.1 nM), the unequal swelling of the EDT-incorporated active fibers induced the [Cd 2+ ]-dependent rolling of the needle. Furthermore, the rolling needle returned to its as-printed state after treatment with a sodium borohydride solution, demonstrating reversible shape programming for repeated Cd 2+ determination. After optimization, the method detection limit was determined to be 0.03 μg L -1 . We validated the reliability and applicability of this method by determining Cd 2+ in reference materials as well as in environmental water, food, and human urine samples. Significance This study is the first to demonstrate a 4D-printed ion-responsive sensing device that incorporated practical geometric functions to enable on-site quantitative analysis of heavy metals. The novelty and significance of this study lie in the pioneering use of 4DP technologies with ion-responsive materials to fabricate a reversible Cd 2+ -responsive sensing device for on-site determination of Cd 2+ based on ion-responsive shape programming, thereby eliminating the need for expensive measurement apparatus and atomic spectrometric methods.

title: Single-nanozyme based hydrogel patch for total antioxidant capacity and pH synchronous visual monitoring
abstract: Simultaneously visual monitoring of diversified indicators in sweat and food is crucial for healthcare and food safety assessment. While nanozymes have been explored for colorimetric detection of various biomarkers in sweat, monitoring different biomarkers with a single nanozyme remains challenging. Herein, a novel strategy for real-time synchronous monitoring of total antioxidant capacity (TAC) and pH value using a single nanozyme decorated hydrogel patch has been demonstrated. Fe 2+ doped calcium peroxide nanoparticles (Fe-CaO 2 ) were encapsulated in a zeolitic imidazolate framework (ZIF) with the modification of Cu 2+ to synthesize a novel nanozyme (FCZC). The characteristic of FCZC for self-generating H 2 O 2 in an acidic environment eliminated the risks associated with the addition of H 2 O 2 externally. FCZC exhibited high peroxidase-like catalytic activity toward the oxidation of 3,3',5,5'-tetramethylbenzidine (TMB) via the Fenton and Fenton-like reactions, with a low Michaelis constant of 0.043 mM. Furthermore, the activity of FCZC exhibited a susceptibility to acidity within a wide pH range. Therefore, based on this, TAC and pH were sensitively detected in the linear ranges of 0.5 μM - 70 μM and 4.0 - 6.8, respectively. A hydrogel patch was constructed by encapsulating FCZC within a sodium alginate hydrogel, enabling synchronous visual detection of TAC and pH in sweat and food samples, which was further integrated with smartphone signaling for in-situ monitoring. The work presented a simple hydrogel sensor enabled the real-time synchronous monitoring of various indicators in sweat and food based on single nanozyme catalysis, facilitating daily health and food safety assessments for the public.

title: An electrochemical sensor platform for rapid nucleic acid detection of Influenza A in unamplified samples and machine-learning-assisted infection diagnosis
abstract: Influenza A remains a major cause of respiratory infection that demands for rapid, accurate and readily accessible diagnostic tools for timely clinical decision-making and outbreak control. Here, we report a smartphone-assisted electrochemical biosensor platform for amplification-free nucleic acid detection of Influenza A based on magnetic beads enriched target capture and methylene blue (MB)-mediated signal transduction. Under optimized conditions, the platform enabled sensitive detection of both synthetic complementary DNA and RNA, with limits of detection of 0.33aM and 3.32aM, respectively, while maintaining high selectivity against mismatched and non-target sequences. Additionally, the platform is also applied to the detection of RNA extracted from nasopharyngeal swab samples and shows superior discrimination ability between positive and negative samples as well as strong correlation with reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) results. Finally, an optimal machine-learning framework based on a support vector classifier (SVC) is developed to analyze DPV signal profiles and directly classify clinical samples without explicit comparison to blank-current responses, achieving an accuracy of 100% in the clinical cohort. Unlike conventional nucleic acid detection approaches that mainly rely on predefined thresholds or quantitative signal interpretation, this study establishes a machine-learning-assisted classification strategy for direct discrimination of influenza A nucleic-acid positive and negative samples based on electrochemical DPV signal profiles. This simple algorithmic framework is particularly suitable for portable devices with resource constrained microcontrollers to realize rapid result analysis. Our results shed a light on potential portable platform for decentralized rapid nucleic acid testing and promising technique for point-of-care infectious disease diagnostics.

title: Decoding in-situ plant stress physiology via bio-hydrogel microneedles
abstract: Electrochemical detection of hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) dynamics enables early monitoring of plant stress physiology, which is crucial for crop health management and yield optimization. However, invasive sensors damage plant tissues, whereas existing non-invasive approaches suffer from cuticular barriers and insufficient exploitation of dynamic biochemical signals, leading to high interfacial impedance, delayed responses, and low accuracy. Here, we introduce an integrated sensing and machine-learning framework (CRH-BMIS) that combines a highly specific Cs/rGO/HRP biohydrogel microneedle with algorithmic analytics. This system overcomes traditional barriers to in situ, tissue-level monitoring of abiotic and Pseudomonas syringae pv. tomato DC3000 (Pst DC3000) stresses. By significantly lowering interfacial impedance, the microneedle exhibits a stable log-linear response over an ultra-broad range (0.01-8000 μM) with exceptional sensitivity (up to 12.46 μA cm -2 decade -1 , LOD 0.00109 μM) and robust anti-interference. Furthermore, utilizing an intelligent diagnostic model based on stress-evoked H 2 O 2 dynamics, CRH-BMIS achieves competitive cross-plant classification of abiotic/biotic stress (96.97% accuracy) and disease-stage classification (91.47% accuracy). This superior performance stems from the deep synergy between minimally invasive microneedles and machine learning algorithms. CRH-BMIS not only delivers accurate, generalizable in situ stress diagnosis but also enables scalable early-warning decision support.

title: A real-time gap ligase chain reaction assay enabling mutation detection and single-tube mutation fraction analysis
abstract: Accurate mutation analysis requires not only highly specific mutant recognition but also reliable mutation fraction analysis. Although gap ligase chain reaction (Gap-LCR) possesses excellent single-base discrimination capability, its integration with real-time fluorescence transduction and direct mutation fraction analysis remains insufficiently explored. Herein, we developed a real-time Gap-LCR platform by coupling Gap-LCR amplification with multicomponent nucleic acid enzyme (MNAzyme)-mediated fluorescence transduction. Using JAK2 V617F as a model target, the proposed assay enabled highly sensitive and specific real-time mutation detection over a concentration range from 10 aM to 100 fM. To enable direct mutation fraction analysis, a reference-locus-assisted dual-locus design was introduced to independently quantify the mutant target and the corresponding reference locus within a single closed-tube reaction. The calculated mutation fractions showed good agreement with predefined values down to 0.05% in synthetic DNA mixtures, and the assay further demonstrated overall agreement with reference NGS results in clinical samples. Overall, this work extends the analytical capability of Gap-LCR from mutation detection to single-tube mutation fraction analysis, providing a practical strategy for quantitative molecular diagnostics.

title: An integrated microfluidic sample-to-answer system for automated detection of common deletional α-thalassemia mutations
abstract: Thalassemia is a prevalent hereditary hematological disorder, and rapid, automated genetic screening is essential for large-scale prevention and control, particularly in primary healthcare settings. To address the limitations of conventional molecular diagnostic methods, we developed an integrated microfluidic sample-to-answer system for simultaneous detection of four common deletional α-thalassemia mutations (-α 3.7 , -α 4.2 , -- SEA , and -- THAI ), together with the HBA2 wild-type locus, enabling accurate discrimination between heterozygous and homozygous deletion genotypes. The system directly uses whole blood without nucleic acid extraction and integrates direct multiplex PCR (dmPCR) with reverse dot blot (RDB) hybridization in a fully closed microfluidic chip, enabling highly automated sample-to-result analysis within 3.5 h while minimizing contamination risk. The RDB-dmPCR assay demonstrated high analytical performance, including a limit of detection of 0.1 μL of whole blood, excellent specificity without cross-reactivity with non-deletional α- or β-thalassemia, strong reproducibility, and robust anti-interference capability. Clinical validation using 97 samples for the RDB-dmPCR assay and an independent cohort of 40 samples for the integrated microfluidic platform achieved 100% sensitivity, 100% specificity, and complete concordance with the reference gap polymerase chain reaction (Gap-PCR) method. By integrating amplification, hybridization, and result interpretation into a single automated workflow, this platform simplifies molecular testing and provides a practical solution for decentralized thalassemia screening in primary healthcare and other resource-limited settings.

title: DFT-guided electronic modulation and interface engineering of nitrogen-rich carbon nitride nanotube arrays for enhanced electrochemical detection of metronidazole
abstract: Developing novel metal-free nanomaterials with high electrocatalytic activity is crucial for the sensitive electrochemical detection of trace metronidazole (MTZ) contaminant. Herein, we report a template-free, supramolecular self-assembly-driven hydrothermal-pyrolysis approach for the high-yield synthesis of nitrogen-rich g-C 3 N 4 nanotube arrays (gCN NTAs). This method affords nanotubes with an average diameter of 376.23 ± 151.18 nm, a nitrogen content of 74.37 at.% by XPS with a synthesis yield of 50.36%. TEM reveals a unique bilayer tubular structure with in-situ coral strip-like nanoarrays, thereby enhancing MTZ detection via aggregation-induced and local electric field effects. The gCN NTAs-based sensor exhibits a concentration-dependent signal-enhancement response toward MTZ, displaying linear ranges of 0.01-100 μM and 200-4000 μM, with correspondingly low limits of detection of 0.0168 and 0.0464 μM, limits of quantification of 0.0561 and 0.1546 μM, and high sensitivities of 0.2571 and 0.0932 μA/μM·cm 2 . In addition, it exhibits excellent selectivity, stability, and recovery rates in real samples. Density functional theory calculations show that N-doping reduces the HOMO-LUMO gap and enhances the local negative electrostatic potential. Adsorption energy and density of states analyses support that the formation of p-π conjugation lowers the reaction energy barrier, improving interfacial electron transfer. Biosafety evaluations validate the low cytotoxicity and high biocompatibility of gCN NTAs, highlighting their outstanding potential for diverse applications.

title: A wearable nanofluidic sensor for determining the sweat nicotine
abstract: The escalating prevalence of electronic cigarettes has intensified public health discourse regarding the implications of nicotine exposure. Consequently, the development of rigorous, non-invasive diagnostic methodologies to evaluate secondhand smoke exposure is imperative. Precise quantification of nicotine levels provides a critical evidence base for designing interventions aimed at smoking cessation and the prophylaxis of smoking-related pathologies. In this study, we introduce a novel biosensing paradigm that leverages the I-V characteristics of asymmetric nanochannel arrays, synergized with the selective enzymatic activity of nicotine oxidase (CYP2B6), for the detection of sweat nicotine. The nanoconfinement effect within these arrays significantly enhances the affinity of CYP2B6 for nicotine, thereby augmenting catalytic efficiency. The developed wearable sensor demonstrates exceptional analytical performance, featuring a bilinear range (0.1 to 9 μM and 10-50 μM) and robust immunity to common sweat-borne interferences, such as glucose and uric acid. Furthermore, the platform exhibits a low limit of detection (0.3 μM) at low nicotine concentration range, underscoring its clinical utility for the sensitive quantification of nicotine exposure. We assessed nicotine levels in human populations, including high smokers, low smokers, secondhand smokers, and non-smokers. The results indicated that a clear increase in nicotine levels correlating with the duration of smoking. Thus, the continuous and personalized wearable sweat nicotine detection sensor based on the proposed detection method can effectively monitor nicotine exposure across a diverse range of populations.

title: The exquisite integration of 1,3,4-thiadiazole and large conjugated group for constructing multi-functional fluorescence probe to detect TNP and Cu2+ in environment, food and living cells
abstract: 2,4,6-Trinitrophenol (TNP) and copper ion (Cu 2+ ), as widely used industrial materials, poses potential threat to ecological environment and food safety. Thus, 2-(2-hydroxyphenyl)-1,3,4-thiadiazole was utilized as bi-functional skeleton and three fluorescent probes XL, XD and XS for dual detection of TNP and Cu 2+ were synthesized. The influence of introducing carbazole, triphenylamine and tetraphenylethylene as chromophore and auxiliary on their fluorescence properties, recognition performance and detection mechanism was explored by systematically experimental study and DFT calculations. Ideally, XL showed the best potentiality as multifunctional fluorescence probe with a rapid response and high sensitivity (LODs of 0.16 μM for TNP and 0.26 μM for Cu 2+ ). More importantly, many methods including UV-vis spectral responses, pH control, EDTA masking agent and differences in response kinetics could be used to separate TNP and Cu 2+ . Furthermore, it was successfully applied to the detection in water, soil, plant foods and alcoholic drinks, supported on-site visual analysis via test strips and smartphones, and was applicable to Cu 2+ imaging in living cells. This strategy provided a technical pathway for rapid screening and field analysis of both TNP and Cu 2+ in real samples.

title: Magnetic enrichment-assisted fluorescent lateral flow aptasensor using dual-functional silica magnetic nanoprobes for detection of aflatoxin M1 in milk
abstract: Background Aflatoxin M 1 (AFM 1 ) contamination in milk poses a significant food safety concern, necessitating sensitive and practical methods for dairy safety monitoring. Herein, a magnetic enrichment-assisted fluorescent lateral flow aptasensor was developed using dual-functional fluorescent silica-magnetic nanoprobes (FSMN-Apt) for AFM 1 detection. The FSMN-Apt probes integrate multicore Fe 3 O 4 nanoparticles for magnetic enrichment, a rhodamine B-doped silica shell for fluorescence signaling, and surface-conjugated AFM 1 aptamers for selective target recognition. The proposed platform addresses the need for rapid and reliable AFM 1 screening in complex dairy matrices. Results The FSMN-Apt fluorescent LFA combined magnetic separation, aptamer-based recognition, and ratiometric fluorescence analysis within a competitive lateral flow format. Under optimized conditions, the assay exhibited a linear detection range of 0.01-50 ng/mL and a limit of detection of 0.21 ng/mL. Increasing AFM 1 concentrations produced a concentration-dependent decrease in the test-to-control fluorescence ratio (F T /F C ). The assay showed high selectivity toward AFM 1 over structurally related mycotoxins and demonstrated good reproducibility. Recovery studies in spiked milk samples yielded 96.1-104.2% with satisfactory precision. Furthermore, the results obtained using the proposed LFA were in good agreement with those obtained by ELISA and HPLC, supporting its analytical reliability in milk matrices. Significance and novelty This study demonstrates a dual-functional silica-magnetic nanoprobe strategy that integrates magnetic enrichment and fluorescence signaling within a competitive lateral flow aptasensor, simplifying the analytical workflow while enabling quantitative ratiometric detection. The combination of magnetic pre-enrichment, selective aptamer recognition, and portable fluorescence readout provides a practical platform for AFM 1 screening and offers a versatile design strategy for nanoprobe-based detection of other food contaminants.

title: Conductive Cu-MOF synergizing with enzyme-free catalytic cascade amplification for ultrasensitive electrochemical detection of miRNA-21
abstract: Background MicroRNA-21 (miRNA-21) is an oncogenic biomarker overexpressed in various early-stage tumors, making its accurate detection vital for diagnosis. However, its concentration in clinical samples is extremely low, posing a significant analytical challenge. Conventional electrochemical sensors often rely on exogenous enzymes for amplification, which suffer from high cost, instability, and complex immobilization procedures. Moreover, the poor conductivity of common electrode materials limits signal transduction efficiency. Therefore, developing an enzyme-free sensing platform with a highly conductive interface that enables robust signal amplification remains an urgent unmet need for trace miR-21 quantification. Results In this work, a laser-induced graphene (LIG) electrode modified with conductive Cu-MOF is developed to mediate an enzyme-free cascade toehold-mediated strand displacement reaction (CTSDR). When miRNA-21 is recognized, the CTSDR is successfully initiated to form numerous G-quadruplexes (G4), which subsequently bind hemin to create a peroxidase-like G4/hemin complex. This complex efficiently catalyzes the hydroquinone (HQ)/H 2 O 2 redox system, generating a significantly amplified current. The sensor delivers a wide linear range from 10 1 to 10 7 fM, with a detection limit reaching down to 1.94 fM. It also demonstrates outstanding selectivity, readily discriminating single-base mismatched sequences, and good reproducibility. Importantly, this strategy successfully detects miRNA-21 in thyroid cancer cell lines and clinical patient serum samples, proving its excellent practical viability. Significance and novelty This work is novel in synergistically integrating a conductive LIG electrode enhanced with Cu-MOF and an enzyme-free catalytic cascade amplification for the first time, and in revealing that CTSDR-generated fuel strands undergo a previously unreported transition to G4 structures induced by K + , enabling ultrasensitive miRNA-21 detection without external enzymes or intricate labeling. Given its facile Cu-MOF synthesis, straightforward electrode modification, and excellent clinical concordance, this strategy provides a highly accessible, affordable, and reliable tool for early tumor diagnostics and routine point-of-care biomarker screening.

title: Quantitative analysis of heavy metals in ores by X-ray fluorescence with improved CARS and support vector regression using ACOR optimization algorithm
abstract: X-ray fluorescence (XRF) spectrometry is widely applied for the quantitative determination of elemental concentrations in ores due to its rapid, non-destructive, and multi-element analytical capabilities. However, the high dimensionality, spectral redundancy, and strong matrix-dependent nonlinear effects inherent in XRF spectra often limit the predictive accuracy and robustness of conventional quantitative models. Therefore, the effective selection of informative spectral variables and the construction of reliable regression models remain critical challenges for accurate ore analysis. In this study, an integrated quantitative framework combining adaptive heuristic optimization and machine-learning regression is proposed to improve elemental concentration prediction from ore XRF spectra. First, a competitive adaptive reweighted sampling (CARS) strategy optimized by the ant colony optimization for continuous domains (ACOR) algorithm is employed to perform robust spectral variable selection. This process removes redundant noisy spectral information while preserving chemically relevant features. Subsequently, an ACOR-optimized support vector regression (ACOR-SVR) model is developed for quantitative analysis. In this model, key SVR hyperparameters are automatically tuned to enhance nonlinear modelling capability and improve generalization performance. The proposed ACSVR framework is evaluated on multi-element ore datasets involving Fe, Cu, Zn, and Pb. The experimental results demonstrate that ACOR-CARS provides more stable and compact feature subsets than conventional CARS, whereas ACOR-SVR consistently outperforms baseline SVR and other classical machine-learning models. High prediction accuracy is achieved for Fe, Cu, Zn, and Pb, with coefficients of determination (R 2 ) reaching 0.9940, 0.9984, 0.9968, and 0.9995, respectively. These results confirm the effectiveness of integrating optimized variable selection with nonlinear regression modelling for XRF-based quantitative analyses. Overall, this study provides a practical and efficient strategy for high-precision elemental quantification in ores, offering strong potential for mineral exploration, resource evaluation and intelligent geochemical analysis.

title: From nature to nanodots: Green microwave-synthesized S,N-self-doped carbon quantum dots for smart fluorescent sensing of indomethacin in pharmaceuticals and spiked human plasma
abstract: A green, innovative and cost-efficient switch-off fluorescent sensor was established for detecting the non-fluorescent anti-inflammatory drug indomethacin (IND) utilizing N,S-co-doped carbon quantum dots (N,S-CQDs) from onion and green pepper as a renewable green carbon source. A highly efficient green synthesis was conducted using a household microwave in only 5 min, underscoring its exceptional speed and effectiveness. Comprehensive physicochemical characterization unequivocally verified the intrinsic nitrogen and sulfur self-doping of the biomass-derived quantum dots. The proposed assay exhibited a remarkable linearity across the concentration interval of 1.0-30.0 μg/mL, with a correlation coefficient above 0.999 and a detection limit as low as 0.24 μg/mL at λex/λem of 340/420 nm. The probe exhibited exceptional selectivity even in the presence of simultaneously administered medicines, possible interferents, and different metal ions. It was proficiently employed for the analysis of IND in both pharmaceutical capsules and human plasma samples. Furthermore, the proposed method exhibited excellent environmental sustainability, as evidenced by favorable AGREE (0.75), Complex GAPI, BAGI (75), and RGB12 (98.6) assessments, confirming its low environmental impact, high practical applicability, and excellent overall sustainability.

title: One-step fabrication of a smart hydrogel without external energy input for integrated health monitoring and externally triggered drug delivery
abstract: Hydrogels exhibit immense potential in wearable health monitoring owing to their exceptional biocompatibility and tissue-like flexibility. However, the rapid, energy-efficient fabrication of structurally homogeneous, multifunctional hydrogel networks remains a formidable challenge. Herein, we report an ultrafast, one-step synthetic strategy to fabricate a self-healing Fe-MXene-polyacrylic acid (PAA) hydrogel within merely 2 min. The hydrogel was incorporated into an integrated health-monitoring platform combining electrochemical sweat analysis, flexible pulse monitoring, and drug delivery. The sweat sensors exhibited sensitivities of 54.4 mV decade -1 for K + and 55.2 mV decade -1 for Na + , approaching the theoretical Nernstian response for monovalent ions. In contrast, the pH sensor displayed a sub-Nernstian sensitivity of 30.4 mV/pH. Concurrently, benefiting from broad-range strain sensitivity (up to 1900%), a high maximum gauge factor (GF = 7.8), and robust tissue adhesion (24 kPa on porcine skin), the system enables high-fidelity dynamic capture of subtle physiological signals, such as arterial pulses. Furthermore, dynamic coordination between Fe 3+ ions and carboxylate groups (-COOH) imparts structural reversibility to the hydrogel network. In the proof-of-concept experiment, the addition of 0.1 wt% citric acid disrupted the Fe 3+ -carboxylate coordination through competitive chelation, thereby facilitating the diffusion-mediated release of paeonol from the hydrogel. Moreover, the use of a low-cost paper-based substrate enhances the environmental friendliness of the device. Upon immersion in water at room temperature, its main structure undergoes water-induced disintegration within 4 h as a result of water absorption, swelling, and progressive structural destabilization. In summary, this simple, rapid, eco-friendly, and multifunctionally integrated hydrogel platform provides a novel paradigm for developing next-generation personalized closed-loop theranostic wearables and green bioelectronics.

title: A benzotriazole-based fluorescent probe with arylboronate recognition for rapid and selective hypochlorite detection in environmental and biological systems
abstract: Hypochlorite (ClO - ), a biologically and environmentally relevant reactive oxygen species, plays a key role in inflammatory processes and water quality regulation. In this work, a benzotriazole-based fluorescent probe (DTPB) was developed for the sensitive detection of ClO - , employing a pinacol boronate ester as the recognition moiety. Upon reaction with ClO - , the arylboronate group undergoes oxidative hydrolysis to generate the corresponding phenolic product (DTPH - ), accompanied by a marked fluorescence quenching at 524 nm. The structural transformation was verified by 1 H NMR and high-resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS), while theoretical calculations further elucidated the underlying electronic transition and sensing mechanism. Under physiological conditions (10 mM PBS, pH 7.4), DTPB exhibited excellent photostability, a rapid response within 60 s, a low detection limit of 60 nM, and high selectivity toward ClO - over other reactive species and common ions. The proposed method was successfully applied to the determination of ClO - in various real water samples, showing satisfactory recoveries and low relative standard deviations. In addition, due to its low cytotoxicity and stable optical response, DTPB enabled fluorescence imaging of intracellular ClO - in A549 cells. These results demonstrate that this probe provides a reliable fluorescence-based analytical platform for monitoring hypochlorite in environmental and biological systems, with potential applications in redox-related studies and water safety assessment.

title: Comprehensive gas and electrolyte analysis in aged automotive lithium-ion cells cycled in various voltage windows
abstract: BACKGROUND: Increasing the range of battery electric vehicles is of significant interest in the automotive industry. Enhancing the voltage window in which the lithium-ion cell is operating directly affects the driving range of the vehicle but can reduce the cell lifetime. The electrolyte and associated degradation reactions have a significant impact on this parameter. To understand lithium-ion cell aging mechanisms comprehensive electrolyte analysis methods are required. RESULTS: A new approach for the gas analysis in industrially produced cells is presented, allowing the identification of the gas amount within the cell and the quantification of the gas composition. By applying this method a comprehensive gas and liquid phase analysis of the electrolyte in large-format automotive cells can be performed to gain insights in the electrolyte degradation process. In a next step the method is applied to perform an electrolyte analysis of lithium-ion cells after long-term cycling. Different cut-off voltages are analyzed to investigate the effect of the voltage window on long-term cycling stability of the electrolyte and identify degradation reactions leading towards capacity loss of the cell. SIGNIFICANCE: A comprehensive analysis of the gas and liquid phase can be performed to gain further understanding in the electrolyte degradation process. Identifying the suitable voltage window for cycling lithium-ion cells is essential for the development of long lasting battery packs for vehicles with a wide electrical range.

title: Peripheral hydrophilic molecular engineering of porphyrin luminophores for enhanced aqueous electrochemiluminescence and environmental sensing
abstract: Porphyrins are attractive electrochemiluminescence (ECL) luminophores, yet their poor aqueous compatibility and aggregation-caused quenching (ACQ) limit their application in aqueous solution. Herein, a peripheral molecular engineering strategy was developed to enhance the aqueous ECL properties of tetraphenylporphyrin (TPP). Glucose (Glu) and tryptophan (Trp) were separately introduced onto the meso-positions of TPP, affording two asymmetric porphyrin derivatives, TPP-Glu and TPP-Trp. Peripheral functionalization improved aqueous compatibility and suppressed intermolecular π-π stacking, thereby reducing ACQ and enhancing both photoluminescence and ECL emission. Among the derivatives, TPP-Trp exhibited the highest ECL performance in the K 2 S 2 O 8 coreactant system, with a relative ECL efficiency of 5.29 times that of TPP. The enhanced ECL response was further exploited for Mercury (Hg 2+ ) sensing through the intrinsic coordination capability of the porphyrin core and the Trp moiety. The resulting ECL sensor enabled sensitive Hg 2+ detection in the linear range of 0.03-60 nM, with a detection limit of 0.01 nM. This work demonstrates that peripheral hydrophilic functionalization suppresses aggregation and enhances aqueous ECL. The approach a versatile design for porphyrin-based ECL luminophores and sensing platforms.

title: Hydrogel bead-based 3D multiplex platform for high precision and high throughput quantification of mTORC1-4E-BP1/2-dependent translation
abstract: BACKGROUND: Quantifying protein phosphorylations and interactions across signaling networks is essential for quantitative biology and systems medicine. Current standard methods like immunoblotting offer limited throughput, precision, and scalability. We present an inverse-precision multiplex workflow based on a 3D hydrogel platform, enabling quantification of protein modifications and interactions within one assay. We chose the example of the mTORC1 (mTOR complex 1) kinase - 4E-BP1/2 signaling axis, clinically targeted by cancer therapies, which tunes protein biosynthesis to nutrient supply and stress. RESULTS: We developed an inverse-precision design combining two orthogonal readouts, 4E-BP1/2 phosphorylation and eIF4E interaction. The design relies on two assays with inverse responses to mTORC1-dependent translation, offering inverse precision. Their combined analysis enhances the assay's robustness and dynamic range (LoD = 9% mTORC1 activity versus LoD = 15% for single readouts). Compared to conventional assays, 3D multiplexing increases precision by > fivefold (CV<4% versus 21% for immunoblotting around LoD), reduces sample consumption by 16-fold (7.8 μg protein input versus 125 μg in 2D format) and time effort by ≥ 80%, while offering a high degree of parallelization. SIGNIFICANCE: Our workflow is compatible with small sample sizes, multiple technical and biological replicates, high-density dose-response curves and time-course data. We validated the assay for different physiological and experimental settings in cell culture and brain tissue. Standard microscopy equipment avoiding the need of specialized infrastructure, and assembly of custom antibody panels without dependence on fixed commercial kits present further advantages over established closed-panel systems. Its scalability, time-efficiency, and high precision make our platform a powerful tool for systems biology and precision medicine.

title: Universal-labeled recombinase polymerase amplification coupled with lateral flow assay for simultaneous detection of Acinetobacter baumannii and its resistance gene
abstract: Acinetobacter baumannii is a WHO critical-priority pathogen whose clinical threat is dramatically exacerbated by carbapenem-resistant strains (CRAB) harboring bla OXA-23. Simultaneous identification of this pathogen and its resistance determinant under field conditions remains an unmet clinical need. Here we report a universal-labeled recombinase polymerase amplification coupled with lateral flow assay (UL-RALA) for simultaneous, sensitive detection of A. baumannii (recA) and its resistance gene bla OXA-23 from clinical sputum. Chimeric tailed primers enable a single universal labeled primer-probe set to amplify both targets, eliminating target-specific probes and suppressing cross-reactivity. Streptavidin-conjugated quantum dot nano-labels deliver independent FAM/recA and DIG/bla OXA-23 fluorescent readouts without signal crosstalk. Under optimized conditions, the platform achieves a limit of detection of 1 copy/μL for both target nucleic acids within 15 min. The outcomes of the clinical validation serve as a strong proof-of-concept for our proposed platform. This modular, platform provides a promising platform for rapid dual-profiling of CRAB infections at the point of care. The modular architecture and encoding-free probe strategy of this UL-RALA methodology It could also provide a highly adaptable, and scalable blueprint for the rapid, on-site diagnostic screening of other emerging infectious pathogens and their associated antimicrobial resistance profiles.

title: Engineering tunable rigid slits and supramolecular soft pockets on silica surfaces for multi-mode chromatographic recognition
abstract: Developing advanced chromatographic interfaces capable of discriminatively recognizing rigid structural isomers and highly polar environmental toxins remains a profound challenge. Herein, we report a systematic "structure-dictates-assembly" paradigm to engineer multi-mode polycyclic aromatic stationary phases with precisely controlled surface micro-topographies. Employing a dihydrazide-anchored thiol-ene click strategy on silica micro-particles, three distinct supramolecular architectures were fabricated: a highly aligned 2-phenanthrenyl phase (2-PNTHZD), a tilted angular 9-phenanthrenyl phase (9-PNTHZD), and a flat-oriented 9-anthracenyl phase (9-ANTHZD). Thermodynamic profiles and solvent-modulated responsive behaviors were comprehensively elucidated using diverse stereochemical and electronic probe matrices. The results reveal three divergent molecular recognition mechanisms. The 2-PNTHZD phase constructs high-density, liquid-crystal-like vertical rigid slits, achieving ultimate length-to-width ratio screening that perfectly segregates challenging tetracene and picene isomers. Conversely, the 9-PNTHZD creates a spatially tilted angular pocket for bent isomers, which remarkably transitions into a highly flexible supramolecular "soft pocket" via active acetonitrile intercalation. This solvent-driven induced-fit mechanism provides a distinct departure from classical reversed-phase thermodynamics, unlocking the baseline resolution of heavily twisted polybrominated biphenyl (PBB) congeners. Furthermore, free from lateral steric hindrance, the wide-open 9-ANTHZD functions as an exceptional π-electron donor surface, leveraging its high HOMO energy to conquer electron-deficient perfluorocarbons and deliver peak-capacity breakthroughs for EPA 529 nitro-explosives. Collectively, this work introduces a highly tunable, multi-mode surface platform, providing a fundamentally predictable toolkit for complex environmental and structural isomer analysis.

title: De novo development strategy for a robust immunocapture-LC-MS/MS assay to quantify soluble fibrinogen-like protein 1 (FGL1) as a potential clinical biomarker for immunotherapy drug development
abstract: De novo development of immunocapture-LC-MS/MS assays to quantify low-abundance protein biomarkers remains challenging due to requirements for high sensitivity, specificity, and robustness. Assay development is often complicated by uncertainties associated with post-translational modifications (PTMs), surrogate peptide selection, antibody performance, and unknown endogenous concentration ranges. To address these challenges, we developed a systematic, four-stage de novo development strategy consisting of: (1) in silico digestion to identify surrogate peptide candidates; (2) optimization of LC-MS/MS conditions and enzymatic digestion conditions; (3) confirmation of antibody performance against endogenous proteins; and (4) evaluation of endogenous protein concentrations. With this strategy, we developed, to our knowledge, the first immunocapture-LC-MS/MS assay to quantify total soluble fibrinogen-like protein 1 (FGL1) in human serum, a major ligand of lymphocyte activation gene-3 (LAG-3) involved in T-cell suppression. The assay utilized IRPNDFIPNVI as the surrogate peptide and mouse serum as the surrogate matrix. After immunocapture enrichment with an anti-FGL1 antibody, the surrogate peptide and internal standard (IS) were separated by reversed-phase UHPLC and detected on a SCIEX Triple Quad 6500+ system using MRM transitions of m/z 649.4 → 856.5 for IRPNDFIPNVI peptide and m/z 652.4 → 856.5 for IRPNDFIPN{VAL( 13 C 5 , 15 N)}I as the internal standard. The assay achieved a calibration range of 10-1000 ng/mL with sufficient sensitivity to enable quantification of FGL1 in serum samples collected from cancer patients. Fit-for-purpose validation using analytical and endogenous quality control samples showed intra-assay precision ≤7.4% CV and inter-assay precision ≤5.2% CV. This assay has been successfully applied in clinical studies to support evaluation of FGL1 as a potential clinical biomarker for immunotherapy drug development.

title: “Apple tree”-like AuNPs@enzyme microreactor: A reusable microfluidic paper-based analytical device for improved acetylcholinesterase inhibitors screening
abstract: Background Acetylcholinesterase (AChE) inhibitors are key therapeutic agents for neurological disorders such as Alzheimer's disease, yet conventional screening of natural product inhibitors are often time-consuming, instrument-dependent, and limited in reusability. To address this, we developed a simple, colorimetric platform based on a reusable microfluidic paper-based analytical device integrated with Au nanoparticle (AuNPs)-mediated enzyme microreactors, coupled with smartphone-based RGB values (blue (B), green (G), and red (R) channel) analysis for rapid and on-site screening of AChE inhibitors from natural products. The microreactors feature an "apple tree"-like architecture, in which AuNPs serve as the "fruits" enabling high-density oriented enzyme immobilization, enhanced substrate accessibility, and excellent reusability. Results AChE was oriented immobilized on concanavalin A-modified AuNPs surface via affinity self-assembly, achieving an 8.6-fold increase in enzyme loading compared to direct adsorption. The immobilized enzyme retained 87.0% of its initial activity after 80 consecutive assays, demonstrating excellent reusability and stability. The method showed superior repeatability with intraday, interday, and batch-to-batch relative standard deviations (RSD) of the colorimetric readouts all below 1.0%. The system enabled visual, quantitative evaluation during bioassay-guided fractionation, substantially reducing unnecessary separation steps. Moreover, half-maximal inhibitory concentration (IC 50 ) values of seven compounds from natural products were determined, correlating well with the reference UV method, confirming the reliability for practical inhibitor screening. Significance This platform offers a cost-effective, reusable, and user-friendly tool for early-stage screening of AChE inhibitors in natural extracts, with potential to accelerate the discovery of lead compounds for neurodegenerative disease therapy while minimizing resource consumption and analytical workload.

title: SERS ratiometric strategy leveraging carbon allocation trade-off enables Tremella fuciformis metabolic phenotyping and traceability
abstract: Background Accurate metabolic phenotyping and geographical traceability of gelatinous fungi are critical for uncovering fungal physiological adaptation mechanisms and advancing edible fungus quality supervision. However, high phenotypic similarity and subtle metabolic differences in homologous fungal samples pose formidable challenges to conventional physicochemical assays. Especially, relying on chemical fingerprinting without biological phenotypic implications, conventional surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) analysis is unable to discern delicate metabolic discrepancies in fungal samples. Results Herein, we propose a metabolic characteristic peak ratio-based SERS strategy using Tremella fuciformis (T. fuciformis) as the model. By extracting intrinsic metabolic signatures represented by the carbon allocation trade-off between stress-resistant functional polysaccharides and storage-type carbohydrates, it delivers metabolic specificity and detection stability/reproducibility that are not possible with traditional fingerprint-based SERS fungal analysis. Integrated with machine learning, this method accurately differentiates six T. fuciformis samples, including specimens with distinct metabolic phenotypes as well as geographically differentiated samples with highly similar phenotypic features, achieving a superior accuracy of 99.2% and an AUC of 1.0. Combined with a custom-built portable Raman device we constructed, the entire detection procedure can be completed within 15 min, enabling efficient on-site analysis. Significance and novelty This study establishes a bio-signature-oriented SERS paradigm that upgrades chemical fingerprint identification to fungal metabolic phenotyping, providing a versatile technical platform for exploring fungal metabolic variation and phenotypic differentiation.

title: A fluorescent optical platform sensor based on ratiometric carbon dots integrated with machine learning for the identification and detection of organic solvents
abstract: Rapid identification of organic solvents is of great significance for chemical analysis, environmental monitoring and laboratory safety. In this study, ratiometric carbon dots (R-CDs) were integrated with machine learning to develop a portable fluorescence-based optical sensing platform for the rapid discrimination and recognition of common organic solvents. Based on the highly sensitive solvatochromic response of R-CDs fluorescence intensity ratio (I 590nm /I 502nm ), a six-channel sensor array was constructed by preparing water/organic-solvent mixtures with different solvent fractions. And owing to the distinct fluorescence responses of R-CDs in solvents with different Relative Polarity (E T N ) values, principal component analysis (PCA), hierarchical cluster analysis (HCA) and linear discriminant analysis (LDA) were employed to discriminate and identify five organic solvents with E T N values ranging from 0.355 to 0.762. Specifically, PCA and HCA were used for label-free analysis of the fluorescence signals, while LDA was employed for model training and prediction. Furthermore, by combining the optical sensing platform with self-developed computer software, a multifunctional system capable of solvent detection, recognition, and result visualization was established. The results showed that five organic solvents could be successfully distinguished with an identification accuracy of 100%, demonstrating the promising potential of the proposed optical sensing platform for organic solvent recognition.

title: Adhesive-free fabrication of covalent organic polymer aerogel coatings for solid-phase microextraction of phenolic compounds
abstract: Background Covalent organic polymer (COP) aerogels, with their hierarchical porous architecture enabling rapid mass transfer and exposing abundant accessible binding sites, hold significant potential as advanced extraction materials for sample pretreatment. Although extensive efforts have been devoted to developing COP aerogels, their direct application as solid-phase microextraction (SPME) coating materials remains unexplored. Results This study introduces a rapid, straightforward, and adhesive-free method for synthesizing COP aerogel-based SPME coatings. Utilizing capillary tubes as confined growth molds, the COP precursor rapidly gels and firmly adheres to the surface of stainless steel wires, forming a monolithic coating. The coating thickness can be customized by simply employing capillary tubes with different internal diameters. When coupled with gas chromatography-mass spectrometry, a highly sensitive method for phenolic compound analysis was developed. The developed method exhibits a broad linear range (2.0-10000 ng L -1 ; R 2 > 0.9911), low detection limits (0.13-0.58 ng L -1 ), and high enrichment factors (4957-22037). Furthermore, the practical applicability was validated through the successful quantification of trace phenolic compounds in grapes, pears and apples, achieving satisfactory recoveries of 89.2-109% with relative standard deviations of 0.35-11.1%. Significance and novelty This study provides a rapid and straightforward approach to synthesizing customizable COP aerogel-based SPME coatings, providing a scale pathway to high-performance extraction media. The established analytical method enables ultrasensitive quantification of trace phenolic contaminants in real fruit matrices, offering a reliable analytical methodology for trace contaminant analysis in food and environmental samples.

title: Coupling of in-tube SPME and SERS for ultrafast screening of hydrophobic pollutants in aqueous matrices
abstract: Background Given the persistence, bioaccumulation, and toxicity of hydrophobic pollutants (HPs), rapid and reliable screening methods are critically needed. Herein, we propose an integrated approach coupling surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) with in-tube solid-phase microextraction (in-tube SPME) for the rapid screening of HPs. The device integrates a dual-functional substrate (tert-dodecylthiol-modified silver nanostructures) within a quartz capillary and a syringe pump for flow control. During analysis, sample solutions are pumped through the capillary, enabling rapid HP adsorption onto the substrate via hydrophobic interactions under continuous flow. Results This dynamic configuration enhances mass transfer efficiency, facilitating rapid SERS detection with a portable Raman spectrometer. The entire "sampling and detection" workflow of the in-tube SPME-SERS method can be completed within 3 min. This method exhibits a good linear relationship (R 2 = 0.997) for the quantitative determination of Sudan III over the concentration range of 5-100 nM, with a limit of detection (LOD) as low as 0.658 nM, demonstrating outstanding sensitivity. Furthermore, the method shows satisfactory performance in terms of spatial homogeneity, batch-to-batch reproducibility, and long-term stability. Significance By balancing speed and accuracy in environmental HP analysis, this work provides a robust framework for portable screening platforms with significant potential for ecological monitoring and exposome research.

title: An antifouling biosensor based on superhydrophilic materials for carcinoembryonic antigen detection in complex human serum
abstract: Inspired by natural micro-nano structures, this work develops a novel antifouling electrochemical biosensor based on hierarchical micro-nano materials with superhydrophilic property for highly sensitive and reliable detection of carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) in complex human serum. This superhydrophilic electrode surface features a hierarchical micro-nano architecture of AuNPs/Cu-MOFs/Cu(OH) 2 and antifouling peptides, significantly enhancing the electrode surface's roughness and hydrophilicity, endowing the electrode surface with exceptional resistance to nonspecific adsorption of biomacromolecules in serum. The aptamer-modified micro-nanostructured electrode is built as the biosensor, enabling efficient access of target CEA molecules to the electrode surface and generating electrochemical signals with favorable sensitivity and reliability. This biosensor demonstrates superior sensing performances with the detection concentration ranging from 1 pg/mL to 0.01 μg/mL and a limit of detection (LOD) as low as 0.34 pg/mL. Moreover, the analytical results from human serum samples are consistent with those obtained via enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) method, confirming the sensor's accuracy and reliability. This work provides a promising strategy for designing antifouling sensor with enhanced applicability in clinical diagnostics and biomarker analysis.

title: Deep eutectic solvent extraction as a route to a ready-to-use natural reagent for automated in-syringe aluminium analysis
abstract: Background Plant extracts provide renewable complexing ligands, but their analytical use is constrained by variable composition and poor compatibility with automated systems. This study investigated whether deep eutectic solvent (DES) extraction can function as a reagent-generation step, yielding a stable extract for direct automated analysis without ligand isolation or solvent exchange. Results A hydrated choline chloride:propylene glycol DES (1:3, mol/mol; 30 wt% water) maximized both recovery of Rubia tinctorum anthraquinones and the Al(III)-dependent absorbance. HPLC-UV and HPLC-MS supported the tentative identification of lucidin primeveroside and ruberythric acid, while molecular dynamics simulations indicated stabilization by propylene glycol and close-range Al(III) association with oxygen donor atoms. The extract was integrated into an automated in-syringe procedure using 100 μL of extract and measurement at 550 nm in a 50 mm cell. The response was linear at 0.10-0.80 mg L -1 (R 2 = 0.997); detection and quantification limits were 0.03 and 0.10 mg L -1 . Repeatability and intermediate precision were ≤4% and ≤5%, while batch-to-batch error and 30-day response variation remained within ±5%. Results for cocoa products and powdered milk agreed with ICP-OES; certified reference material bias was 3.7%. Significance DES extraction becomes an analytical reagent-production step directly compatible with automation. The design links ligand recovery, molecular characterization, storage, and low-volume measurement, providing a transferable strategy for automated assays based on multicomponent renewable reagents.

title: Multimodal microscopic imaging combining dual branch structure-component decoupled fusion for breast tumor image analysis and label-free intelligent diagnosis
abstract: Rapid and accurate analysis of breast tissue is essential for pathological studies and surgical decision support, whereas conventional frozen section pathology relies on time-consuming staining and subjective interpretation, limiting efficiency. This study introduced a multimodal fusion strategy that simultaneously integrates four complementary imaging modalities, including bright-field, phase-contrast, green fluorescence, and blue fluorescence imaging, to comprehensively capture tissue morphology, structural and molecular features. Further, a dual-branch structure-component decoupling network was designed to separately model structural and compositional information while allowing cross-branch interaction. An input-level spatial modality fusion module (SMF) was used to adaptively fuse paired modalities, while a contribution estimation module quantified structural, compositional, and coupling contributions to enable interpretable classification. The network achieved a three-class accuracy of 92.51% and an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.9852, outperforming dual-modality and tri-modality combinations. The four-modality fusion efficiently integrated structural and molecular features, enabling comprehensive tissue feature representation, and improved classification performance. This approach demonstrated that combining structural and compositional information via dual-branch decoupling and multimodal fusion allowed rapid, accurate, and interpretable tissue classification. It provided a reliable tool for tissue feature analysis and pathological assessment and shows strong potential for clinical applications.
