title: A KIT-6 mesoporous silica nanoparticle-based chemiluminescent aptasensor for sensitive detection of 8-Oxo-dG
abstract: Background Excessive accumulation of reactive oxygen species disrupts repair mechanisms and causes irreversible damage to lipids, proteins, and DNA. A target-responsive chemiluminescence sensor was developed for the sensitive detection of 8-OxodG, an important biomarker of oxidative DNA damage. Results In this chemiluminescence sensor, acridinium ester (AE) was loaded into KIT-6 mesoporous silica nanoparticles and capping the pores with an 8-oxodG-specific aptamer. In the presence of 8-oxodG, target-aptamer recognition induced aptamer detachment and AE release. The released AE reacted with H 2 O 2 to generate a concentration-dependent chemiluminescence signal. Under optimized conditions, the sensor exhibited a response range of 0.01-100 μM and a detection limit of 4.8 nM in PBS, by achieving a satisfactory recovery rate of 70.4-108.9% with RSD of 12.7-20.0%. The sensor also showed good selectivity and was successfully evaluated in spiked artificial urine with detection limit of 22.03 nM. Significance The combination of aptamer-controlled molecular gating, the interconnected pore structure of KIT-6, and chemiluminescent signal generation provides a sensitive controlled-release platform for 8-oxodG detection and supports its further development for biological-sample analysis.

title: Logic-gated in situ assembly of membrane-anchored G-quadruplex potassium channels for cancer cell apoptosis
abstract: Background Precise recognition of the tumor microenvironment (TME) coupled with selective activation of therapeutic functions remains a major challenge in precision medicine. To address this, we present a fusogenic liposome-anchored DNA nanodevice that performs an AND logic operation in response to ATP and acidic pH and undergoes in situ assembly on the plasma membrane. Results The nanodevice comprises two transmembrane DNA strands (S1 and S2) containing pH-responsive i-motif switches and split G-quadruplex segments that are sequestered by ATP-binding aptamers. Upon fusion with the cell membrane, TME-specific stimuli trigger the structural reconfiguration of the nanodevice. Acidic conditions induce i-motif folding, bringing the two strands into proximity, while ATP binding displaces the aptamer locks. Under acidic and ATP-rich conditions, aptamer release and i-motif folding jointly promote membrane-localized assembly of a G-quadruplex structure. The nanodevice showed a ratiometric fluorescence response to pH and ATP, including a linear ATP response from 0.2 to 1.0 mM with a detection limit of 0.097 mM. The assembled G-quadruplex structure acted as an artificial transmembrane ion channel, induced intracellular K + depletion, mitochondrial membrane depolarization, caspase-3 activation, and apoptosis. Significance This work provides a proof-of-concept strategy for logic-gated ion interference under tumor-mimicking extracellular conditions, highlighting the utility of DNA nanodevices in translating multiple microenvironmental stimuli into targeted cellular perturbations.

title: Analytical strategies for stage-appropriate solubility determination of drug candidates in the pharmaceutical industry: A review
Machine learning-assisted fluorescence immunochromatographic detection of Salmonella typhimurium in complex food matrices via tannic acid-enhanced AIE nanoprobes
abstract: Background Rapid on-site detection of Salmonella typhimurium in complex food matrices remains challenging due to the need for fluorescent probes that maintain intense emission in aqueous environments while resisting interference from salts and pH fluctuations. In this work, we explore tannic acid (TA) as a non-covalent interfacial modifier to construct SiO 2 /TCPE/TA (STT) nanoparticles for fluorescence immunochromatographic assays (ICA). Density functional theory (DFT) and time-dependent DFT calculations reveal that TA interacts with the aggregation-induced emission luminogens (AIEgens) TCPE through cooperative π-π stacking and hydrogen bonding, which stabilizes the excited state, slightly narrows the energy gap, and suppresses non-radiative decay pathways. Results Guided by the theoretical predictions, we synthesize STT nanoparticles featuring uniform spherical morphology, tunable size, and a TA-enriched surface. The TA modification boosts the absolute fluorescence quantum yield from 12.91% to 30.51% and extends the fluorescence lifetime from 1.79 ns to 2.57 ns. Taking advantage of these improved photophysical properties, the STT-based ICA strip achieves a visual detection limit of 500 CFU mL -1 and a quantitative limit of 128 CFU mL -1 for S. typhimurium. Practical applicability is confirmed in spiked milk, chicken, and lettuce samples, with recoveries ranging from 82.75% to 119.29%. Moreover, a machine-learning classifier trained on strip images from the three food matrices attains perfect classification accuracy across five concentration levels, enabling automated and objective result reading. Significance This work presents a non-covalent confinement strategy to engineer bright and robust AIE nanoprobes. By combining mechanistic insights from DFT calculations with experimental validation, the TA-mediated approach not only enhances fluorescence performance but also ensures matrix tolerance. The successful integration of STT nanoparticles into a lateral flow immunoassay, coupled with machine-learning-assisted interpretation, offers a rapid, sensitive, and user-friendly platform for foodborne pathogen surveillance, with strong potential for point-of-need applications.

title: Bimetallic synergy-induced Ce/Cu coordination polymer nanozyme with broad-temperature oxidase activity for smartphone-assisted antioxidant sensing
abstract: Total antioxidant capacity (TAC) reflects food quality and redox state, and a simple, sensitive assay is needed. We synthesized a bimetallic AMP-Ce/Cu coordination polymer by one-pot room-temperature coordination of Ce 4+ , Cu 2+ , and adenosine monophosphate (AMP). Electronic coupling between Ce and Cu gave the polymer oxidase-like activity, letting it activate dissolved O 2 directly; the bimetallic material reached ∼4-fold the activity of AMP-Ce 4+ alone. Scavenger and electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) assays showed superoxide radical as the dominant oxidant, with hydroxyl radical secondary. The sensor responded to AA linearly from 15 to 1750 nM and detected down to 4.5 nM. The oxidase-like activity retained >90% of its peak value across 0-55 °C. A paper-based strip delivered rapid, smartphone-assisted on-site readout. Applied to five tea varieties, the method separated their TAC levels. This work shows that lanthanide-transition-metal coordination polymer nanozymes can serve broad-temperature, on-site TAC detection.

title: Outside Front Cover
Editorial Board
Mechanistic insights into iontronic glucose biosensing in enzyme-functionalized single nanochannels
abstract: Iontronic biosensing strategies based on enzyme-functionalized nanochannels rely on the transduction of local pH variations generated by enzymatic reactions at confined interfaces. Despite glucose oxidase (GOx) being one of the most extensively studied enzymes in biosensing, its implementation in iontronic single-nanochannel sensors remains comparatively limited and the factors governing signal generation are still poorly understood. Here, we investigate the mechanisms underlying glucose sensing in GOx-functionalized solid-state single nanochannels. GOx was immobilized within bullet-shaped nanochannels using a cationic polyelectrolyte that promotes enzyme adsorption while amplifying local pH-induced variations in surface charge density. Systematic studies were performed to evaluate the influence of the amount of enzyme, dissolved oxygen availability, and substrate concentration on the sensing response. The results are consistent with a mechanism in which the iontronic response is governed by a steady-state proton concentration established near the nanochannel interface, resulting from the balance between enzymatic proton generation and mass transport. Consequently, both the amount of immobilized enzyme and the local oxygen availability strongly influence signal generation. Based on these findings, a mechanistic framework is proposed that rationalizes the observed dependencies and provides quantitative guidelines for sensor optimization. Based on this understanding, a glucose-dependent iontronic response was demonstrated over the 50-5000 μM range without external oxygen supplementation. More broadly, the results establish design principles for iontronic biosensors based on oxidoreductases and pH-coupled signal transduction.

title: Quantitative characterization of complexity of chromatographic profiles using structure-weighted information entropy
abstract: Quantitative evaluation of chromatographic separation performance is crucial for method optimization in complex systems. The existing measurement indicators of information entropy use the intensity distribution alone without accounting for the time-domain structure and separation state of chromatographic peaks, which limits their discriminatory power in multi-factor condition optimization. In this study, structure-weighted spatial Rényi entropy (SSRE) was therefore proposed through incorporating a Gaussian structural weighting function and a uniformity correction term accounting for peak spacing, resolution, and response distribution. In 64 full-factorial simulated conditions, the average single-factor sensitivity of SSRE was 36.5%, 2.6 times that of Shannon entropy, while the chromatographic discrimination index (CDI) averaged 1.7 times that of the four classical entropies over 100 repeated runs. SSRE identified the theoretically optimal condition in every run and the classical measures in no more than 26%. The design is also the one used to optimize the SSRE parameters. On a held-out simulation with a different peak model, noise structure and design geometry, the same parameters were applied without refitting and SSRE remained closest to an independent reference with a mean Spearman coefficient of 0.571 against 0.549 for Shannon entropy. In 16 gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS) datasets from Lycium barbarum L. (goji), the condition ranked highest by SSRE was among those with the most favourable peak-level parameters. For profiles acquired from the same material system under different pretreatment or acquisition conditions, SSRE provides a peak-detection-free basis for ranking candidate conditions. These findings support SSRE as a complementary measure of chromatographic structure for pretreatment evaluation and method optimization, although broader applicability requires further validation.

title: Synergistically fluorinated triazine COFs as adsorption-ionization integrated matrix for analysis and in situ MALDI imaging of PFOS
abstract: Background Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs), like perfluorooctane sulfonic acid (PFOS), will accumulate continuously in organisms and pose toxic risks. Matrix-assisted laser desorption ionization mass spectrometry imaging (MALDI-MSI) is an effective method for analyzing their biological accumulation characteristics and microscopic spatial distribution. Currently, traditional organic matrices lack specific enrichment capabilities for PFOS, while inorganic adsorption matrices are prone to damaging the ion source. Therefore, the development of organic matrices with dual functions of adsorption and ionization is necessary to overcome these limitations and achieve high-sensitivity in situ MSI of trace PFOS in biological tissues. Result A novel MALDI matrix for ultrasensitive detection and in situ tissue imaging of trace PFOS was developed, using fluorine-engineered triazine covalent organic framework TAPT-DFTA fabricated by Schiff-base condensation as an integrated adsorption-ionization matrix. Featuring a sea urchin-like nanostructure and a high specific surface area of 1057.50 m 2 /g, TAPT-DFTA delivers excellent detection reproducibility with signal RSD values lower than 6.3%. DFT simulations confirm its spontaneous PFOS capture driven by synergistic F-F interactions and hydrophobic forces. Under optimized conditions, it achieves a monolayer adsorption capacity of 63.33 mg/g and an ultralow PFOS LOD of 100 pg/mL, alongside robust salt tolerance and strong anti-interference performance toward biological macromolecules. The matrix further supports high-spatial-resolution MALDI imaging to clearly map PFOS accumulation and spatial distribution in mouse kidney and brain tissues. Significance This work innovatively constructs fluorinated triazine COFs TAPT-DFTA via fluorine engineering to integrate PFOS adsorption and MALDI ionization, breaking single-function drawbacks of traditional matrices. This fluorination tuning strategy balances framework laser stability and energy transfer efficiency, resolving the core trade-off problem that restricts COFs-based MALDI matrix performance. It achieves ppt-level PFOS detection and tissue in-situ imaging, offering a new paradigm for trace persistent organic pollutant spatial analysis.

title: A unified HILIC-FLD-MS workflow for simultaneous peptide and released N-glycan mapping of protein biopharmaceuticals
abstract: BACKGROUND: Quality control of protein biopharmaceuticals has evolved from separate single-attribute assays toward consolidated methods that monitor diverse critical quality attributes in fewer analyses, most often using bottom-up RPLC-MS/MS workflows. Despite its central role in protein characterization, RPLC remains limited in resolving deamidated peptides, retaining hydrophilic species, and separating N-glycoforms, with glycan analysis still often requiring a dedicated HILIC-FLD assay after their release and labeling. RESULTS: We introduce a unified HILIC-FLD-MS multi-attribute method that brings peptide mapping and released N-glycan profiling into a single chromatographic run. The method exploits distinct HILIC retention windows of tryptic peptides and RapiFluor-MS-labeled glycans, enabling concurrent monitoring of peptide- and glycan-related quality attributes with minimal interference. In this configuration, HILIC retains the strengths of released glycan analysis, including superior glycan resolution and reliable FLD-based quantification, while broadening peptide mapping beyond the limitations of RPLC. Comparative experiments further revealed fewer temperature-induced in-column peptide artifacts under HILIC conditions and demonstrated that chromatographic separation can induce cleavage of terminal sialic acids, especially in glycopeptides. SIGNIFICANCE: The proposed method extends HILIC's role from a dedicated glycan separation mode to an integrated, complementary platform for multi-attribute monitoring in biopharmaceutical quality control. By combining peptide-level information with released glycan quantification, the workflow enables more efficient product evaluation while preserving a reliable readout for glycosylation assessment.

title: Selective enrichment and profiling of GlcNAc-containing oligosaccharides in Ophiocordyceps sinensis (Berk.) across five developmental stages using WGA-functionalized NH2-MIL-125
abstract: Glycosaminoglycans (GAGs)-like oligosaccharides in Ophiocordyceps sinensis (O. sinensis) are potential mediators of fungus-host interactions. However, their characterization is severely hindered by co-existing neutral saccharides and the low abundance N-acetylglucosamine (GlcNAc)-containing species (0.67%) of total monosaccharide. To overcome this matrix interference, we engineered a dual-interaction affinity platform (NH 2 -MIL-125-WGA) by covalently immobilizing Wheat Germ Agglutinin (WGA) onto an amino-functionalized titanium metal-organic framework. The optimized material achieved a high WGA loading capacity of 413.14 ± 16.93 μg/mg and maintained over 80% recovery of target acidic glycans, even facing a 1000-fold excess of neutral sugars. The elimination of matrix suppression enabled the identification of 52 previously undetectable GAG-like oligosaccharides in O. sinensis via tandem mass spectrometry. Furthermore, comparative glycomic profiling across five developmental stages (mycelium, zombie larva, fruiting bodies, and spore spread period) revealed that highly sulfated and polymerized oligosaccharides were significantly upregulated during the infective mycelium stage but were notably downregulated during the transition to the reproductive fruiting body stage. These findings demonstrate the capability of the NH 2 -MIL-125-WGA platform for trace glycan analysis and suggest that dynamic variations in GAG content and sulfation patterns are critical to the fungal life cycle.

title: A vacuum-compatible polymer coating for stabilizing nanoparticles and volatile compounds in vMALDI-MS analysis
abstract: Matrix-assisted laser desorption ionization mass spectrometry operated under high vacuum (vMALDI-MS) enables molecular analysis and spatial mapping of metabolites in biological tissues through protonation or deprotonation mechanism. However, its application is constrained by matrix sublimation under high vacuum and low ionization efficiency for redox-active species lacking labile protons. We developed a vacuum-compatible polymer coating for vMALDI-MS adaptable to two complementary ionization strategies, deprotonation using the volatile proton sponge 1, 8-bis(dimethylamino)naphthalene (DMAN) for acidic metabolites, and electron-transfer ionization on (Bi 2 O 3 ) 0 · 07 (CoO) 0 · 03 (ZnO) 0 . 9 nanoparticles for redox-active species without labile protons. Polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) is introduced to form a protective thin film that concurrently prevents nanoparticle dispersion during laser ablation, suppresses organic matrix sublimation, and preserves tissue integrity. A home-built ThermoSonic FilmMaster was established for the deposition of both organic matrices and inorganic nanoparticles. We validated this approach using standard compounds and tissue homogenates, in which volatile short-chain fatty acids, indole derivatives, and aldehydes were putatively annotated by accurate mass matching. We further applied it to image brain sections from 4T1 tumor-bearing mice, where less volatile metabolites such as long-chain fatty acids and lipids were spatially resolved. This approach complements ambient ionization techniques and provides a coating approach for stabilizing nanoparticles and volatile compounds in vMALDI-MS analysis.

title: Continuous flow-through multi-phase electromembrane extraction for protein desalting
abstract: Background Micro-electromembrane extraction (μ-EME) enables efficient protein desalting prior to mass spectrometry by applying an electric field to actively drive interfering salt ions across a free liquid membrane. While this technique provides excellent sample cleanup, conventional static micropipette tip formats face severe physical constraints, including intricate manual phase assembly, prolonged processing times per droplet, and fundamentally low sample throughput. Therefore, the critical problem addressed in this study is overcoming the operational limitations of static extraction by engineering a continuous flow-through EME architecture that automates liquid handling and maximizes protein desalting throughput. Results A continuous flow-through EME platform was developed, processing samples at 2-6 μL/min. The baseline three-phase configuration, utilizing 1-pentanol organic phases and dialysis membranes, achieved 88.8-96.8% salt removal and 92.3-98.7% lysozyme recovery for 92.4-123 mM NaCl samples. To resolve electrolysis-induced acidification, an advanced five-phase configuration was engineered with outermost aqueous acceptor solutions. For 110 mM NaCl, this setup removed 98.2% Na + and 99.6% Cl - with 80.2% lysozyme recovery. Crucially, to tackle the challenging removal of weak-acid phosphate buffers, a concentration-matched ammonia solution was introduced into the anodic acceptor. This dynamically neutralized electrolysis-generated protons, stabilized the sample pH at ∼7.4, and prevented phosphate protonation, enabling >85.8% removal of 1-10 mM phosphate. Operating near the analytes' isoelectric points minimized electromigration, ensuring high recoveries of cytochrome C (>67.6%) and myoglobin (>91.9%). Significance and novelty The novelty of this study involves integrating a continuous flow-through architecture with an active, ammonia-based pH modulation strategy to facilitate the removal of complex polyprotic salts. Findings indicate that aligning the environmental pH with the protein's isoelectric point helps minimize adsorptive loss. Ultimately, this structurally optimized platform serves as a fundamental proof-of-concept for an automated sample pretreatment approach that enhances post-desalination mass spectrometry signal-to-noise ratios.

title: A sample-to-answer framework for on-site body fluid identification based on microbial signature
abstract: Background On-site body fluid identification can rapidly provide decisive evidence for crime scene reconstruction and suspect apprehension. However, current laboratory-based methods are unsuited to field-based scenarios. Protein-based biochemical strategies fail to amplify trace biomolecules and protein is susceptible to denaturation, while nucleic acid-based approach relying on RNA profiling or DNA methylation inevitably requires purification, endonuclease digestion or bisulfite conversion that conflict with speediness and convenience. Therefore, a rapid, portable, and user-friendly strategy is urgently needed for on-site body fluid identification. Results In this study, a systematic sample-to-answer framework for on-site body fluid identification is established based on microbial signature. A tailor-made lysis buffer is formulated to lyse Streptococcus salivarius and Lactobacillus crispatus, characteristic of saliva and vaginal secretion respectively, releasing nucleic acids for direct amplification without further purification. Due to the excellent efficiency under straightforward condition, loop-mediated isothermal amplification is employed for characteristic DNA recognition. Besides, a lateral flow device is assembled, enabling result interpretation by naked eye. To suppress carryover contamination under rudimentary field conditions, uracil-DNA glycosylase-based anti-aerosol strategy is further integrated. The sole apparatus required is only a heater for isothermal incubation during amplification. Hence, a handheld device of cigarette-case size is designed and fabricated to fit this framework and on-site deployment. The reagents for amplification are mixed and lyophilized beforehand to simplify the procedure more and avoid cold-chain transport. Significance A systematic sample-to-answer framework for on-site body fluid identification is established, enabling accurate identification of body fluid left on various carriers involving sexual assault and confinement. The entire workflow can be completed within 1 h, substantially reducing the operational complexity and equipment requirement of conventional laboratory-based assays. This framework demonstrates its feasibility as a rapid and practical tool for on-site body fluid identification and highlight its potential for field deployment in forensic investigations.

title: A signal-enhanced competitive ELISA based on peptide screened by solid-liquid phase panning hybrid for sensitive detection of respiratory syncytial virus glycoprotein
abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is the leading cause of severe lower respiratory tract infections in infants, young children and immunocompromised individuals, to which effective vaccines and specific antiviral therapies remain elusive. Although several RSV vaccines and long-acting monoclonal antibodies have been approved for specific populations, rapid and sensitive diagnostic tools are still critical for early clinical triage. RSV glycoprotein (GP) is a highly glycosylated adhesion protein in mediating viral adhesion and immune escape, making it an ideal target for antigen detection. Herein a combination of solid phase panning with liquid phase panning strategy was explored to isolate peptide GS24 (sequence: SRTCTPNFCYLG) with high affinity and specificity to RSV GP. Molecular dynamics simulation indicates that Arg 2 and Phe 8 residues on GS24 play a crucial role in binding, due to lower binding energies. Glu232 and Glu284 residues on the RSV GP interact with Arg 2 of the peptide, respectively, to form two pairs of hydrogen bonds (Glu232-Arg2, Glu284-Arg2). Additionally, there exists π-π stacking interaction between Pro234 of RSV GP and Phe8 of the peptide. Then the peptide GS24a was used as a recognition probe, and coordination reaction between L-ascorbic-acid 2-phosphate and Fe 3+ as colorimetric signal, a signal-enhanced competitive binding of peptide/alkaline phosphatase-conjugated streptavidin complex to magnetic bead-immobilized antigen was constructed. The as-developed signal-enhanced competitive ELISA can detect target RSV GP within the linear range of 0.15-10 ng/mL and detection limit of 0.1 ng/mL. Finally, the proposed method was applied to detect human nasopharyngeal swab samples reproducibly, with the results in agreement well with commercial test strip, suggesting its good accuracy. This proposed method features simplicity, convenience and good sensitivity, which may offer a promising alternative for point-of-care RSV diagnosis. This work also provides guidance for developing similar immunoassay to detect other respiratory diseases.

title: DESI-MS imaging reveals spatial variations of secondary metabolites in Astragalus roots and their correlation with biosynthesis
abstract: Mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) has advanced the in situ analysis of chemical constituents in traditional Chinese medicine (TCM). However, many TCMs that are derived from perennial roots or rhizomes (e.g., ginseng, Astragalus, and licorice) present two main challenges: their hard texture hindering effective sectioning, and their secondary metabolites, particularly those with post-modification, are prone to unwanted molecular ion fragmentation, which reduces analytical sensitivity. In this study, Astragalus roots were used as a model to address these challenges in desorption electrospray ionization (DESI)-MSI. Firstly, poly-L-lysine moistening-cryosectioning method facilitated tissue sectioning and enhanced signal intensity, while optimizing the collision gas flow rate and scan time minimized undesired ion fragmentation. Applying this method to Astragalus roots revealed that isoflavones and their glycosides were widely distributed across all tissues, whereas saponins and organic acids exhibited distinct tissue-specific localization in the periderm and cambium, respectively. These spatial distributions were validated by LC/MS analysis. Integration with transcriptomic data revealed correlations between metabolite localization and the expression of their biosynthetic genes. Finally, application of the method to samples with different origins further revealed variations in the spatial distribution of isoflavones, including formononetin (17) and calycosin (12), as well as organic acids. Collectively, these findings provide an effective strategy for MSI analysis of TCMs and plant secondary metabolism, highlighting the complex spatial organization of metabolites and offering insights into their biosynthesis.

title: Complementary molecular windows revealed by direct NanoESI and SPE-ESI FT-ICR-MS for dissolved organic matter characterization
abstract: Nanoelectrospray ionization (nanoESI) coupled with Fourier transform ion cyclotron resonance mass spectrometry (FT-ICR-MS) has emerged as a powerful approach for the direct molecular characterization of dissolved organic matter (DOM) without solid-phase extraction (SPE). However, the differences in molecular coverage and compositional selectivity between direct nanoESI and conventional SPE-ESI for DOM analysis remain unclear. In this study, two standard reference materials, Suwannee River natural organic matter (SRNOM) and Elliott soil fulvic acid (ESFA), were used to systematically compare two ionization sources (nanoESI and ESI) and two sample introduction modes (direct injection and SPE pretreatment). Compared with conventional ESI, nanoESI increased total ion intensity by 4.5-fold and 3.9-fold for SRNOM and ESFA, respectively, and expanded assigned molecular formulas by 1.5-1.7 times. ESI yielded a greater number of aromatic and highly unsaturated compounds, whereas nanoESI enabled broader molecular coverage, including aliphatic compounds, oxygen-rich aromatics, and heteroatom-containing species. SPE pretreatment enriched lignins and condensed aromatics in both samples, while direct nanoESI retained more lipid- and peptide-like compounds in SRNOM and abundant aminosugar- and carbohydrate-like compounds in ESFA. Combing the ionization and pretreatment effects, SPE-ESI favors the detection of aromatic fractions, whereas direct nanoESI better captures aliphatic- and tannin-like components. The two methods yield complementary information and enabled more comprehensive and unbiased molecular profiling of environmental DOM.

title: Synergistic CID and EAD fragmentation by high-resolution mass spectrometry for rapid discovery and de novo structural deduction of a new peptide
abstract: The conventional natural product (NP) discovery pipeline is constrained by a sequential, isolation-before-identification paradigm that suffers from low throughput and inherent chemical blindness. High-resolution mass spectrometry (HR-MS) offers a compelling alternative, enabling direct interrogation of crude extracts, while the dual fragmentation modalities, CID for conventional bonds and EAD for diagnostic radical-directed cleavages, collectively enable structure assembly without prior purification. In this study, we report a CID and EAD integrated strategy that successfully guided the de novo structural deduction of a new peptide from Streptomyces parvulus ZS18011. A FUNEL-based MS 1 filter prioritized the ion at m/z 811.4716 as a candidate octapeptide, whose full backbone was subsequently deducted by orthogonal CID and EAD fragmentation. The structural assignment was corrected by NMR spectroscopy and genome sequencing, ultimately identifying the smallest new member of the linaridin family. This work underscores a broader transition in NP discovery, from blind screening to knowledge-guided prioritization, thereby accelerating the identification of new NPs.

title: Near-infrared excited core-shell upconversion composites for living cells proteome labeling
abstract: Near-infrared excitation effectively eliminates interference from intracellular visible-light-absorbing photosensitizers for living cells proteome labeling. Herein, a core-shell upconversion composites (CS-NaYF 4 @MOF) were developed for NIR activated proteome proximity labeling in living cells. A NIR-responsive photosensitizer was fabricated by in situ growth of a Cu-TCPP-based metal-organic framework (MOF) shell on Nd 3+ -sensitized core-shell upconversion nanoparticles. Upon 808 nm NIR excitation, the composites generate green upconversion luminescence to efficiently activate Cu(II) meso-Tetra(4-carboxyphenyl)porphine (Cu-TCPP) for reactive oxygen species production, enabling protein labeling in living cells with nucleophilic substrate. The characterizations confirm the successful formation of a crystalline MOF coating with homogeneous elemental distribution. Cellular assays reveal low photo-toxicity, allowing time- and concentration-dependent protein labeling under NIR light irradiation. By combining click chemistry and mass spectrometry, high-throughput proteome identification in living cells is successfully realized. This work not only extends the application of MOF-based materials in proteomics, but also offers a NIR excited strategy for living cells proteome labeling.

title: Fluorescent labeling of lysosomal α-L-fucosidase using an activity-based near-infrared (NIR) fluorogenic probe
abstract: Background Lysosomal α-L-fucosidase catalyzes the degradation of fucosylated glycoconjugates and is implicated in multiple pathological events. Although conventional fluorogenic substrates have been utilized to detect the glycosidase in cells, they are inappropriate for long-term imaging owing to the diffusion of the fluorophores released upon enzymatic cleavage. On the other hand, existing activity-based probes are useful for capturing the target enzyme, but they cannot be readily used for live-cell fluorescence imaging. Results We developed αFuc-Bn-NIR(CM)-AY, an activity-based near-infrared (NIR) fluorogenic probe for selective fluorescence imaging and covalent labeling of active α-L-fucosidase. The probe comprised (1) an α-L-fucose recognition unit linked to a hemicyanine-derived NIR fluorophore through a self-immolative scaffold, (2) a carbamate-based reactive moiety appended to the fluorophore, and (3) a terminal alkyne bioorthogonal handle. The probe functioned as a mechanism-based, irreversible inhibitor that covalently labeled and inactivated active α-L-fucosidase upon fluorescence activation. In addition, αFuc-Bn-NIR(CM)-AY showed high selectivity toward α-L-fucosidase and enabled robust fluorescent labeling of the enzyme. Moreover, the probe allowed detection of the enzyme at concentrations as low as 20 nM, and the labeling was markedly reduced by an α-L-fucosidase inhibitor. In live cells, enzyme-mediated activation produced persistent lysosome-associated fluorescence with minimal cytotoxicity. The terminal alkyne further facilitated click chemistry-mediated biotinylation and affinity enrichment of labeled lysosomal α-L-fucosidase from treated cells. Significance αFuc-Bn-NIR(CM)-AY integrates fluorescence activation, covalent enzyme labeling, and affinity-based enrichment within a single NIR platform, overcoming the diffusion-associated limitation of conventional fluorogenic substrates and the imaging limitation of existing activity-based probes. It provides a useful tool for prolonged imaging and covalent capture of active lysosomal α-L-fucosidase.

title: l-Histidine functionalized MXene quantum dots as novel fluorescent sensors for wide range detection of methyl orange
abstract: The wide-range and highly selective detection of toxic dye molecules remains an important challenge in environmental analysis. As an organic synthetic dye, methyl orange (MO) can pose considerable health risks even at low concentrations. Although diverse analytical approaches have been established for the detection of MO, the simultaneous achievement of a broad detection range and high selectivity remains challenging. Herein, nitrogen-functionalized MXene quantum dots (N-MQDs) were fabricated and employed for the first time as fluorescent probes for MO detection. N-MQDs were obtained using 2D MXene Ti 3 C 2 nanosheets and l-histidine as raw chemicals via the hydrothermal method. Notably, l-histidine, a non-toxic dopant, was utilized for the first time in the preparation of N-MQDs. Furthermore, the introduction of l-histidine contributed to the passivation of surface defect sites in N-MQDs, resulting in bright fluorescence emission. N-MQDs exhibited a detection limit of 0.02 μM for MO and a detection range of 0.05-450 μM, which is wider than those of most reported methods for MO detection. N-MQDs were applied to the detection of MO in real water samples, and satisfactory spike recovery values were obtained. Mechanistic investigation of the response toward MO demonstrated that the fluorescence quenching of the N-MQDs by MO was attributed to Förster resonance energy transfer. The results obtained in this work demonstrate that N-MQDs are promising fluorescence probes for MO detection and show great promise in environmental monitoring applications.

title: Integrated targeted metabolomics and complementary [α-15N] glutamine tracing reveal glutamine metabolic remodeling associated with RA-ILD
abstract: Background Rheumatoid arthritis-associated interstitial lung disease (RA-ILD) is a severe complication with limited therapeutic options, characterized by destructive joint lesions and pulmonary fibrosis involving excessive collagen deposition. Glutamine metabolism supplies precursors for collagen-related amino acid biosynthesis, which drives the fibrotic remodeling process, but its cross-organ redistribution and pathway-specific utilization remain difficult to resolve using conventional metabolomic readouts. An analytical strategy capable of integrating quantitative multi-matrix profiling with isotope-resolved nitrogen tracing is therefore needed to characterize alterations in glutamine-related amino acid metabolism associated with RA-ILD and its pharmacological modulation. Results We established a complementary analytical framework in which 3-trimethylsilyl-1-propanaminium chloride (TSPC) derivatization-assisted UPLC-QqQ-MS/MS targeted metabolomics and intestinal amino acid transporter profiling were applied to an RA-ILD rat model, while [α- 15 N] glutamine tracing was independently performed in a TGF-β1-induced fibrotic cell model to examine pathway-specific glutamine nitrogen utilization. The validated method enabled sensitive quantification of glutamine-related amino acids in serum, lung tissue, and cells. In RA-ILD rats, cross-matrix profiling revealed a compartment-dependent disturbance of glutamine-related amino acid distribution, characterized by pulmonary accumulation coupled with altered circulating availability. Clematis triterpenoid saponins (CTSs) partially normalized this metabolic imbalance and were associated with coordinated regulation of intestinal glutamine transporters. Stable-isotope tracing in a fibrotic cell model further showed preferential incorporation of glutamine-derived nitrogen into the serine-glycine axis, which was supported by increased expression of ATF4-associated serine-glycine biosynthetic enzymes in lung tissue. CTSs treatment attenuated the corresponding lung transcriptional alterations. Significance Together, invivo multi-matrix metabolomics characterized systemic glutamine-related metabolic redistribution and its response to CTSs in RA-ILD, whereas complementary in vitro isotope tracing provided pathway-level evidence for preferential glutamine-derived nitrogen utilization through the serine-glycine axis under fibrotic stimulation. Such a complementary framework also provides a transferable analytical strategy for investigating cross-organ diseases and multi-level interventions of traditional Chinese medicines.

title: CRISPR/Cas12a-based simplified lateral flow assay for sensitive detection of OTA and AFB1
abstract: Abstract Ochratoxin A (OTA) and Aflatoxin B1 (AFB1) rank among the most widespread mycotoxins in contaminated agricultural products, presenting significant risks to human health via dietary and inhalation exposure. Their harmful impacts encompass hepatotoxicity, nephrotoxicity, neurotoxicity, and immunosuppressive effects. A multiplex CRISPR/Cas12a-assisted lateral flow assay (MC-LFA) was developed for the simultaneous detection of OTA and AFB1, achieving detection limits as low as 50 pg/mL and 250 pg/mL, respectively. The visual detection sensitivity for both mycotoxins was enhanced by 1 to 2 orders of magnitude compared to commercial assays. The experimental procedures have been streamlined by integrating streptavidin lines onto the test strip, eliminating conventional magnetic separation steps. Additionally, the approach eliminates the requirement for crRNA replacement, thereby substantially reducing operational costs. This approach exhibits considerable potential for broad application, given its high sensitivity, specificity, operational simplicity, and cost-effectiveness. This work underscores the significant potential of the MC-LFA strategy for food safety monitoring in resource-limited settings, establishing it as a versatile tool with broad applications in public health, agriculture, and environmental surveillance.

title: An integrated “Sampling-SERS detection-regeneration” analytical platform based on flexible Ag/AgCl/CdS heterojunctions for pesticide monitoring
abstract: Background Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) has emerged as a powerful tool for the rapid detection of pesticide residues. As the demand for rapid on-site screening of agricultural products continues to rise, traditional SERS approaches that rely on rigid substrates and cumbersome pretreatment steps struggle to meet the diverse requirements of practical field testing. Therefore, achieving a seamless transition from direct on-site sampling to highly sensitive and accurate quantitative analysis remains a critical challenge. Results An integrated analytical platform was developed by constructing a noble-metal/semiconductor Ag/AgCl/CdS (AASC) heterojunction on a flexible carbon cloth substrate. The substrate's flexibility ensures conformal contact with irregular surfaces for rapid in situ sampling. Driven by the synergy between the electromagnetic enhancement of localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) from Ag nanoparticles (Ag NPs) and the charge-transfer (CT) mechanism within the Z-scheme heterojunction, the AASC substrate exhibits exceptional SERS sensitivity, achieving a limit of detection (LOD) of 6.46 × 10 -11 M for 4-mercaptobenzoic acid (4-MBA). The integrated semiconductor components also impart photocatalytic activity, yielding an 83.64% degradation efficiency for malachite green (MG) within 90 min. For practical applications, the AASC platform enables swabbing-based in-situ screening of thiram (TRM) and thiabendazole (TBZ) residues on real fruit surfaces, achieving surface LODs of 0.096 and 0.805 ng/cm 2 , respectively. Significance and novelty While inherently focused on surface-level contaminants rather than deeply penetrating systemic pesticides, this rapid swabbing strategy excels as a highly efficient and non-destructive frontline screening tool. The method demonstrates excellent quantitative reliability and supports alternating cyclic detection of different pesticides, followed by efficient substrate regeneration through photocatalytic degradation. This integrated "sampling-SERS detection-regeneration" strategy provides a sustainable and reliable solution for on-site pesticide monitoring and environmental safety analysis.

title: Magnetic solid-phase extraction coupled with fluorescent lateral flow immunoassay for simultaneous on-site detection of methamphetamine, morphine, and ketamine in wastewater
abstract: Background Wastewater-based epidemiology provides objective, non-invasive data on community drug use, but conventional ultra-high performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (UPLC-MS/MS) analysis is laboratory-based and time-consuming. Although fluorescent lateral flow immunoassay (LFIA) offers a simple, rapid, and low-cost alternative for on-site screening, its direct application to wastewater is limited by low analyte concentrations and complex sample matrices. Results We developed a magnetic solid-phase extraction (MSPE)-LFIA platform based on polydopamine-coated magnetic nanoparticle adsorbents for simultaneous detection of methamphetamine, morphine, and ketamine in wastewater. By investigating the organic solvent compatibility of commercial LFIA strips and using an acidic eluent with low methanol content, the nitrogen blowdown reconstitution step was avoided. Under optimized conditions, the proposed method achieved limits of detection of 13.6, 14.4, and 50.8 ng L -1 , offering 66-, 61-, and 45-fold higher sensitivity than direct LFIA, with recoveries of 86.8-115.7% and RSDs below 12.3%. The entire procedure was completed within 15 min without bulky instrumentation. The method was applied to real wastewater samples, and the results exhibited good consistency with UPLC-MS/MS and a lower false-negative rate (16.7%) compared with direct LFIA (100%). Significance This work provides the first MSPE-LFIA platform for simultaneous on-site screening of methamphetamine, morphine, and ketamine in wastewater. This platform enabled direct eluate loading and eliminated the nitrogen blowdown step, thereby simplifying the workflow. Given its simplicity and low cost, it is expected to be applicable to multiplex detection of common illicit drugs or other hazardous organic pollutants in wastewater.

title: Unlocking coordinatively unsaturated Bi sites in mixed-linker Bi-MOFs on laser-induced graphene electrode for on-site monitoring of toxic heavy metals
abstract: Background To protect public health and ensure food safety, heavy metal ions in environment and food must be identified both quickly and accurately. Electrochemical techniques have become a focus of research interest, largely owing to their potential for simultaneous quantification of multiple heavy metal ions, low cost, ease of miniaturization, and simple operation. Results A newly developed electrochemical sensor using a defective bismuth-based metal-organic framework (BiFcFc'-MOF) on laser-induced graphene (LIG) is reported for the simultaneous analysis of Pb 2+ and Cd 2+ ions. The BiFcFc'-MOF was synthesized using Bi ions coordinated with 1,1'-ferrocene dicarboxylic acid (Fc) and ferrocene carboxylic acid (Fc') as mixed π-conjugated linkers, which creates abundant coordinatively unsaturated Bi sites. The combination of BiFcFc'-MOF and LIG allows for large surface area and rapid electron transfer through the conductive LIG network, resulting in an enhanced sensitivity and a reduction in detection limits (LOD). The sensor demonstrates low LOD values of 0.38 μg/L for Cd 2+ and 0.98 μg/L for Pb 2+ under optimal conditions, surpassing numerous electrochemical platforms in performance. The practical potential was also confirmed by applying the sensor to lake water, soil, soybean, sorghum, and rice, yielding satisfactory recovery rates. Significance and Novelty: A defective BiFcFc'-MOF with abundant coordinatively unsaturated Bi sites is first fabricated via a mixed ferrocene-based ligand strategy, breaking the activity-conductivity trade-off of conventional MOFs. This study presents a hopeful strategy for on-site monitoring of toxic metal ions in complex samples.

title: Electrochemical profiling of urinary extracellular vesicle proteomes to reveal differential hypoxic adaptation
abstract: Hypobaric hypoxia induces physiological stress, yet early molecular alterations preceding functional impairment are not adequately captured by conventional physiologic analysis. Extracellular vesicles (EVs), encapsulated proteins and RNAs reflective of cellular state, represent a compelling source of non-invasive biomarkers for interrogating hypoxia-induced molecular adaptation at the proteome and post-transcriptional levels. Here, we present an electrochemical-proteomic framework for quantitative profiling of urinary EV (uEV) cargo during hypobaric hypoxic exposure. Two analog astronauts were monitored during a 10-day high-altitude expedition (14,860 ft). Pre-, mid-, and post-exposure physiological assessments using pulse oximetry and spirometry were complemented by molecular analysis of uEVs. EVs were captured directly on a screen-printed gold electrode-based immunosensor, followed by electric-field lysis for offering on-chip access to intravesicular cargo. EV enrichment and hypoxic stress responses were validated by Western blotting. Non-faradaic electrochemical impedance spectroscopy enables quantification of EV-associated proteins, including epithelial secretory proteins (MUC5AC and MUC1), EV biogenesis markers (TSG101), membrane remodeling proteins (GM2AP), and growth factor signaling receptors (HER2, EGFR, and GPC1), while EV-associated microRNAs were profiled by small RNA sequencing. The participant exhibiting greater physiological perturbation under hypoxia showed reduced pulmonary function and coordinated upregulation of EV proteins linked to epithelial activation, vesicle biogenesis, membrane remodeling, and growth-factor signaling, along with microRNAs (miR-200 family, miR-375, and the miR-17-92 cluster). In contrast, the participant maintaining more stable pulmonary function under hypoxia exhibited stable lung mechanics with minimal molecular perturbation. These findings underscore electrochemical uEV profiling as a sensitive and non-invasive approach for proteome-level assessment of individual-specific physiological response to hypoxic stress under extreme environmental conditions.

title: HOF-101/AgInS2 photogate-engineered organic photoelectrochemical transistor for amplified miRNA-21 biosensing
abstract: Background Nucleic acid detection requires sensitive and controllable signal transduction strategies for reliable bioanalysis. Organic photoelectrochemical transistor (OPECT) provides a promising platform for transistor-level signal amplification, while its analytical performance is strongly dependent on photogate design and interfacial signal transduction. Results Herein, we report a photogate-engineered OPECT for transistor-amplified biosensing of miRNA-21, enabled by a HOF-101/AgInS 2 heterojunction. The integration of AgInS 2 quantum dots with a photosensitive hydrogen-bonded organic framework (HOF-101) forms an efficient photogate, promoting photoinduced charge separation and enabling light-driven modulation of the interfacial gate potential. Upon target recognition, catalytic hairpin assembly (CHA) triggers rolling circle amplification (RCA), producing G-rich DNA strands that, in the presence of hemin, generate peroxidase-mimetic catalytic centers. These catalytic units then mediate enzymatic precipitation at the photogate interface, leading to the accumulation of insulating deposits. The resulting interfacial deposition modulates the photogating response and effective gate voltage, thereby transducing molecular recognition events into amplified transistor current responses. This molecular-to-transistor signal transduction pathway enables highly sensitive and selective measurement of miRNA-21. The present design provides a strategy for integrating photoresponsive interface engineering with transistor-level amplification for advanced bioanalysis.

title: MoS2/Ti3C2 composite interface as an electrochemical platform for dopamine and ascorbic acid sensing
abstract: The electrochemical quantification of dopamine (DA) and ascorbic acid (AA) is of great physiological importance. However, it remains challenging due to the sluggish electrode kinetics of both molecules, motivating the design of electrode materials with tailored interfacial properties. Here, a porous layered MoS 2 /Ti 3 C 2 nanocomposite with in-situ grown MoS 2 on Ti 3 C 2 MXene is prepared via a facile hydrothermal route and evaluated as a modified electrode material for DA and AA sensing. Electrochemical characterization reveals that the composite substantially enhances the oxidation peak current for both analytes relative to pristine MoS 2 , indicating improved electrocatalytic activity. For individual detection, the composite electrode exhibits linear response ranges of 0.8-1.6 mM for DA and 0.7-3.3 mM for AA, with detection limits (S/N = 3) of 4.5 μM and 9.2 μM, respectively. The observed electrochemical performance is attributed to a synergistic mechanism: the highly conductive Ti 3 C 2 framework supports rapid charge transfer, while the in-situ grown MoS 2 nanosheets form a three-dimensional porous architecture that mitigates Ti 3 C 2 restacking, increases the density of accessible active sites, and promotes analyte diffusion. These findings establish the MoS 2 /Ti 3 C 2 nanocomposite as a promising material platform for continuing development in electrochemical biosensing, including application in decentralized diagnostics for neurological disorders.

title: Synergistic dual-signal amplification aptasensor and AuNPs@TtTp COF-based SERS platform for ultrasensitive detection of SARS-CoV-2 receptor-binding domain
abstract: Background Early and accurate detection of the virus SARS-CoV-2, responsible for COVID-19 pandemic, is essential for controlling the disease spread. However, existing diagnostic platforms are constrained by cost, turnaround time, or limited sensitivity. Surface-enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) technique offers an attractive alternative, though conventional SERS substrates suffer from limited reproducibility and weak, non-specific analyte binding. Results This study presents developing a highly sensitive and selective signal-off SERS aptasensor for detecting SARS-CoV-2 by combining a gold-nanoparticle-embedded covalent organic framework (AuNPs@TtTp COF) substrate with Au@4ATP@Ag@Au core-shell SERS tags functionalized with the virus RBD (receptor binding domain)-specific DNA aptamer. Target-induced disassembly of the tag-aptamer-COF hotspot architecture produces a concentration-dependent decrease in SERS intensity, giving a detection limit of 1.3 × 10 -17 g/mL over a dynamic range of 1 × 10 -16 - 1 × 10 -10 g/mL, with RSD values of 6.65 - 7.61% across replicate spots and substrates. Molecular dynamics simulations of three candidate aptamer-RBD complexes identifies the TZ1 model as most stable (binding free energy -57.99 kcal/mol). The aptasensor detects RBD in diluted human saliva, with results closely matching those of a commercial antigen test-kit. Significance By embedding gold nanoparticles within a triazine-linked COF and pairing them with dual-shell Au@4ATP@Ag@Au SERS tags, this platform achieves reproducible, ultrasensitive detection of the SARS-CoV-2 RBD, several orders of magnitude below other alternatives and outperforming previously reported SERS-based sensors for the same target. Because the design relies only on swapping the aptamer sequence to redirect target recognition, this strategy offers a readily adaptable template for rapid, low-cost diagnostics against other viral pathogens, and its performance in real saliva samples points toward a practical route from bench-scale detection to point-of-care screening.

title: A paper-tip dual-mode aptasensor integrating SERS and colorimetric method for detecting oxytetracycline
abstract: Oxytetracycline (OTC) is widely used in aquaculture and livestock farming, and its leaching into the environment and residues in food can easily lead to bioaccumulation risks. There is an urgent need to develop a simple and efficient method for detecting OTC. Herein, we developed a novel paper-tip dual-mode aptasensor for rapid and high-sensitivity detection of OTC. Firstly, a novel composite probe was designed by co-modifying 4MBA and horseradish peroxidase (HRP) on the silver nanoparticles (AgNPs), which owns the Raman "hotspot" effect and the catalytic activity of peroxidase. Then, we utilized the lateral flow on the paper tip to achieve the target capture and probe enrichment within 1 h, simplifying the experimental operation and ensuring detection stability. The paper-tip aptasensor could provide Raman and colorimetric signals that effectively addressed the false-positive issues and low accuracy commonly observed in traditional paper-based sensors. The paper-tip aptasensor displayed a wide linear detection range for the detection of OTC (1-10,000 nM) with low detection limit of 0.635 nM (Raman) and 0.728 nM (colorimetric). The recovery of OTC in spiked real samples ranged from 81.05% to 111.60% (n = 3), which indicated the good applicability of the paper-tip aptasensor. The paper-tip aptasensor has the advantages of simple operation, low cost, portability and high sensitivity, which is anticipated to serve as a powerful alternative for rapid, on-site antibiotic detection.

title: Enhancing untargeted lipidomics using offline two-dimensional LC–MS and systematic evaluation of data processing tools
abstract: Although two-dimensional liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (2DLC-MS) has been explored to improve lipidomic coverage, its practical implementation remains limited by challenges in fractionation design and interpretation of complex datasets. Here we report an optimized offline hydrophilic interaction chromatography-reversed-phase liquid chromatography (HILIC-RPLC) 2DLC-MS workflow for untargeted lipidomics. A simplified five-fraction HILIC strategy was developed to enhance lipid class separation while maintaining practical analytical throughput. Optimization of solvent composition, mobile phases, and gradient conditions improved compatibility between chromatographic dimensions and enabled efficient fractionation prior to RPLC-MS analysis. Compared with conventional one-dimensional RPLC-MS, the proposed workflow reduced lipid co-elution and ion suppression, resulting in approximately two-fold higher lipid feature coverage in biological samples including serum, tissue, and cultured cells. Chromatographic fractionation information was further used as an orthogonal parameter to evaluate lipid annotation reliability. Using this framework, three lipidomics software platforms-MetaboScape, MS-DIAL, and LipidScreener-were systematically evaluated for processing 2DLC-MS datasets. The results reveal substantial variability among software tools and demonstrate that integrating chromatographic fractionation with data processing improves confidence in untargeted lipidomic analysis.

title: Peptide-engineered catalytic and antifouling interface for reliable electrochemical analysis in undiluted biological samples
abstract: Background Catalytic signal amplification can improve the sensitivity of electrochemical analysis, but its analytical reliability is frequently compromised in complex biological matrices because nonspecific adsorption hinders mass transport, blocks electron-transfer pathways, and attenuates signal output. Integrating signal amplification with effective antifouling regulation within a single analytical interface is therefore important for maintaining quantitative performance in untreated biological samples. Here, we address the challenge of reconciling catalytic amplification with matrix tolerance for reliable electrochemical analysis in undiluted biological samples. Results A peptide-engineered analytical interface was constructed by integrating a peptide-templated Au/PNF nanozyme with an antifouling and MMP-2-responsive peptide layer. Self-assembled hIAPP 20-29 nanofibers directed Au nanoparticle nucleation to generate a peroxidase-like nanozyme capable of H 2 O 2 -dependent electrochemical signal amplification. The multifunctional peptide suppressed nonspecific adsorption while preserving target accessibility. The resulting platform enabled MMP-2 determination over 0.5-100 ng mL -1 with a calculated detection limit of 37 pg mL -1 . In undiluted human serum, the antifouling interface provided improved recovery and precision compared with the corresponding non-antifouling interface. It also markedly reduced matrix-induced signal suppression after exposure to FBS and whole blood, demonstrating improved matrix tolerance and more stable analytical performance under severe biological interference. Significance and novelty This work integrates catalytic amplification and antifouling regulation within a peptide-engineered electrochemical interface and experimentally distinguishes catalytic, interfacial, and matrix-tolerance contributions. The strategy maintains analytical reliability in undiluted serum while preserving catalytic signal generation, providing a general design concept for electrochemical analysis in complex biological matrices where signal amplification alone is insufficient.

title: A comparison of PCA, ASCA, and vASCA for enhancing the interpretability of biological Raman spectroscopy
abstract: Background Raman spectroscopy is often used to analyze complex biological systems, but interpreting the resulting spectra remains difficult because of overlapping vibrational bands and the limitations of standard multivariate approaches such as Principal Component Analysis. This work assesses whether ANOVA-Simultaneous Component Analysis and its variable-selection extension can address these interpretability issues. More specifically, the goal was to determine if this approach could isolate spectral features that reflect metabolic syndrome and its progression over time. Results Serum Raman spectra were collected from control rats and those with metabolic syndrome at four time points. The datasets were then analyzed comparatively using Principal Component Analysis, ANOVA-Simultaneous Component Analysis, and Variable-Selection ANOVA-Simultaneous Component Analysis, with attention not only to statistical separation but also to the interpretability of the resulting features in a biochemical context. Variable-Selection ANOVA-Simultaneous Component Analysis shows a narrower set of statistically relevant spectral regions. Among these, a Raman band in the 907-926 cm -1 range appeared as a candidate signature associated with metabolic syndrome. Temporal variation was also evident, particularly in lipid- and protein-related bands between 8 and 52 weeks, although some overlap across groups persisted. Compared with the other methods, this approach yielded a clearer feature-based separation and, in most comparisons, stronger statistical contrasts. Significance and novelty The use of Variable-Selection ANOVA-Simultaneous Component Analysis makes the relationship between spectral features and the physiology of the disease clearer. Our approach paves the way to establish an interpretable tool to identify relevant spectral signatures in biological Raman spectra datasets.

title: Simplified liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry quantification of adalimumab reveals peptide interference and modestly stronger exposure-response associations than ELISA
abstract: Adalimumab therapeutic drug monitoring in inflammatory arthritis is constrained by variability in analytical methods, with most clinically established target concentrations derived from immunoassays. In this study, we developed and validated a simplified liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) method for adalimumab quantification and compared its analytical and clinical performance with ELISA in patients with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) or psoriatic arthritis (PsA). Serum samples from 258 observations were analysed. The two methods showed overall good agreement, although systematic differences were observed. Both methods demonstrated an association between higher adalimumab concentrations and improved clinical response; however, LC-MS showed a somewhat stronger discriminatory performance and more consistent associations with clinical outcomes than ELISA. This was most evident in analyses based on DAS28-defined response, whereas PsARC-based stratification showed more limited discriminatory power. Receiver operating characteristic analyses indicated improved classification performance when using DAS28, with LC-MS showing a modest but consistent advantage over ELISA. Exposure-response analyses supported a concentration-dependent treatment effect with a plateau at higher exposure levels, more clearly reflected by LC-MS. In addition, LC-MS measurements appeared more evenly distributed across analytical runs, whereas ELISA showed clustering that may reflect inter-assay variability. Overall, LC-MS provides a broader analytical range and somewhat stronger exposure-response associations, although the incremental benefit over ELISA is moderate and must be balanced against cost and practical considerations for routine implementation.

title: Gas-phase stabilization by tertiary interactions in yeast tRNAPhe and quaternary contacts in a small RNA-RNA complex
abstract: Native mass spectrometry (nMS) and ion mobility (IM) are now established tools for the structural analysis of proteins and protein complexes, but their application to RNAs and RNA-RNA assemblies remains less developed. Here, we examine how magnesium, ionization polarity, solution temperature, and collisional activation influence the mass-corrected collision cross section (mCCS) of wild-type (WT) and a structurally destabilized mutant (MT) yeast tRNA Phe . Under positive-polarity ionization, magnesium was essential for WT tRNA Phe to fold into and retain native-like structures. In 2 mM magnesium acetate, increasing the solution temperature from 25 to 60°C produced little change in the mCCS of WT tRNA Phe , whereas the mCCS of MT tRNA Phe increased. Collisional activation further distinguished the two constructs: increasing the trap collision energy induced a pronounced decrease in the mCCS of WT but only a modest decrease for MT tRNA Phe , consistent with the absence of magnesium-supported tertiary contacts in the mutant. We also assessed the HJ3 RNA-RNA heterodimer using collision- and surface-induced dissociation (CID and SID, respectively). CID primarily resulted in charge stripping, while SID generated proportionally charged monomers, indicating preservation of native quaternary contacts. Collectively, these results demonstrate how IM-nMS measurements can be leveraged to gain insights into the tertiary and quaternary RNA structures and their gas-phase stability.

title: Comprehensive MS data uncover aged microplastics transformations in human serum
abstract: Background Microplastics (MPs) are currently the focus of scrupulous international action as persistent man-made pollutants. Upon entering the body, MPs interact with proteins to form a biocorona that influences their biological fate and toxicity. Results Here, we incubated real-world MPs, collected from different marine environments, with human serum and used three complementary MS setups to (i) assess the protein-binding kinetics; (ii) identify the major proteins dominating the corona; and (iii) assess the depletion of minor metal-containing proteins due to attachment to MPs. The results of isotopic ratio MS analysis showed definite time-dependent isotopic alterations of MPs related to corona formation. Using MS-based proteomics revealed fundamental similarities in the corona compositions of seawater and sedimentary MPs exposed to human serum. According to metal-specific ICP-sector field MS measurements, the bio-MP interactions involve a substantial proportion of copper in the serum proteome (>30%) and may thereby induce a notable disruption of its homeostasis and functions. Significance This study proves the importance of profiling human serum proteins in MP coronas and suggests that binding of low-abundance metal-containing proteins may modulate their biological functions.

title: Measurement uncertainty evaluation from analytical validation data: Asymmetric coverage interval due to uncorrected significant bias
abstract: BACKGROUND: Reliability in analytical measurements depends on appropriate measurement uncertainty estimation. In top-down approaches, precision and recovery data obtained during analytical method validation are commonly used for this purpose. Although significant systematic effects should preferably be corrected, correction is not always feasible, and uncorrected bias may instead be incorporated into the uncertainty estimate. However, treating directional bias as a symmetric uncertainty component may result in unnecessarily wide intervals. This study proposes an asymmetric approach (ASYM) in which bias shifts the uncertainty interval without increasing the random uncertainty component. RESULTS: A Python-based Monte Carlo algorithm was developed to evaluate coverage probability and interval width over recovery values from 40% to 120% and precision up to 30%. ASYM was compared with a conventional root-sum-of-squares symmetric approach (RSSu or SYM) and alternative uncertainty models (SUMU, SUMUmax, and Ue). Moreover, the models were additionally evaluated using real analytical validation datasets from pesticide residues by LC-MS/MS. When bias was small relative to precision, the approaches generally provided similar coverage. As bias increased, ASYM and SUMU generally maintained coverage closer to the nominal 95% level, whereas other models produced wider intervals and misstated coverage levels. Application to real analytical data supported these trends. A practical decision framework based on the bias-to-precision ratio was suggested. SIGNIFICANCE AND NOVELTY: This study systematically evaluates asymmetric uncertainty estimation for uncorrected bias, distinguishing directional bias from random uncertainty. ASYM avoids artificially inflated intervals, provides coverage closer to the nominal level, and supports uncertainty model selection using the bias-to-precision ratio.

title: A multiway approach to overcome the peak resolution challenges in gas-chromatography coupled to ion mobility spectrometry
abstract: BACKGROUND: Gas-chromatography coupled to ion mobility spectrometry (GC-IMS) is a powerful platform for untargeted analysis of volatile compounds, combining high sensitivity and short analysis times. However, its practical implementation still presents several analytical and computational challenges. From the instrumental perspective, the high sensitivity of isothermal GC-IMS makes it prone to signal saturation and memory effects, which can compromise the reproducibility of measurements. On the data-analysis side, the nature of GC-IMS outputs produce large and collinear datasets, in which baseline drift, shift in ion mobility and retention time modes, and peak overlap hinder the reliable extraction of relevant chemical information. RESULTS: This work proposes a comprehensive workflow from the analytical strategy to the data analysis using as benchmark a data set of honey samples of different origin. Analysing the GC-IMS data, obtained with an instrument operating in isothermal condition, a prominent and marked memory effect was observed; it could be contained only through the systematic use of frequent blanks. Notably, most papers in the literature do not adopt blanks at such frequency. Attention was then devoted to the preprocessing, to improve data quality prior to modelling while limiting the number of preprocessing steps. A multiway approach, i.e. Parallel Factor Analysis 2 (PARAFAC2) applied interval wise, was adopted, for the first time, to resolve overlapping peaks and extract chemically meaningful components from the GC-IMS landscape. The results obtained were also compared with Multivariate Curve Resolution-Alternating Least Squares (MCR-ALS) and recent improved PARAFAC2 algorithms. SIGNIFICANCE: A complete pipeline for the GC-IMS analysis was carefully developed and validated. PARAFAC2, was successfully applied for the deconvolution of GC-IMS data. This approach provided comparable results with previous methods and indicated that the same grade of automation reached in the analysis of GC-MS data with the same approach is feasible.

title: Lysosome-targeted fluorescent probe for real-time imaging of hypochlorite in rheumatoid arthritis and machine learning-assisted quantification in plant tissues
abstract: Background Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic autoimmune inflammatory disease closely associated with excessive oxidative stress. Hypochlorite (ClO - ) are key reactive oxidants in inflammatory microenvironments which contribute to lysosomal dysfunction and inflammatory cascade amplification. However, rapid and selective visualization of ClO - in complex biological systems remains challenging. In addition, residual ClO - in plant-derived foods raises safety concerns, while conventional analytical methods are unsuitable for direct in situ detection. To address this issue, we developed a lysosome-targeted fluorescent probe HB-Z, for sensitive ClO - detection in RA models and plant tissues. Results The designed probe HB-Z consists of a 1,8-naphthalimide-based fluorophore, p-aminophenyl ether recognition unit, and morpholine lysosomal-targeting group, enabling remarkable turn-on fluorescence response upon ClO - triggered cleavage. Spectroscopic studies demonstrated excellent selectivity, rapid response within seconds, high sensitivity, and good pH stability. HB-Z successfully imaged exogenous and endogenous ClO - in live RAW 264.7 macrophages with distinct lysosomal localization. In a λ-carrageenan-induced acute arthritis mouse model, HB-Z enabled visualization of elevated joint ClO - levels and real-time monitoring of oxidative fluctuations during disease progression and antioxidant-mediated remission. Furthermore, HB-Z achieved concentration-dependent fluorescence imaging of exogenous ClO - residues in soybean sprouts. By integrating fluorescence features and soaking time, a stochastic gradient descent machine-learning classifier further enabled three-class discrimination of disinfection status with high accuracy. Significance This probe provides a versatile platform for dynamic ClO - imaging in inflammatory diseases and intelligent assessment of food disinfection quality, possessing great potential for exploring the mechanism of inflammatory diseases and realizing intelligent food safety detection.

title: An in-situ analyzer based on CCD spectral integration for enhanced dynamic range fluorometric detection of ammonium in seawater
abstract: Accurate measurements of ammonium (NH 4 + ) are essential for elucidating the nitrogen cycle, assessing eutrophication and supporting sustainable marine ecosystem management. In this study, we present a fully automated in-situ ammonium analyzer based on fluorometric detection combined with reverse flow injection analysis (rFIA). The system integrates a CCD detector with digitally optimized spectral-band integration to improve signal extraction and achieve a wide detection range. The analyzer achieves a broad analytical range from 0.13 μmol/L to 50 μmol/L, with a calculated detection limit of 0.043 μmol/L and precision better than 5% RSD above the quantification limit, enabling reliable quantification of both background concentrations in open oceans and elevated levels in eutrophic coastal waters. Designed for long-term deployments, the sensor features a waterproof housing and optimized reagent preservation to maintain analytical stability over extended periods. Laboratory and field deployments demonstrate high sensitivity, accuracy and stability, enabling autonomous ammonium monitoring in seawaters with varying salinities at an analytical frequency of approximately one measurement per hour. This work provides a reliable analytical tool for real-time in-situ measurements of ammonium and contributes to improved understanding of nitrogen biogeochemistry and ecosystem responses to environmental change.

title: Direct and highly sensitive impedimetric detection of creatinine in artificial urine using photopolymerized boronic-functionalized imprinted polymers films
abstract: Highly sensitive creatinine (Cre) detection in complex urinary matrices remains challenging because of nonspecific interference and limited molecular selectivity. Here, a boronic acid-functionalized molecularly imprinted polymer (MIP) electrode was developed for label-free electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) detection of Cre in undiluted artificial urine. A Cre-imprinted film containing 4-vinylbenzeneboronic acid (4-VBBA) was photopolymerized on a vinyl-functionalized Au electrode to enhance molecular recognition. The optimized MIP electrode exhibited a linear dynamic range of 5-250 nM, a sensitivity of 0.027 nM -1 , and a limit of detection (LOD) of 1.63 nM. Its sensitivity was 6.75-fold higher than that of the non-imprinted polymer (NIP). Incorporation of 4-VBBA further increased the sensitivity from 0.020 to 0.027 nM -1 and improved the selectivity coefficients from 3.12 to 5.76 to 4.49-8.57. The Cre response remained well preserved in the presence of a 10-fold excess of individual interferents. The sensor also demonstrated high fabrication reproducibility (RSD, 2.15%), operational repeatability over ten regeneration cycles (RSD, 2.67%), and analytical recoveries of 98.69-101.55%. These results establish the 4-VBBA-functionalized MIP as a robust and highly selective recognition interface for sensitive Cre sensing in complex urine-like matrices.

title: Optoelectronically synergized MoS2 field-effect transistor sensor for the detection of Alzheimer's disease biomarker Aβ42
abstract: Background Early diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease (AD) relies heavily on the ultra-sensitive detection of its core biomarker, amyloid-beta 42 (Aβ 42 ). To address this critical need, this paper presents a photoelectric synergistically enhanced field-effect transistor (FET) biosensor based on two-dimensional molybdenum disulfide (MoS 2 ) for the highly sensitive and specific detection of Aβ 42 . Results Experimental results demonstrate that light illumination significantly amplifies the sensing current under identical gate voltages and target concentrations. This enhancement enables the device to effectively overcome the subthreshold region and smoothly transition into the linear operating regime at lower voltages, thereby substantially optimizing signal readout efficiency in low-concentration regions. Benefiting from this photoelectric synergy, the sensor exhibits a markedly enhanced signal response and an optimized dynamic range. The limit of detection decreases to 4.15 × 10 -18 g/mL, representing a 26.29% reduction compared to dark conditions. Furthermore, the relative standard deviation (RSD) of the current response under illumination improves to 2.47% (n = 3), outperforming the 4.86% recorded in the dark and indicating simultaneous enhancements in detection repeatability and device stability. Supported by Silvaco TCAD simulations, the core operating mechanism is elucidated: the specific binding of target Aβ 42 molecules inherently introduces localized interface charge perturbations at the MoS 2 channel. This alteration of the interfacial charge state fundamentally governs the electrical response of the device, which is synergistically amplified under light illumination to achieve ultra-high sensing sensitivity. Significance and novelty This study demonstrates that the photoelectric synergistic strategy offers a highly effective pathway to overcome the sensitivity and performance bottlenecks of traditional FET biosensors. Concurrently, it establishes a novel and promising paradigm for the design of high-performance, multimodal photoelectric biomedical diagnostic chips.

title: Eutectogel-based thin film microextraction coupled with UPLC-PDA for selective detection of diflufenican
abstract: Background Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substance (PFAS) pesticides remain an under-quantified source of human dietary exposure, largely due to their trace-level occurrence and the complexity of food matrices. These analytical challenges underscore the need for selective extraction approaches capable of minimizing matrix interferences. Results In this work, a new thin-film microextraction (TFME) device incorporating multifunctional eutectogels was developed for the selective extraction and preconcentration of the PFAS herbicide diflufenican from food samples prior to UPLC-PDA quantification, and its performance was systematically evaluated. High-throughput screening of selectivity-enhanced deep eutectic solvents (DESs) toward diflufenican was performed using machine-learning-enhanced quantum chemical methods. Simultaneously, the eutectogel-based thin film was fabricated via UV-initiated photopolymerization of the DES, monomer, and crosslinker, yielding supramolecular gels stabilized by non-covalent interactions.
