Towards cross-instrument LIBS calibration for rare earth element analysis
abstract: Background: Laser-Induced Breakdown Spectroscopy (LIBS) has emerged as a promising technique for rare earth elements (REEs) analysis, offering rapid, in situ, and multi-element detection capabilities. However, LIBS-based REE identification remains challenging due to spectral complexity, line overlap, matrix effects, and limited interlaboratory reproducibility. Instrument-dependent factors, including acquisition conditions and system configurations, often introduce significant variability in both spectral signatures and spatial distributions, hindering direct comparison across different platforms and limiting the transferability of analytical models and calibration strategies between platforms and limiting the transferability of analytical models and calibration strategies between instruments. Results: To address these limitations, this work proposes a comprehensive pipeline for interlaboratory LIBS analysis of REEs, integrating image registration, feature selection, and Cross-Instrument Calibration. A key component of the approach is the establishment of spatial correspondence between datasets, ensuring reliable point-to-point comparisons. An affine transform assisted by Mutual Information was used for this task. Additionally, feature selection strategies as Mutual Information and Regularization are explored to identify the most informative spectral features, enabling signal reconstruction using K-Nearest-Neighbours and Ridge Regression while minimizing overfitting. The methodology is validated using REE-bearing samples analyzed with two distinct LIBS systems, with different spatial resolutions. Ridge Regression achieved MAE values between 0.030 and 0.035 and RMSE values between 0.049 and 0.056, with regularization-based feature selection providing a marginal improvement in quantitative performance. Significance: The proposed approach demonstrates that spatial registration combined with spectral calibration transfer can mitigate instrument-dependent differences and facilitate the comparison of LIBS measurements acquired across different systems. This provides a framework for improving cross-system reproducibility and supports the broader use of LIBS for robust, scalable, and transferable REE characterization across instrumentation platforms.

title: A dual-responsive fluorescent probe for simultaneous monitoring of GSH and viscosity dynamics during cuproptosis and its crosstalk with ferroptosis
A derivatization-based LC-MS/MS method for hydrogen peroxide using a cationic xylene tag with preservation of the O–O bond
abstract: ABSTRACT Background Hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) is widely used as a bleaching agent, disinfectant, and oxidant, functions as a redox signaling molecule, and serves as a precursor to peroxide-based improvised explosives, making its reliable detection important across industrial, pharmaceutical, and forensic fields. However, conventional assays respond to the oxidizing activity of H 2 O 2 ; in particular, probe reaction-based methods detect species that have lost the characteristic feature of H 2 O 2 , the intact O–O bond. To the best of our knowledge, no mass spectrometric method has yet enabled the identification of H 2 O 2 through a derivatization product that preserves its intact O–O bond. Results We developed a derivatization-based LC-MS/MS method for H 2 O 2 using a cationic xylene tag (CAX-B), which reacts under alkaline aqueous conditions (0.1 M NaOH, pH ≈ 12.7, 25 °C, 30 min) to form the cationic adduct CAX-OOH with retention of the O–O bond. The structure of CAX-OOH was validated by MS fragmentation analysis and 18 O-labeling experiments, which confirmed the incorporation of both oxygen atoms from H 2 O 2 . Quantification was performed using selected reaction monitoring (SRM) with the transition m/z 238 > 192, which showed excellent linearity ( r > 0.999) over the range of 2.5–250 μM and a detection limit of 0.042 μM. The intra- and inter-day precisions were 3.0–3.5% and 4.1–4.9% RSD, respectively, with accuracies ranging from 99.8 to 106.3%. Application to commercial products yielded results consistent with conventional titrimetric and spectrophotometric methods, confirming the reliability of the approach. Significance and Novelty To our knowledge, this study demonstrates the first LC-MS/MS strategy for the molecular-level identification of H 2 O 2 through a stable derivatization product that preserves the intact O–O bond. This specificity cannot be achieved by conventional probe-based detection, making the method particularly valuable in applications requiring unambiguous identification, such as forensic or mechanistic studies.

Selected ion flow tube mass spectrometry (SIFT-MS) for real time nitric oxide analyses to aid the development of nitric oxide release in multi modal wound dressings
abstract: Diabetic foot ulcers (DFUs) account for almost 1% of NHS expenditure in the UK and affect an estimated 18.6 million people worldwide annually. Nitric oxide (NO)-releasing dressings have emerged as a promising treatment due to NO’s vasodilatory, antimicrobial, and wound-healing properties. Effective clinical application requires sustained, safe NO generation and monitoring of toxic by-products such as nitrogen dioxide (NO 2 ). This study presents real-time characterisation of the acidified nitrite reaction using selected ion flow tube mass spectrometry (SIFT-MS) to quantify NO, NO 2 , and nitrous acid (HNO 2 ). The effect of pH on NO production was investigated using citric acid/sodium citrate buffers (pH 3.0-6.2). NO production showed a strong inverse relationship with pH, decreasing from 4000 nmol mg -1 sodium nitrite at pH 3.0 to 347 nmol mg -1 sodium nitrite at pH 6.2. Apart from pH 3.0, HNO 2 and NO 2 levels remained relatively constant, with median values of 97.0 and 1.20 nmol mg -1 sodium nitrite, respectively. Alternative acid sources were also evaluated to assess production kinetics and improve patient comfort through operation at higher pH values. Comparison of citric and ascorbic acids demonstrated that reaction products are influenced by acid chemistry beyond proton concentration alone. Ascorbic acid produced substantially less NO 2 (148 vs 842 nmol mg -1 sodium nitrite over 3 h), while citric acid enhanced NO generation (8720 vs 5660 nmol mg -1 nitrite at 1 M). Simulated wound conditions showed minimal effects from NaCl or Hank’s balanced salt solution, whereas bovine serum albumin significantly reduced NO production. These findings demonstrate the utility of SIFT-MS for optimising NO-generating wound dressings and improving DFU treatment outcomes.

Non-phthalate plastic additives contamination from laboratory consumables: A quantitative assessment across sample preparation workflows
abstract: ABSTRACT Background The growing interest in analyzing plastic additives (PAs) is driven by their environmental persistence and adverse health effects, demanding reliable trace-level quantification. However, laboratory-derived contamination during sample preparation remains poorly characterized across common consumables and extraction workflows. This study presents, to our knowledge, the first comprehensive and quantitative assessment of non-phthalate plastic additive (NPPA) contamination from laboratory consumables and reagents. Twenty-eight NPPAs were monitored in blank extracts obtained from centrifuge tubes, pipette tips, syringes, syringe filters, and extraction salts, using ethyl acetate (EtOAc) and acetonitrile (ACN) as solvents, analyzed by gas and liquid chromatography coupled to high-resolution mass spectrometry (GC-HRMS and LC-HRMS, respectively). The lack of quantitative information on NPPA contamination introduced by routine laboratory consumables hampers the reliability of trace-level plastic additive analysis. Results Syringe-filter assemblies were identified as the dominant contamination source, with nylon membranes releasing up to 218.7 ng of total NPPAs in EtOAc, compared to 70.1 ng for polytetrafluoroethylene filters. Commercially pre-packaged QuEChERS salt kits showed substantially higher contamination than individually weighed salts, with 1-hydroxycyclohexyl phenyl ketone (HCPK) levels approximately 1840-fold greater. EtOAc extracts (GC-HRMS) showed higher NPPA contamination than ACN extracts (LC-HRMS) for most materials evaluated. Plastic-stored technical-grade acetone increased the NPPA background by approximately 13-fold compared to glass-stored LC-MS-grade acetone. At the workflow level, best- and worst-case scenarios differed by nearly one order of magnitude in GC-based workflows and by more than two orders of magnitude for QuEChERS-based LC workflows, demonstrating the strong influence of material selection on cumulative contamination. Significance and Novelty This study provides the first quantitative assessment of NPPA contamination arising from routine laboratory consumables across complete sample-preparation workflows. The results identify critical contamination sources, establish practical mitigation strategies, and demonstrate that consumable selection can have a greater impact on NPPA background levels than the extraction workflow itself, thereby improving the reliability of trace-level plastic additive determinations.

abstract: ABSTRACT Background The diagnosis of many male reproductive disorders still relies on invasive surgical procedures, revealing the need for new, non-invasive approaches capable of providing deeper molecular information. Seminal plasma represents a promising diagnostic specimen because it directly reflects the biochemical environment of the male reproductive tract. However, despite its potential for metabolomics-based biomarker discovery, seminal plasma remains largely unexplored compared with other biological matrices such as blood plasma or urine. One of the reasons for that is the lack of a reference profile for the human seminal plasma metabolome. In addition, no consensus normalization strategy has yet been established for this underexplored biological matrix, rendering even more challenging the quantitative evaluation of its biochemical content. Results A comprehensive lipidomic and metabolomics characterization of human seminal plasma was achieved by integrating two orthogonal and complementary analytical platforms: RP-UHPLC-QTOF-MS for lipid analysis and CE-TOF-MS for polar metabolites analysis. Data-processing and annotation workflows specifically developed for each analytical platform generated a reference profile comprising 265 lipid species and 125 polar metabolites, together with semiquantitative abundance data. In order to contextualize this characterization, the molecular composition of seminal plasma was compared with that of human blood plasma, a well-established reference matrix in metabolomics. Three normalization strategies based on probabilistic quotient normalization (PQN), fructose concentration, and ejaculate volume were systematically evaluated. Among them, PQN most effectively reduced dilution-related. Significance This study establishes the first comprehensive reference metabolomic profile of human seminal plasma by combining complementary analytical platforms with robust annotation workflows and semiquantitative information. It also proposes a best-performing normalization strategy for this biological matrix, laying the foundation for standardized seminal plasma metabolomics and facilitating future biomarker discovery and the development of non-invasive diagnostic approaches in male reproductive medicine.

PelletScan 360®: Rapid Determination of Proteins in Bovine Milk by Computer Vision and 360° Pellet Imaging
abstract: ABSTRACT Background Protein content indicates bovine milk quality and integrity, and its reduction may indicate water adulteration. Conventional methods often require time-consuming procedures and specialized instrumentation. This work presents PelletScan 360®, a portable, low-cost instrument for rapid total protein determination in raw bovine milk. The method involves ethanol-induced protein precipitation and centrifugation, followed by digital image analysis of the resulting pellet. The instrument rotates an Eppendorf tube containing the centrifuged sample through 360°, while a webcam and computer vision algorithm automatically recognize and measure pellet area. Results The method was optimized using 250 μL of milk, 1300 μL of anhydrous ethanol, and centrifugation at 3200 × g for 3 min. Calibration and prediction used raw bovine milk and samples prepared by controlled water dilution, covering 1.75–3.50 g/100 g protein. The calibration model showed excellent linearity (R 2 = 0.997). Prediction yielded a slope of 0.997 and an intercept of 0.006, with no significant lack of fit. Precision ranged from 0.37 to 1.19% relative standard deviation, and accuracy from 99.68 to 100.5%. Estimated detection and quantification limits were 0.232 and 0.775 g/100 g, respectively. Throughput was 1.8 min per sample, with an operational cost below US$ 0.05. The AGREE score was 0.74, compared with 0.22 for Kjeldahl. Significance PelletScan 360® provides a rapid, low-cost, environmentally favorable approach to milk protein determination. Its novel 360° pellet-scanning strategy transforms physical and morphological features of centrifuged materials into quantitative signals, opening promising analytical possibilities across chemistry.

High-throughput multi-element analysis: a wash-free spatially segregated multiplex immunoassay for heavy metals in water
abstract: Pb, Cd, Hg, Ni and Cr are highly toxic contaminants and potential deliberate adulterants in food and water systems. Current reference methods like atomic absorption spectrometry (AAS) or inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) are expensive and demanding, thus unsuitable for high-throughput or on-site applications. Conversely, commercial field tests lack trace-level sensitivity. We developed a wash-free, spatially segregated multiplex suspension array fluorescence immunoassay (SAFIA) for parallel metal quantification in aqueous matrices. Employing EDTA-functionalised microparticles and flow cytometric readout, the platform achieved IC 20 -related assay quantification limits of 7.1 μg/L (Pb), 3.6 μg/L (Cd), 3.1 μg/L (Hg), 11.7 μg/L (Ni) and 8.0 μg/L (Cr). Validation across complex environmental and drinking water matrices demonstrated robust accuracy (recoveries: 81.2%–128.3%). Independent method comparison confirmed robust trueness (relative bias ≤ 20%). While commercial test strips rely on subjective, semi-quantitative visual readouts, microfluidic paper-based analytical devices (μPADs) often lack sensitivity required by stringent regulatory limits. Techniques such as laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (LIBS) or surface enhanced raman scattering (SERS) face severe matrix interferences and reproducibility issues in aqueous samples. The developed SAFIA addresses these analytical challenges. The wash-free approach offers a rapid, user-friendly, robust and sensitive screening platform for multiple toxic metals in liquid matrices. Spatial segregation provides a practical strategy to mitigate pronounced analyte-dependent interference caused by co-localisation of assay-specific reagent populations in multi-analyte metal-EDTA immunoassays. The bead-based format is, in principle, compatible with multiplexed detection strategies employing spectrally encoded particle populations, supporting decentralised water security assessment and food defence frameworks.

Innovative sample preparation and LC-MS/MS analysis for isoflavone’s quantification in food of the current French diet
abstract: Isoflavones are produced from certain classes of vegetables (mainly soybean). They have attracted considerable interest due to their purported health benefits. Nevertheless, significant discrepancies on their health effects associated with their daily consumption are reported in the literature, particularly given their structural similarity to 17β-estradiol. Furthermore, it still challenging to quantify these compounds as their concentrations and forms vary widely. Therefore, an efficient method is required, which allows analysing a wide range of isoflavones at different levels under reliable quantification in multiple food items. This study describes the development and validation of sample preparation followed by high-performance liquid chromatography tandem mass-spectrometry analysis, enabling the simultaneous quantification of eighteen isoflavones in total diet foodstuffs (aglycones, glycosylated, malonylated and acetylated forms). Sample preparation consists in a protein precipitation for liquid matrices or solvent-assisted extraction by beads grinding for other matrices (fat and solid ones). All samples undergo enzymatic hydrolysis using a mixture of three enzymes. Then they are purified on SPE C18. Limits of quantification were between 0.2 and 4 ng/g. For foods containing soya, these limits were higher for genistein, daidzein and glycitein (respectively 85/71/5 ng/g), given their high levels in these matrices. Recovery values ranged between 65 and 116%; while combined measurement uncertainty was between 21 and 42%. Twenty-five food items were analysed and delivered a comprehensive and reliable determination of these phytoestrogens, from ppb to several dozen of ppm for daidzein and genistein. In conclusion, the method developed allows accurate quantification of isoflavones across a wide range of concentration (from soy-based to non-soy food), while simultaneously reducing costs and environmental impact compared to conventional analytical approaches. The overall objective being providing a reliable analytical tool for characterising the occurrence of these substances in foods; this method is particularly well-suited for studies on overall dietary intake. • Quantification of isoflavone aglycones and conjugated glycosides from ppb level in food. • Sample preparation through better sustainable analytical chemistry. • Determination of adapted performance criteria (LOQ, recovery, accuracy, matrix effect). • First analytical campaign on twenty-five food matrices.
